original.ru: Какого цвета волшебные туфельки Дороти в фильме «Волшебник страны Оз» (1939)?
original.en: What colour are Dorothy's magic slippers in the film The Wizard of Oz (1939)?
original.fact: In Baum's book they are silver: the film made them red to show off Technicolor colour.

verdict: Iconic film plus a great reveal (silver in the book, red to show off Technicolor), and 'Silver' is a lovely trap; only flaw is the hyphenated 'Рубиново-красные', the one long, specific option. Cheap fix: plain 'Красные'.

rewrite.q_ru: Какого цвета волшебные туфельки Дороти в фильме «Волшебник страны Оз» (1939)?
rewrite.q_en: What colour are Dorothy's magic slippers in The Wizard of Oz (1939)?
rewrite.why_better: Single colour words remove the length tell, so the book's 'silver' trap actually bites.

original.ru: В каком фильме звучит знаменитое «I'll be back» («Я вернусь»)?
original.en: Which film gave us the famous line "I'll be back"?
original.fact: Schwarzenegger found "I'll" hard to say and asked for "I will be back", but Cameron refused.

verdict: Fine easy recognition warm-up; KEEP as such. The behind-the-scenes fact (Arnold struggled to say "I'll" and wanted "I will be back") is stronger than the question and could become its own question.

original.ru: Что киллер Леон из фильма Люка Бессона (1994) повсюду носит с собой?
original.en: What does the hitman Léon in Luc Besson's 1994 film carry everywhere?
options: Аквариум с рыбкой | A goldfish bowl
original.fact: At the end Mathilda plants it in the ground by her school, giving it the roots Léon himself never had.

verdict: Satisfying recognition for anyone who saw Léon, with a touching 'roots' fact; those who did not see it can only guess. KEEP as an easy recognition question.

original.ru: Почему фильм «В джазе только девушки» (1959) сняли чёрно-белым?
original.en: Why was Some Like It Hot (1959) shot in black and white?
options: * В цвете грим мужчин смотрелся жутко | Colour made the men's make-up ghastly
Так потребовала Мэрилин Монро | Marilyn Monroe demanded it
Цветная плёнка была запрещена | Colour film was banned
Не хватило денег | There was no money
original.fact: Monroe's contract required colour, but after seeing colour tests of Curtis and Lemmon in drag make-up she agreed to black and white.

verdict: Fun 'why' question: men in drag make-up looking ghastly in colour is a funny image, and the Monroe distractor is a clever half-truth (her contract demanded colour). 'Colour film was banned' is a throwaway.

original.ru: На чём Одри Хепбёрн и Грегори Пек катаются по Риму в «Римских каникулах» (1953)?
original.en: What do Audrey Hepburn and Gregory Peck ride around Rome in Roman Holiday (1953)?
options: В конной коляске | A horse carriage
original.fact: It was Hepburn's first major role and her first American film, and it won her an Oscar straight away.

verdict: 'Rome + 1953 + romance' points straight at the Vespa even for those who never saw the film, and the fact (Hepburn's first Oscar) is a standard bio line unrelated to the question.

original.ru: В «Новых временах» (1936) зрители впервые услышали голос Чаплина. Что он спел?
original.en: Modern Times (1936) was the first time audiences heard Chaplin's voice. What did he sing?
options: * Песенку на выдуманной тарабарщине | A song in made-up gibberish
original.fact: The Tramp loses the cuffs with his lyrics and sings gibberish of French and Italian bits to the tune of Je cherche après Titine.

verdict: Lovely payoff: the first time Chaplin speaks, he sings nonsense. The correct option is the longest and the obviously 'Chaplin-ish' one, but the reveal still delights.

original.ru: Какой фразы на самом деле НЕТ в фильме «Касабланка» (1942)?
original.en: Which famous line is NOT actually said in Casablanca (1942)?
options: * «Сыграй это ещё раз, Сэм» | "Play it again, Sam"
«За тебя, малыш» | "Here's looking at you, kid"
«Задержите обычных подозреваемых» | "Round up the usual suspects"
«У нас всегда будет Париж» | "We'll always have Paris"
original.fact: Ilsa just says "Play it, Sam"; the "again" version was cemented by Woody Allen's 1969 play of that title.

verdict: Classic misquote question: every option sounds like Casablanca, the famous one is the fake, and the Woody Allen origin is a great 'tell someone' fact. The NOT wording is justified here.

original.ru: Что постановил суд насчёт «Носферату» (1922) — пиратской экранизации «Дракулы»?
original.en: What did a court order about Nosferatu (1922), an unlicensed Dracula adaptation?
options: * Уничтожить все копии | Destroy every copy
Показывать только ночью | Show it only at night
original.fact: Bram Stoker's widow won the case, but a few copies survived abroad, so the film still exists.

verdict: Strong story (a court ordered a film destroyed, it survived anyway), but the question does not explain why a court was involved and 'show it only at night' is a throwaway.

rewrite.q_ru: «Носферату» (1922) сняли по «Дракуле» без разрешения. Что за это решил суд?
rewrite.q_en: Nosferatu (1922) adapted Dracula without permission. What did the court order?
options: * Уничтожить все копии | Destroy every copy
Отдать вдове Стокера сборы | Give Stoker's widow the takings
Вырезать все сцены с вампиром | Cut every vampire scene
rewrite.why_better: The setup tells players it was a pirate film, and a credible money option replaces the joke one, so the drastic real verdict lands as a surprise.

original.ru: Сколько костюмов сшили для Элизабет Тейлор в фильме «Клеопатра» (1963)?
original.en: How many costumes were made for Elizabeth Taylor in Cleopatra (1963)?
original.fact: It earned Taylor a Guinness record, beaten five years later by Julie Andrews with 125 costume changes in Star!

verdict: Decent estimation (dozens of outfits for a queen) with a fair range; the record-breaking angle in the fact is the payoff, so it must be right.
fact_check_note: The fact says Julie Andrews beat Taylor's 65-costume Guinness record five years later with 125 changes in Star! (1968). Many sources instead credit Madonna in Evita (1996, 85 changes) as the record breaker; verify which claim the source supports before keeping the 'five years later' line. The answer 65 itself looks fine.
lead_check: Lead check (web): Taylor's 65 costumes and the Guinness record are well sourced; the Julie Andrews "125 changes in Star!" record is found only on fan blogs, and other sources name Madonna in Evita as the record breaker. Cut that sentence from the fact.

original.ru: «Челюсти» планировали снять за 55 съёмочных дней. Сколько дней ушло на самом деле?
original.en: Jaws was scheduled for 55 days of shooting. How many did it actually take?
original.fact: Spielberg skipped filming the shark's final explosion, fearing the worn-out crew would throw him in the water.

verdict: Great closest value: the 55-day anchor invites reasoning about overruns, the near-triple answer surprises, and Spielberg fleeing the crew is a perfect reveal.

original.ru: В какой телеигре выигрывает юноша из Мумбаи в «Миллионере из трущоб» (2008)?
original.en: Which TV quiz does the young man from Mumbai win in Slumdog Millionaire (2008)?
options: * «Кто хочет стать миллионером?» | Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?
original.fact: It is based on a novel by Indian diplomat Vikas Swarup and won eight Oscars, including Best Picture.

verdict: The film title contains "Millionaire", so the answer is given away; KEEP only as a free easy point. The more surprising fact (the novel was written by an Indian diplomat) is buried in the reveal and could carry its own question.

original.ru: В 2017 году на «Оскаре» по ошибке объявили не тот лучший фильм. Какой назвали?
original.en: At the 2017 Oscars the wrong Best Picture was read out. Which film was announced?
options: Манчестер у моря | Manchester by the Sea
original.fact: The presenters had been handed the Best Actress envelope (Emma Stone, La La Land); the real winner was Moonlight.

verdict: A famous TV blunder that people half-remember, credible Best Picture rivals, and the envelope mix-up explanation is a satisfying reveal.

original.ru: Кто спел заглавную песню к фильму «007: Координаты „Скайфолл“» (2012)?
original.en: Who sang the title song of the Bond film Skyfall (2012)?
original.fact: It was the first Bond song ever to win an Oscar; Sam Smith and Billie Eilish later won for theirs too.

verdict: Good easy recognition with smart distractors (Sam Smith and Billie Eilish really sang Bond themes), but little surprise. KEEP as a deliberate easy question.

original.ru: Чем уникален «Русский ковчег» Сокурова, снятый в Эрмитаже в 2001 году?
original.en: What is unique about Sokurov's Russian Ark, shot in the Hermitage in 2001?
options: * Весь фильм — один кадр | The film is one unbroken shot
Он снят при свечах | It was lit only by candles
Он снят задом наперёд | It was filmed backwards
original.fact: The camera moved for 87 minutes without a cut through 33 rooms of the Hermitage; three tries failed, the fourth worked.

verdict: Impressive Russian film feat with plausible gimmick distractors, and the 'three failed tries, fourth worked' detail is a strong payoff.

original.ru: Песня «Naatu Naatu» в 2023 году получила «Оскар». Из фильма какой страны она?
original.en: The song Naatu Naatu won an Oscar in 2023. Which country's film is it from?
original.fact: It comes from the Telugu action film RRR and was the first Indian, and first Asian, song to win the Oscar.

verdict: The song title sounds Indian and the viral RRR dance makes India the reflex answer; the reveal adds only a 'first Asian song' record.

original.ru: Кто первой из женщин получил «Оскар» за режиссуру?
original.en: Who was the first woman to win the Oscar for Best Director?
original.fact: She won in 2010 for The Hurt Locker, beating her ex-husband James Cameron and his Avatar.

verdict: Name recall with little reasoning, but the fact (she beat her ex-husband Cameron and Avatar) is a great hook that should be in the question.

rewrite.q_ru: Первая женщина с «Оскаром» за режиссуру обошла в тот год бывшего мужа — Кэмерона. Кто она?
rewrite.q_en: The first woman to win Best Director beat her ex-husband, James Cameron, that year. Who is she?
rewrite.why_better: The ex-husband rivalry gives the table a story to react to and a clue (who was married to Cameron?) to reason from.

original.ru: Жёлтый комбинезон Невесты в «Убить Билла» — дань уважения какой звезде?
original.en: The Bride's yellow jumpsuit in Kill Bill is a tribute to which star?
original.fact: Bruce Lee wore the same yellow suit with black stripes in Game of Death, the film he left unfinished when he died.

verdict: Satisfying recognition: the yellow jumpsuit is iconic, all four options are martial arts stars, and the unfinished Game of Death adds a poignant note.

original.ru: Что вместо пальцев у людей в одной из вселенных фильма «Всё везде и сразу»?
original.en: In one universe of Everything Everywhere All at Once, what do people have instead of fingers?
original.fact: This absurdist comedy won 7 Oscars including Best Picture, and Michelle Yeoh became the first Asian Best Actress.

verdict: Absurd and very funny for anyone who saw it, and the options make everyone laugh; the fact is a generic Oscar tally, and older players may not know the film.

original.ru: На съёмках «Аватар: Путь воды» Кейт Уинслет задержала дыхание под водой. На сколько секунд?
original.en: Filming Avatar: The Way of Water, Kate Winslet held her breath underwater. For how many seconds?
original.fact: That's 7 minutes 14 seconds, beating Tom Cruise's roughly 6 minutes for Mission: Impossible – Rogue Nation.

verdict: Jaw-dropping number (over 7 minutes) that players can compare to their own breath-holding; the tolerance is fair, though seconds make the slider awkward.

original.ru: Сколько всего «Оскаров» получила трилогия «Властелин колец»?
original.en: How many Oscars did the Lord of the Rings trilogy win in total?
original.fact: The first two films won 4 and 2, then The Return of the King won all 11 of its nominations, tying Ben-Hur and Titanic.

verdict: Well-known trilogy, reasonable estimation path (many know Return of the King swept), fair range and tolerance; solid hard question.

original.ru: Кто НЕ входит в знаменитую тройку из комедий Гайдая?
original.en: Who is NOT part of the famous trio from Gaidai's comedies?
original.fact: Coward was Georgy Vitsin, Experienced was Yevgeny Morgunov, and Dunce was Yuri Nikulin, a circus clown before films.

verdict: Every Russian player knows Coward, Dunce and Experienced, so "Sly" is a free point; KEEP only as an easy warm-up. The Nikulin-was-a-circus-clown fact would make a better question of its own.

original.ru: Куда Женя Лукашин с друзьями ходит каждый год 31 декабря?
original.en: Where do Zhenya Lukashin and his friends go every year on December 31?
options: На каток | To the ice rink
original.fact: Hence the second half of the title, «S lyogkim parom!», the greeting Russians say after a steam bath.

verdict: The title 'С лёгким паром' gives it away and the fact only restates that; KEEP as a deliberate easy warm-up everyone will get.

original.ru: Как подчинённые за глаза зовут Калугину в «Служебном романе»?
original.en: What do the staff call their boss Kalugina behind her back in Office Romance?
original.fact: The film grew out of the play Colleagues, which Ryazanov wrote in 1971 with his regular co-writer Emil Braginsky.

verdict: Warm recognition ('Мымра' gets a laugh), but the fact about the play is dry. KEEP as an easy recognition question.

original.ru: Что Гайдай поставил в финал «Бриллиантовой руки», но по требованию начальства вырезал?
original.en: What did Gaidai put at the end of The Diamond Arm, only to be told to cut it?
options: Погоню на танке | A tank chase
Высадку на Луну | A Moon landing
original.fact: Film chief Alexei Romanov was outraged by a mushroom cloud in a comedy; Gaidai insisted it showed «the complexity of our time».

verdict: A beloved comedy with a genuinely shocking cut ending, absurd-but-plausible distractors, and Gaidai's deadpan excuse as a perfect reveal.

original.ru: Какую награду получил первый фильм Тарковского «Иваново детство»?
original.en: Which prize did Tarkovsky's first feature, Ivan's Childhood, win?
original.fact: Tarkovsky was 30 and got the project only after another director's version had been rejected.

verdict: A festival-prize lookup with nothing to reason from, and the fact (he got the project after another director failed) is mild.

original.ru: «Москва слезам не верит»: Гоша, он же Гога, он же…?
original.en: Moscow Does Not Believe in Tears: Gosha, also known as Goga, also known as…?
original.fact: All are pet forms of Georgy. And twenty years pass between the film's two halves, from 1958 to 1978.

verdict: Everyone will say the quote along; non-fans can deduce that all forms come from Georgy. A warm, quotable recognition question.

original.ru: Какой российский фильм получил «Оскар» в 1995 году?
original.en: Which Russian film won an Oscar in 1995?
options: «Особенности национальной охоты» | Peculiarities of the National Hunt
original.fact: Nikita Mikhalkov also played the lead, and his screen daughter was his own little daughter Nadya.

verdict: A medium-slot Oscar lookup: recognition for the 40-50 group, a guess for the 23-year-olds, and no same-answer reframing lifts it. The Nadya-plays-his-daughter fact is nice and could seed a different question.

original.ru: Какой кремль сыграл царский Кремль в «Иван Васильевич меняет профессию»?
original.en: Which kremlin stood in for the tsar's Kremlin in Ivan Vasilievich Changes Profession?
original.fact: The 16th century Kremlin was shot in Rostov the Great, while the tsar's chambers were built on a Mosfilm sound stage.

verdict: Fun filming-location fact, but 'Moscow' is a near-throwaway and Tula is random; the reveal is modest.

rewrite.q_ru: Какой кремль «сыграл» Московский Кремль XVI века в «Иван Васильевич меняет профессию»?
rewrite.q_en: Which kremlin played the 16th century Moscow Kremlin in Ivan Vasilievich Changes Profession?
rewrite.why_better: Four old-Russian-city kremlins are all credible film locations, so players argue about which one looked most like Moscow.

original.ru: Сколько минут длится «Пёс Барбос и необычный кросс», где впервые появились Трус, Балбес и Бывалый?
original.en: How many minutes long is Dog Barbos and the Unusual Cross, the trio's first film?
original.fact: The ten minute short closed the 1961 Moscow Film Festival, and the trio became instant national favourites.

verdict: Surprising that the trio started in a ten-minute short; easy to estimate from 'short vs feature' and the tolerance rewards it.

original.ru: Сколько лет Людмиле Прокофьевне Калугиной, грозной начальнице из «Служебного романа»?
original.en: How old is Lyudmila Kalugina, the dreaded boss in Office Romance?
original.fact: Just 36, though her staff call her «our old woman» behind her back.

verdict: Everyone pictures 'our old woman' as much older, so 36 gets a real reaction and invites age-guessing banter; the fact only restates the answer.

original.ru: На какой машине ездит мистер Бин?
original.en: What car does Mr. Bean drive?
original.fact: He locks it with a padlock, and in one episode drives it from an armchair strapped to the roof.

verdict: Easy recognition with a funny reveal (padlock, armchair on the roof); the lawnmower option is a joke but adds a laugh. KEEP as a deliberate easy question.

original.ru: Что кричит Шелдон из «Теории большого взрыва», когда кого-то разыграл?
original.en: What does Sheldon from The Big Bang Theory shout after pranking someone?
original.fact: Writer Stephen Engel coined it: he shouted it whenever his pranks on fellow writers worked.

verdict: Quick recognition that people enjoy shouting; all distractors are real catchphrases. KEEP as an easy recognition question.

original.ru: Какой первый покемон у Эша в мультсериале «Покемон»?
original.en: What is Ash's first Pokémon in the Pokémon series?
original.fact: Ash overslept: the starter Pokémon were gone, so Professor Oak gave him a stubborn Pikachu.

verdict: Near-universal recognition; the starter Pokémon are sly distractors for those who know the games, and 'Ash overslept' is a small payoff. KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Что обожает есть бог смерти Рюк в аниме «Тетрадь смерти»?
original.en: What does the death god Ryuk love to eat in Death Note?
original.fact: Apples are like cigarettes to death gods: without them Ryuk gets withdrawal, twisting into knots and doing handstands.

verdict: Anime fans get it instantly, others have nothing to reason from, and 'Notebooks' is a throwaway; the withdrawal-handstands fact is genuinely funny.

rewrite.q_ru: Что обожает есть бог смерти Рюк в аниме «Тетрадь смерти»?
rewrite.q_en: What does the death god Ryuk love to eat in Death Note?
rewrite.why_better: 'Human souls' and 'raw meat' are what a death god 'should' eat, so non-fans can reason and get caught, and the mundane apple becomes the surprise.

original.ru: Что такое «лаф-бокс», без которого с 1950-х не обходились ситкомы?
original.en: What was the "laff box" that sitcoms relied on from the 1950s?
options: * Машина записанного смеха | A machine of recorded laughter
Первый пульт | The first remote control
Ящик для писем зрителей | A box for viewers' letters
original.fact: Engineer Charley Douglass kept it padlocked and hidden from producers; laughs were played on it like an organ.

verdict: "Laff" gives away "laughter" and the distractors are unrelated; the padlocked, secret machine is the real story and should be the hook.

rewrite.q_ru: Инженер Чарли Дуглас держал своё изобретение для ситкомов под замком. Что это было?
rewrite.q_en: Engineer Charley Douglass kept his sitcom invention padlocked. What was it?
options: * Машина записанного смеха | A machine of recorded laughter
Пульт табло «Аплодисменты» | The APPLAUSE sign switch
Машина искусственного снега | A fake snow machine
rewrite.why_better: Dropping the word "laff" removes the give-away, and the padlock mystery makes players weigh four believable studio gadgets before the organ-like machine is revealed.

original.ru: Кем работает Декстер Морган в полиции Майами?
original.en: What is Dexter Morgan's job with the Miami police?
options: * Экспертом по следам крови | Blood spatter analyst
original.fact: By day he reads blood at crime scenes; by night he secretly hunts killers who escaped justice.

verdict: The answer is the show's premise and the fact just restates it; fans get a free point, others guess.

original.ru: Какая кинозвезда сыграла в «Друзьях» бывшего одноклассника, ненавидевшего Рэйчел?
original.en: Which film star played Rachel's old classmate who hated her, in Friends?
original.fact: He was married to Jennifer Aniston at the time, and that one episode earned him an Emmy nomination.

verdict: Star cameo in a beloved sitcom, reasoning path via his marriage to Aniston, and an Emmy nod as a bonus; good fun.

original.ru: Кто играл молодую Елизавету II в первых двух сезонах «Короны»?
original.en: Who played the young Elizabeth II in the first two seasons of The Crown?
original.fact: The show recasts as characters age: from season three, Olivia Colman took over as the Queen.

verdict: Actress-name recall with no reasoning path, and the reveal (they recast as the Queen aged) is common knowledge to viewers.

original.ru: Сколько лет Питер Фальк играл лейтенанта Коломбо?
original.en: For how many years did Peter Falk play Lieutenant Columbo?
original.fact: From 1968 to 2003, yet the part was first offered to Bing Crosby, who said no so he could keep playing golf.

verdict: Surprisingly long run that people can estimate from Falk's ageing face, and the Bing-Crosby-chose-golf fact is a great payoff.

original.ru: Раз в сколько минут герои «Остаться в живых» должны были вводить код в компьютер бункера?
original.en: In Lost, how often, in minutes, did the code have to be typed into the hatch computer?
original.fact: That is exactly the sum of the very numbers that had to be typed in: 4, 8, 15, 16, 23 and 42.

verdict: Fans know 108, everyone else picks a random number; giving the famous numbers in the question turns it into a fun mental-maths puzzle that the reveal confirms.

rewrite.q_ru: Герои «Остаться в живых» вводили в компьютер 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42. Раз в сколько минут?
rewrite.q_en: In Lost the castaways typed 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42 into a computer. How often, in minutes?
rewrite.why_better: Sharp players can spot that the numbers add up to the answer, so it rewards reasoning instead of fandom and the reveal gets an 'of course!'.

original.ru: Что показывали по телевизору утром 19 августа 1991 года, в первый день путча?
original.en: What did Soviet TV show on the morning of 19 August 1991, the first day of the coup?
options: * Балет «Лебединое озеро» | The ballet Swan Lake
Хоккейный матч | An ice hockey match
original.fact: The ballet replaced the usual programmes, and Swan Lake on every channel became a byword for something big happening.

verdict: Iconic Soviet TV moment that both generations know as a meme; the 'Balet' prefix makes the correct option the longest, cheap to fix.

rewrite.q_ru: Что показывали по телевизору утром 19 августа 1991 года, в первый день путча?
rewrite.q_en: What did Soviet TV show on the morning of 19 August 1991, the first day of the coup?
options: Хоккейный матч | An ice hockey match
rewrite.why_better: Dropping 'Балет' evens the option lengths so the answer is recalled, not spotted.

original.ru: Как на самом деле звали Штирлица из «Семнадцати мгновений весны»?
original.en: What was Stierlitz's real name in Seventeen Moments of Spring?
original.fact: During the first showing in 1973 city streets emptied, and crime was reported to drop noticeably.

verdict: Warm recognition; the other options are famous Soviet screen heroes, which is a fun touch, and the 'empty streets' fact lands. KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Что в «Что? Где? Когда?» решает, какой вопрос будет сыгран следующим?
original.en: In What? Where? When?, what decides which question is played next?
options: * Волчок со стрелкой | A spinning top with an arrow
Бросок кубика | A roll of the dice
Выбор капитана | The team captain's choice
original.fact: The top is the game's random generator: its arrow points at a viewer's envelope, and that question is played.

verdict: Everyone knows the волчок, so it is a free point, and the fact only restates the rule. KEEP only as a deliberate easy warm-up.

original.ru: Чей голос годами звучал за кадром «Что? Где? Когда?», пока имя ведущего держали в секрете?
original.en: Whose voice spoke off screen in What? Where? When? for years while the host's name was kept secret?
original.fact: His name was left out of the credits and only revealed in 1980, after viewers' letters and requests from Eldar Ryazanov.

verdict: A nice 'secret host' story for the older players, but the question is long, and Yakubovich is too obviously from another show.

rewrite.q_ru: Имя ведущего «Что? Где? Когда?» годами не писали в титрах. Как его звали?
rewrite.q_en: For years the host of What? Where? When? was left out of the credits. Who was he?
rewrite.why_better: Shorter, leads with the mystery, and four genuine Soviet TV hosts make it a real recall test.

original.ru: Кто вёл музыкальную передачу «Утренняя почта»?
original.en: Who hosted the music show Morning Mail?
original.fact: Nikolaev hosted it from the first episode in 1974 and even came back to it in the late 1990s.

verdict: Host-name recall that the 23-year-olds cannot reason about, with a flat fact (he hosted it from 1974).

original.ru: Кто вёл самые первые выпуски «Поля чудес» до Якубовича?
original.en: Who hosted the very first episodes of Field of Miracles, before Yakubovich?
original.fact: Yakubovich turned the offer down at first and only stepped up to the drum in November 1991.

verdict: Most people assume Yakubovich hosted from day one, so Listyev is a real surprise, and all options are credible TV hosts.

original.ru: Где в 1986 году прозвучала фраза «В СССР секса нет»?
original.en: Where was the phrase "There is no sex in the USSR" heard in 1986?
options: * На телемосте Ленинград — Бостон | A Leningrad to Boston TV link-up
В игре КВН | In a KVN game
В программе «Время» | On the Vremya news
original.fact: The question was about TV ads; someone shouted "We have sex, we have no ads!" and her "we have love" was lost.

verdict: Legendary phrase, and the reveal (the question was about ads, 'we have love' was drowned in laughter) gets a big reaction; the telemost option is a little longer than the rest.

original.ru: На что намекало название КВН, когда игра только появилась?
original.en: What did the name KVN hint at when the show first appeared?
options: * На телевизор «КВН-49» | The KVN-49 TV set
На клуб в МГУ | A Moscow University club
На фамилии трёх студентов | Three students' surnames
original.fact: The set was named after its designers' initials; people read KVN as "Bought, switched on, doesn't work".

verdict: Surprising double meaning, and 'Купил, включил, не работает' is a great line to repeat at the table.

original.ru: В каком году вышел первый выпуск «Что? Где? Когда?»?
original.en: In which year did the first episode of What? Where? When? air?
original.fact: The first episode aired on 4 September 1975; the familiar rule of playing to six points only came in 1982.

verdict: A founding-year question nobody cares about; the six-points rule fact is dry. The script also flags similarity to ru_tv_025 (not in this batch).

original.ru: В каком году впервые вышел в эфир КВН?
original.en: In which year was KVN first broadcast?
original.fact: The first game went out live on 8 November 1961 and ran for about an hour and a half.

verdict: Another founding year: estimable but joyless, and the fact (live, 90 minutes) adds little.

original.ru: За чем вечно гоняется белка Скрат в «Ледниковом периоде»?
original.en: What is Scrat the squirrel forever chasing in Ice Age?
options: За куском сыра | A piece of cheese
original.fact: Scrat is made up, yet a fanged fossil mammal from Argentina, described in 2011, was nicknamed the real Scrat.

verdict: Easy recognition with a good pine-cone trap and a fun 'real Scrat' fossil reveal. KEEP as a deliberate easy question.

original.ru: Кем работал крокодил Гена?
original.en: What was Gena the Crocodile's job?
options: * Крокодилом в зоопарке | Crocodile at the zoo
Сторожем на стройке | Building site watchman
original.fact: Gena was voiced by Vasily Livanov, the Soviet screen Sherlock Holmes.

verdict: The famous joke answer (a crocodile working as a crocodile) gets a smile, though the option echoes the question's word; Livanov-as-Gena is a good reveal.

original.ru: Где живёт Шрек в начале первого фильма?
original.en: Where does Shrek live at the start of the first film?
original.fact: Shrek is Yiddish for 'fear' or 'fright', and in William Steig's 1990 picture book he really is scary.

verdict: Pure recognition everyone gets; KEEP as an easy warm-up. The Yiddish 'Shrek = fear' fact is strong enough to deserve its own question.

original.ru: В честь кого назвали Молнию Маккуина из «Тачек»?
original.en: Who was Lightning McQueen from Cars named after?
options: Актёра Стива Маккуина | Actor Steve McQueen
* Аниматора Pixar Гленна Маккуина | Pixar animator Glenn McQueen
Режиссёра Стива Маккуина | Director Steve McQueen
Королевы Англии | The Queen of England
original.fact: Glenn McQueen died in 2002, and Pixar named its hero in his memory.

verdict: Great trap (everyone assumes actor Steve McQueen), but 'The Queen of England' is a throwaway and two Steve McQueens confuse more than they tempt.

rewrite.q_ru: В честь кого назвали Молнию Маккуина из «Тачек»?
rewrite.q_en: Who was Lightning McQueen from Cars named after?
options: * Аниматора Pixar Гленна Маккуина | Pixar animator Glenn McQueen
Актёра Стива Маккуина | Actor Steve McQueen
Модельера Александра Маккуина | Designer Alexander McQueen
rewrite.why_better: Every option is a real famous (Mc)Queen, so the actor trap stays strong, the duplicate Steve McQueen is gone and nothing is a pure throwaway.

original.ru: Кто первым озвучивал Микки Мауса?
original.en: Who was the first voice of Mickey Mouse?
options: * Сам Уолт Дисней | Walt Disney himself
original.fact: Disney voiced Mickey for almost 20 years; his wife picked the name, as he had wanted to call the mouse Mortimer.

verdict: Nice surprise that Disney himself voiced Mickey, and 'Mortimer' is a fun reveal; 'Сам' in the correct option is a slight tell.

original.ru: Кто озвучил Шрека в оригинальной версии?
original.en: Who voiced Shrek in the original version?
original.fact: Chris Farley recorded most of the part first, but he died in 1997 and the role was recast.

verdict: Russian players know the dubbed Shrek, so the original voice is name recall; the Chris Farley story is good but Farley is unknown here.

original.ru: Какой советский мультфильм, по словам Миядзаки, удержал его в профессии аниматора?
original.en: Which Soviet cartoon, Miyazaki says, kept him working in animation?
original.fact: As a young animator he was thinking of quitting, then saw this 1957 film at a studio screening and stayed.

verdict: Proud-of-our-cartoons surprise with four credible Soviet classics (Cheburashka is a real Japan favourite), and the near-quitting story pays off.

original.ru: Кто озвучил Винни-Пуха в советском мультфильме?
original.en: Who voiced Winnie the Pooh in the Soviet cartoon?
original.fact: The director found his voice too low, so the recording was sped up by running the tape faster.

verdict: The voice is instantly recognisable once you think of it, all distractors are great comic actors, and the sped-up-tape fact surprises.

original.ru: В каком году вышел «Пароходик Вилли» — официальный дебют Микки Мауса?
original.en: In which year did Steamboat Willie, Mickey Mouse's official debut, come out?
original.fact: It was actually the third Mickey film: the first two, silent ones, found no distributor.

verdict: A release year that is estimable but nobody cares about; the 'third Mickey film' fact is mild.

original.ru: Сколько щенков родилось у Понго и Пэдди в «101 далматинце» (1961)?
original.en: How many puppies were born to Pongo and Perdita in 101 Dalmatians (1961)?
original.fact: Cruella bought the rest in pet shops, ending up with 99 Dalmatians in all.

verdict: Everyone assumes 101 were born, the real 15 surprises, and the reveal explains where the rest came from; fair range and tolerance.

original.ru: Кто в оригинале озвучивает Грута, который говорит только «Я есть Грут»?
original.en: Who voices Groot, whose only line is "I am Groot"?
original.fact: Diesel gives the one line a new meaning every time, and he even voiced Groot in some foreign-language dubs.

verdict: All four are action stars with deep voices, so it is a fair recognition guess, and Diesel voicing Groot in foreign dubs is a fun extra.

original.ru: Какой страной правит Чёрная Пантера?
original.en: Which country does Black Panther rule?
original.fact: Created in 1966 by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, he was the first Black superhero in mainstream American comics.

verdict: Easy recognition with witty fictional-country distractors (Genovia from The Princess Diaries); the reveal is a solid but familiar 'first Black superhero' line. KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Как зовут дворецкого Бэтмена?
original.en: What is the name of Batman's butler?
original.fact: In 1943 Alfred was plump and clean shaven; the comics slimmed him and added a moustache to match the actor in the film serial.

verdict: Fine warm-up recognition, but zero surprise and the moustache fact is no payoff. KEEP as a deliberate easy recognition question.

original.ru: Кто, кроме Тора, поднимает молот Мьёльнир в «Мстителях: Финал»?
original.en: In Avengers: Endgame, who besides Thor lifts the hammer Mjolnir?
original.fact: It was hinted in Age of Ultron, when the hammer budged slightly for Steve at the party and Thor looked worried.

verdict: A crowd-pleasing movie moment fans cheered in cinemas, credible options, and the Age of Ultron foreshadowing is a satisfying reveal.

original.ru: Чем зарабатывает на жизнь Обеликс?
original.en: How does Obelix earn his living?
options: Поёт песни | Singing as a bard
original.fact: Menhirs are the huge standing stones of ancient Gaul, and his very name comes from the word obelisk.

verdict: Familiar from the Depardieu films, the menhir answer is satisfying, and 'Obelix from obelisk' is a nice click.

original.ru: Откуда взялся псевдоним создателя Тинтина Эрже (Hergé)?
original.en: Where does the pen name of Tintin's creator, Hergé, come from?
options: * Его инициалы наоборот | His initials reversed
Кличка его собаки | His dog's name
Так он чихал | The sound of his sneeze
original.fact: His name was Georges Remi, and the initials R.G. read aloud in French sound like Hergé.

verdict: Clever answer and a funny sneeze distractor, but Tintin is half-known in Russia; putting his real name in the question turns it into a satisfying deduction.

rewrite.q_ru: Бельгиец Жорж Реми, автор комиксов о Тинтине, подписывался «Эрже». Откуда этот псевдоним?
rewrite.q_en: Belgian Georges Remi, creator of Tintin, signed himself Hergé. Where does the name come from?
options: * Его инициалы наоборот | His initials reversed
Кличка его собаки | His dog's name
Так он чихал | The sound of his sneeze
rewrite.why_better: With 'Georges Remi' on screen, players can sound out R.G. themselves, so it rewards thinking and gets an aha even from people who never read Tintin.

original.ru: Какого цвета был Халк в самом первом комиксе 1962 года?
original.en: What colour was the Hulk in his very first comic in 1962?
original.fact: The printer could not keep the grey even from page to page, so Stan Lee switched him to green.

verdict: Everyone knows green Hulk, so grey is a real surprise and the printing-problem reason is a good story; 'Polka dot' is a joke option but earns a laugh.

original.ru: Где впервые появилась Харли Квинн, подружка Джокера?
original.en: Where did Harley Quinn, the Joker's sidekick, first appear?
options: * В мультсериале | In a cartoon series
В фильме 1989 года | In the 1989 film
В видеоигре | In a video game
original.fact: She was created for Batman: The Animated Series in 1992 as a minor henchwoman and proved so popular that the comics took her in.

verdict: Surprising origin (a cartoon side character who became a film star), credible format distractors, good reveal.

original.ru: Сколько лет было Стэну Ли, когда вышла «Фантастическая четвёрка» (1961), начало эпохи Marvel?
original.en: How old was Stan Lee when the Fantastic Four, which began the Marvel age, came out in 1961?
original.fact: He was about to quit comics, but his wife told him to write one story his own way first, since he had nothing to lose.

verdict: People can reason from his cameo-era old age, the number is mildly surprising, and the 'nothing to lose' wife advice is a lovely reveal; the tolerance is generous.

original.ru: В каком году вышел первый комикс о Супермене, с которого начался «золотой век» комиксов?
original.en: In what year did Superman's first comic come out, starting the golden age of comics?
original.fact: Two Cleveland teenagers, Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster, dreamed him up in 1933 and spent five years looking for a publisher.

verdict: Estimable but dull publication year; the teenagers-searching-five-years fact is better than the question it rides on.

original.ru: Кто такой Донки Конг?
original.en: What is Donkey Kong?
original.fact: Miyamoto meant "donkey" as stubborn and thought "Kong" simply meant gorilla; it is not a typo for Monkey Kong.

verdict: The name invites the 'donkey' trap, and the 'not a typo for Monkey Kong' fact is a nice myth-buster.

original.ru: Кто смеётся над тобой в Duck Hunt, если промахнулся?
original.en: Who laughs at you in Duck Hunt when you miss?
original.fact: In the arcade version you could shoot the dog and he scolded you; on consoles Nintendo made him unshootable to keep it family friendly.

verdict: Shared Dendy-era grudge against the laughing dog gets a groan, and the shootable-dog arcade fact is fun. KEEP as an easy nostalgia question.

original.ru: Какой реальный город изображает GTA: Vice City (2002)?
original.en: Which real city is GTA: Vice City (2002) based on?
original.fact: It is set in 1986 in the style of Scarface and Miami Vice, and the car radios play real 80s hits.

verdict: 'Vice' plus Miami Vice makes it easy; KEEP as an easy recognition question with a decent 80s-radio reveal.

original.ru: Игру какой компании скопировала советская «Электроника» «Ну, погоди!»?
original.en: The Soviet Elektronika handheld "Nu, Pogodi!" copied a game by which company?
original.fact: It copies Egg from the Game & Watch line, where a wolf in a hat was already catching the eggs.

verdict: Everyone had the Elektronika, few know it was a Nintendo copy, and 'the original wolf wore a hat too' is a perfect reveal. Nintendo is a little longer, but Atari/Sega are fair traps.

original.ru: Что давал в Doom код IDDQD?
original.en: What did typing IDDQD do in Doom?
options: Переход на любой уровень | A jump to any level
Хождение сквозь стены | Walking through walls
original.fact: The screen said "Degreelessness Mode On", the joke official name for god mode.

verdict: A nostalgia flash for Doom players and a coin toss for everyone else; the 'Degreelessness' fact is mild.

original.ru: Как световой пистолет в Duck Hunt понимал, что ты попал?
original.en: How did the light gun in Duck Hunt know you had hit?
options: * Экран мигал белым квадратом | The screen flashed a white box
Невидимый луч бил в датчик | An invisible beam hit a sensor
Ловил ультразвук от телевизора | It picked up ultrasound from the TV
Подсказывала собака | The dog told it
original.fact: On a shot the screen went black for a frame, then the duck became a white box; the trick needs an old tube TV and fails on flat screens.

verdict: A childhood mystery solved: credible tech distractors and a reveal that explains why it fails on modern TVs.

original.ru: Чем сначала должна была стать Diablo (1996)?
original.en: What was Diablo (1996) first planned to be?
options: Дополнением к Warcraft | A Warcraft add-on
original.fact: The team voted for real time, and David Brevik had the basics working within a few hours.

verdict: Niche development history only PC gamers care about; the 'working in hours' fact does not land for a family.

original.ru: В какой стране StarCraft стал почти национальным спортом?
original.en: In which country did StarCraft become almost a national sport?
original.fact: By 2001 half of all StarCraft copies sold worldwide had been sold in South Korea, where matches were shown on TV.

verdict: Korea's esports fame makes it guessable, but the surprising part (half of all copies sold there) is hidden in the fact; move it into the question.

rewrite.q_ru: К 2001 году почти половину всех проданных в мире копий StarCraft купили в одной стране. В какой?
rewrite.q_en: By 2001 almost half of all StarCraft copies sold worldwide were bought in one country. Which?
rewrite.why_better: The 'half the world's copies' hook makes even non-gamers go 'wait, really?' and invites reasoning about esports nations.

original.ru: Сколько маленьких точек нужно съесть Пакмену, чтобы пройти лабиринт?
original.en: How many small dots does Pac-Man have to eat to clear the maze?
original.fact: Plus four big energizers. A perfect game, eating every dot, fruit and ghost up to level 256, scores 3,333,360 points.

verdict: Everyone has played Pac-Man and can estimate dots in a maze, so it is a fair hard question. Its fact mentions level 256, which spoils games_retro_040 if both are played in one evening.

original.ru: На каком уровне Pac-Man ломается: половина экрана превращается в кашу и пройти дальше нельзя?
original.en: On which level does Pac-Man break, with half the screen turning to garbage so no one can go on?
original.fact: The level number lived in one byte, which only counts to 255; on level 256 the counter overflows and the game draws garbage.

verdict: A broken level in Pac-Man is a fun surprise, techies can reason to 256, and the one-byte overflow is a satisfying explanation; keep apart from games_retro_041, whose fact names level 256.

original.ru: Как в Among Us предатель тайно перемещается по кораблю?
original.en: How does the impostor secretly move around the ship in Among Us?
options: В шкафу на колёсах | Inside a rolling wardrobe
original.fact: Tiny studio Innersloth released it in 2018, and it went almost unnoticed for two years until streamers picked it up in 2020.

verdict: Quick 'sus' recognition that gets a reaction from players, with a 'wardrobe on wheels' joke option. KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Как называется игровая валюта Roblox?
original.en: What is Roblox's in-game currency called?
original.fact: Roblox came out back in 2006, so it is older than most of the children who play it.

verdict: Roblox → Robux gives the answer away; 'older than its players' is a nice fact. KEEP only as a free easy point.

original.ru: Игры «Ведьмак» сделаны по книгам писателя из какой страны?
original.en: The Witcher games are based on books by a writer from which country?
original.fact: Andrzej Sapkowski sold the game rights for a flat fee, not royalties, and once the games were hits he demanded more.

verdict: Many know Sapkowski is Polish, the neighbours are fair distractors, and the flat-fee regret is a good reveal.

original.ru: Чем знаменита игра Undertale? Её можно пройти…
original.en: What is Undertale famous for? You can finish it...
options: * никого не убив | without killing anyone
не сходя с места | without moving
ни разу не прыгнув | without ever jumping
с закрытыми глазами | with your eyes shut
original.fact: Every enemy can be talked down and spared; Toby Fox made the game almost single-handedly.

verdict: Charming idea, but the game is unknown to the older players and 'with your eyes shut' is a throwaway; tighter distractors would make non-players reason.

rewrite.q_ru: Чем знаменита игра Undertale? Её можно пройти…
rewrite.q_en: What is Undertale famous for? You can finish it...
options: * никого не убив | without killing anyone
ни разу не погибнув | without ever dying
не подняв ни одного предмета | without picking anything up
не сказав ни слова | without saying a word
rewrite.why_better: All four sound like real 'challenge run' claims, so non-gamers have to think and the pacifist answer feels like a discovery.

original.ru: Какая страна в 2014 году воссоздала себя в Minecraft в натуральную величину?
original.en: Which country recreated itself at full scale in Minecraft in 2014?
original.fact: About 4 billion blocks and a terabyte of data: Denmark's geodata agency built it to help teach geography.

verdict: Fun 'a whole country in Minecraft' surprise, reasoning via a small flat country, and the geography-lesson purpose is a nice reveal.

original.ru: Как зовут главного героя игры The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild?
original.en: What is the hero of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild called?
original.fact: Many think Zelda is the hero, but Zelda is the princess; you play as Link.

verdict: Recognition question that works as a trap for the "Zelda is the hero" myth; KEEP. The script flags similarity to games_retro_007 (not in this batch), so check the two do not both test Link vs Zelda.

original.ru: Стриминговый сервис Twitch вырос из сайта, где один человек…
original.en: The streaming service Twitch grew out of a site where one man...
options: * транслировал всю свою жизнь | streamed his whole life
продавал старые игры | sold old games
учил играть в шахматы | taught chess
показывал своих кошек | showed off his cats
original.fact: In 2007 Justin Kan wore a head camera 24/7 for Justin.tv; its gaming section later became Twitch.

verdict: Genuine 'wait, seriously?': Twitch began with a man streaming his whole life; distractors are plausible small-site ideas.

original.ru: Сколько планет можно посетить в No Man's Sky?
original.en: How many planets can you visit in No Man's Sky?
original.fact: The planets are not stored anywhere: a formula builds them from a 64-bit seed on the fly, hence 2 to the 64th.

verdict: Amazing scale, but four '18 ×' options make 'pick the biggest' a pure pattern guess; an 'infinitely many' trap would make it bite.

rewrite.q_ru: Сколько планет можно посетить в No Man's Sky?
rewrite.q_en: How many planets can you visit in No Man's Sky?
rewrite.why_better: Breaking the '18 ×' pattern removes the pick-the-biggest tell, and 'infinitely many' is a tempting trap the 2-to-the-64th reveal explains.

original.ru: ВВС США в 2010 году собрали суперкомпьютер из PlayStation 3. Сколько приставок в нём было?
original.en: In 2010 the US Air Force built a supercomputer out of PlayStation 3s. How many consoles?
original.fact: About 1,760 PS3s cost far less than a normal supercomputer and ranked among the world's fastest machines at the time.

verdict: Fun premise (a military supercomputer made of PlayStations), but there is little to reason from and the 0-10000 range is very wide.

rewrite.q_ru: ВВС США собрали суперкомпьютер из PlayStation 3. Сколько приставок в нём было?
rewrite.q_en: The US Air Force built a supercomputer out of PlayStation 3s. How many consoles did it use?
rewrite.why_better: A tighter range makes the slider less arbitrary, so 'a couple of thousand' instinct guesses land in the bonus zone.

original.ru: Сколько всего приставок Nintendo Wii продали за всё время?
original.en: How many Nintendo Wii consoles were sold in total?
original.fact: About 101.6 million: the low-powered Wii outsold the PS3 and Xbox 360 thanks to its wave-it-around remote.

verdict: A sales figure with a modest reveal; nothing to argue about at the table.

original.ru: Кто победит в крестиках-ноликах, если оба игрока не ошибаются?
original.en: Who wins at tic-tac-toe if both players play perfectly?
options: * Никто: будет ничья | Nobody: it's a draw
Тот, кто ходит первым | The first player
Тот, кто ходит вторым | The second player
Тот, кто ставит нолики | Whoever plays noughts
original.fact: It is so simple that in 1952 the EDSAC computer already played it flawlessly, in a program called OXO.

verdict: Everyone has played it and can reason to the draw; the 1952 computer fact is a nice surprise. 'Whoever plays noughts' overlaps with 'the second player'.

original.ru: Какие фигуры двигаются во время рокировки?
original.en: Which pieces move when you castle?
options: * Король и ладья | King and rook
Король и ферзь | King and queen
Ладья и конь | Rook and knight
Ферзь и слон | Queen and bishop
original.fact: It is the only move in which a player moves two of their pieces at once, and the king steps two squares.

verdict: A chess-rules check with a fact that just restates the rule; no surprise for players, no fun for non-players.

original.ru: Камни какого цвета делают первый ход в игре го?
original.en: In the game of Go, which colour moves first?
original.fact: Moving first is an advantage, so White gets bonus points called komi, usually 6.5 or 7.5, to make up for it.

verdict: Really a 50/50 between black and white (red and blue are filler); the hook is that it is the opposite of chess, which the question should say.

rewrite.q_ru: В шахматах первыми ходят белые. А камни какого цвета ходят первыми в го?
rewrite.q_en: In chess White moves first. Which colour moves first in Go?
rewrite.why_better: The chess contrast sets up a 'surely the same?' trap, so the reversal and the komi reveal feel like a twist.

original.ru: Что можно сделать в шахматах, если 50 ходов подряд никто не брал фигур и не ходил пешкой?
original.en: In chess, what may happen after 50 moves with no capture and no pawn move?
options: * Потребовать ничью | A player can claim a draw
Выиграть, если фигур больше | Whoever has more pieces wins
Снять с доски ферзей | Both queens are removed
Сыграть блиц | A blitz game decides it
original.fact: And under current FIDE rules, after 75 such moves the game is drawn automatically, even if nobody asks.

verdict: A tournament-rules question only chess players care about; 'claim a draw' is guessable but nobody reacts.

original.ru: Что значит слово «дженга» на языке суахили?
original.en: What does the Swahili word behind Jenga mean?
original.fact: Creator Leslie Scott was born in Tanganyika, now Tanzania, grew up speaking Swahili and launched the game in 1983.

verdict: Familiar game, a surprising Swahili origin, and 'tower'/'to fall' are tempting traps; borderline GOOD, no cheap fix needed.

original.ru: Как изобретатель «Скрэббла» решил, сколько фишек с каждой буквой положить в набор?
original.en: How did Scrabble's inventor decide how many tiles each letter gets?
options: * Подсчитал буквы в газетах | He counted letters in newspapers
Сделал всех букв поровну | He gave all letters equal numbers
Спросил жену | He asked his wife
original.fact: Alfred Butts tallied letters by hand in The New York Times and other papers, which is why rare letters score more.

verdict: Clever method players can reason to, plausible alternatives, and the reveal explains why rare letters score more.

original.ru: В средневековых шахматах эта фигура ходила лишь на одну клетку по диагонали. Какая?
original.en: In medieval chess, which piece could move only one square diagonally?
original.fact: The queen, once a vizier, moved one square diagonally; it became the strongest piece in Spain in the late 1400s.

verdict: The strongest piece was once the weakest: a real 'wait, seriously?'. The fact mostly restates the question, though the Spain date adds a little.

original.ru: На доске какого размера играют в международные шашки?
original.en: What size of board is international draughts played on?
original.fact: Each player starts with 20 pieces instead of 12, and only the 50 dark squares of the hundred are used.

verdict: Board dimensions are an exam fact with a flat reveal.

original.ru: Сколько костей в классическом китайском наборе для маджонга?
original.en: How many tiles are in a classic Chinese mahjong set?
original.fact: Mahjong took shape in 19th century China and caused a real craze in America and Europe in the 1920s.

verdict: Few have handled a mahjong set, so the tile count is hard to estimate, and the 1920s craze fact is unrelated to the number.

original.ru: Сколько всего фишек в англоязычном наборе «Скрэббл»?
original.en: How many tiles are in an English-language Scrabble set?
original.fact: 98 lettered tiles and 2 blanks; the priciest, Q and Z, are worth 10 points and there is one of each.

verdict: Estimable and fair, but a round 100 tiles is no surprise and the reveal is a points table; it also sits next to the stronger board_019 Scrabble question.

original.ru: Какая группа записала Smells Like Teen Spirit в 1991 году?
original.en: Which band recorded Smells Like Teen Spirit in 1991?
original.fact: Teen Spirit was a deodorant: a friend wrote that Cobain smelled of it, and he didn't know the brand.

verdict: Easy recognition with a brilliant reveal (Teen Spirit was a deodorant). KEEP as an easy question; the fact carries it.

original.ru: Кто из битлов написал песню Imagine?
original.en: Which Beatle wrote the song Imagine?
original.fact: In 2017 Yoko Ono was officially credited as co-writer: Lennon himself said much of the idea was hers.

verdict: Well-known answer (Lennon's signature song); the Yoko co-credit is a mild twist. KEEP as an easy recognition question.

original.ru: Какой жанр прославил фильм «Лихорадка субботнего вечера» с песнями Bee Gees?
original.en: Which genre did Saturday Night Fever, with its Bee Gees songs, make huge?
original.fact: The soundtrack was the best-selling album ever until Michael Jackson's Thriller overtook it.

verdict: Bee Gees + 'Fever' = disco for anyone; KEEP only as a free easy point. The best-seller-until-Thriller fact is decent.

original.ru: Откуда взялось название Led Zeppelin?
original.en: Where did the name Led Zeppelin come from?
options: * Шутка: «рухнут, как свинцовый шар» | A joke: like a lead balloon
Так звали деда гитариста | The guitarist's grandfather's name
Название паба, где они играли | A pub they played in
Марка их первого фургона | Their first van's make
original.fact: Balloon became zeppelin, and they dropped the a from Lead so Americans would not say leed.

verdict: Great origin story, but the correct option is the long one that literally says 'joke'; balanced short options and a translated band name let players reason it out. The script's 'similar to' brands/rulers ids are other name-origin questions, not the same fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Led Zeppelin — это «свинцовый цеппелин». Откуда взялось такое название?
rewrite.q_en: Led Zeppelin means a lead zeppelin. Where did the name come from?
options: * Из шутки, что они провалятся | A joke that they would flop
Из названия паба | From a pub's name
Из фамилии менеджера | From their manager's surname
Из марки их фургона | From their van's make
rewrite.why_better: Equal-length options remove the tell, and 'a lead airship' invites players to work out the 'it will sink' joke themselves.

original.ru: Как впервые вышла в свет I Will Survive Глории Гейнор?
original.en: How was Gloria Gaynor's I Will Survive first released?
options: * На обороте другого её сингла | As the B-side of one of her singles
Как реклама духов | As a perfume advert
В фильме про диско | In a disco film
original.fact: DJs kept flipping the record to play the B-side until it went to No. 1 in 1979.

verdict: Lovely underdog story (DJs flipped the record), but the correct option is far longer than the rest.

rewrite.q_ru: Как впервые вышла песня I Will Survive Глории Гейнор?
rewrite.q_en: How was Gloria Gaynor's I Will Survive first released?
options: * На стороне Б сингла | As a B-side
В рекламе духов | In a perfume advert
В фильме о диско | In a disco film
rewrite.why_better: Balanced lengths mean the answer has to be reasoned (an anthem hidden on a B-side), which makes the reveal more satisfying.

original.ru: Чей клип первым показал канал MTV в 1981 году?
original.en: Whose music video was the first ever shown on MTV in 1981?
original.fact: The song was called Video Killed the Radio Star, released in 1979, two years before MTV.

verdict: Michael Jackson is a strong trap, and once players remember 'Video Killed the Radio Star' the irony clicks; good reveal.

original.ru: Почему глаза Дэвида Боуи казались разного цвета?
original.en: Why did David Bowie's eyes look like two different colours?
options: * Удар друга в школьной драке | A friend's punch in a school fight
Цветная контактная линза | A coloured contact lens
Ожог от сценической пиротехники | A burn from stage pyrotechnics
Глазные капли | Eye drops he used
original.fact: One pupil stayed dilated for good. The puncher, George Underwood, later designed his album covers.

verdict: Surprising cause and a great twist (the friend who punched him designed his covers); credible distractors.

original.ru: О каком реальном событии песня Deep Purple Smoke on the Water?
original.en: Which real event is Deep Purple's Smoke on the Water about?
options: * Пожар в казино на концерте | A casino fire during a concert
Пожар на нефтяном танкере | A burning oil tanker
Костры на фестивале «Вудсток» | Bonfires at Woodstock
original.fact: In Montreux in 1971 a fan fired a flare at a Frank Zappa gig, and smoke drifted over Lake Geneva.

verdict: Everyone knows the riff, few know the story; the Montreux casino fire and Frank Zappa make a vivid reveal.

original.ru: Сколько лет было Стиви Уандеру, когда его песня впервые стала №1 в США?
original.en: How old was Stevie Wonder when he first had a US No. 1 hit?
original.fact: Fingertips (1963) was a live recording of 'Little Stevie', the blind boy wonder, on harmonica.

verdict: Surprisingly young; 'Little Stevie' gives a reasoning path. A tolerance of 7 on a 5-40 range is generous (6 to 20 all score), so consider 4.

original.ru: В каком году вышел альбом Майкла Джексона Thriller?
original.en: In what year was Michael Jackson's album Thriller released?
original.fact: Seven of its nine songs came out as singles, and every one made the US top ten.

verdict: Estimable release year with no surprise; the 'seven top-ten singles' fact is fine but does not rescue a date question.

original.ru: Какой французский дуэт прославился тем, что выступал в шлемах роботов?
original.en: Which French duo became famous for performing in robot helmets?
original.fact: They took the name from a review that panned their earlier band as 'a daft punky thrash'.

verdict: Easy recognition with real French duos as distractors, and the name-from-a-bad-review fact is a nice payoff. KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Хит BTS «Dynamite» (2020) — первая песня группы, целиком спетая на каком языке?
original.en: BTS's hit 'Dynamite' (2020) was the band's first song sung entirely in which language?
original.fact: It made BTS the first all-South Korean act to top the US Billboard Hot 100.

verdict: Players can reason that a global hit needed English, and Japanese is a credible trap; solid easy question.

original.ru: Какая группа выиграла «Евровидение-2006» в гриме и костюмах монстров?
original.en: Which band won Eurovision 2006 dressed and made up as monsters?
original.fact: It was Finland's first win, after trying without luck since 1961.

verdict: Memorable Eurovision moment; Rammstein and Slipknot never entered, so only Måneskin really competes, but the 45-year Finnish drought is a good reveal. KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Какое словечко для одержимого фаната пошло от песни Эминема 2000 года?
original.en: Which word for an obsessive fan comes from a 2000 Eminem song?
original.fact: In the song a fan called Stan writes Eminem ever more desperate letters; 'stan' is now in the Oxford dictionary.

verdict: Players who know the song deduce it, the others enjoy learning a slang word came from a track; credible slang distractors.

original.ru: Какая песня первой из рэп-композиций получила «Оскар»?
original.en: Which was the first rap song to win an Oscar?
options: * Lose Yourself — Эминем | Lose Yourself, Eminem
In da Club — 50 Cent | In da Club, 50 Cent
Empire State of Mind — Джей-Зи | Empire State of Mind, Jay-Z
Gold Digger — Канье Уэст | Gold Digger, Kanye West
original.fact: Eminem skipped the 2003 ceremony: sure he would not win, he was asleep at home.

verdict: 8 Mile makes it guessable, and 'he slept through his own Oscar' is a great reveal.

original.ru: Какую премию в 2018 году первым из рэперов получил Кендрик Ламар?
original.en: Which prize did Kendrick Lamar win in 2018, the first rapper ever to do so?
original.fact: Before him the Pulitzer for Music had only gone to classical composers and jazz musicians.

verdict: A rapper winning the Pulitzer is surprising, and the Nobel (Bob Dylan) is a clever trap; Kendrick is less known to the older players.

original.ru: Где впервые прозвучала песня Фаррелла Уильямса «Happy»?
original.en: Where was Pharrell Williams's song 'Happy' first heard?
options: * В мультфильме «Гадкий я 2» | In the film Despicable Me 2
В рекламе Coca-Cola | In a Coca-Cola advert
На открытии Олимпиады в Сочи | At the Sochi Olympics opening
В сериале «Теория большого взрыва» | In The Big Bang Theory
original.fact: Its video was the world's first 24-hour one: the song loops all day with different people dancing each time.

verdict: Many forget it began in a cartoon, credible launch-venue distractors, and the 24-hour video is a fun extra.

original.ru: Кем прославился рэпер Дрейк, прежде чем начал читать рэп?
original.en: What was the rapper Drake famous as before his music career?
options: * Актёр молодёжного сериала | A teen TV series actor
Ведущий кулинарного шоу | A cookery show host
original.fact: In the Canadian series Degrassi he played Jimmy, a basketball player who ends up in a wheelchair.

verdict: Surprising past for a rap star, but with nothing to reason from; mentioning Canada adds a hockey trap and a hint.

rewrite.q_ru: Рэпер Дрейк начинал не с музыки. Кем он сначала прославился у себя в Канаде?
rewrite.q_en: The rapper Drake did not start in music. What first made him famous in Canada?
options: * Актёр молодёжного сериала | A teen TV series actor
Ведущий кулинарного шоу | A cookery show host
rewrite.why_better: 'Canada' makes hockey a tempting trap, so the table debates before the Degrassi reveal.

original.ru: Сколько концертов в лондонской арене O2 собирался дать Майкл Джексон в 2009 году?
original.en: How many shows at London's O2 arena did Michael Jackson plan to play in 2009?
original.fact: At first 10 shows were announced, but tickets sold so fast that the number grew fivefold.

verdict: Famous, poignant event; 50 shows surprises people who remember 'a comeback tour', and the 10→50 fact makes a satisfying reveal.

original.ru: Сколько баллов набрал Александр Рыбак, победив на «Евровидении-2009»?
original.en: How many points did Alexander Rybak score when he won Eurovision 2009?
original.fact: It was a record under the old voting system; Rybak was born in Minsk and grew up in Norway.

verdict: Rybak is liked, but nobody has a sense of Eurovision point scales, so 387 cannot be estimated; the 'record' reveal is mild.

original.ru: Какой российский дуэт в 2003 году первым из наших артистов возглавил британский хит-парад?
original.en: Which Russian duo became the first Russian act to top the UK singles chart, in 2003?
original.fact: "All the Things She Said", the English version of "Ya soshla s uma", stayed at number one for four weeks.

verdict: Proud national moment both generations remember, with four credible 2000s girl groups as options.

original.ru: Кто написал музыку к «Миллиону алых роз»?
original.en: Who composed the music for "A Million Scarlet Roses"?
original.fact: The tune came from Pauls's Latvian song about a girl a goddess gave life to but forgot to give happiness.

verdict: Easy recognition for most, with strong composer distractors, and the original Latvian lullaby story is a lovely reveal. KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Из какого фильма песня «Прекрасное далёко»?
original.en: Which film is the song "Beautiful Faraway" from?
options: «Мэри Поппинс, до свидания» | Mary Poppins, Goodbye
* «Гостья из будущего» | Guest from the Future
original.fact: Yevgeny Krylatov and Yuri Entin wrote it: the same pair wrote "Winged Swings" for Adventures of Electronic.

verdict: A sing-along recognition question; Adventures of Electronic is a clever trap (same authors). KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Мелодию «Города золотого» выдали за старинную итальянскую. Кто её, как считается, сочинил?
original.en: The tune of "The Golden City" was passed off as old Italian music. Who is believed to have written it?
original.fact: Lutenist Vavilov released it in 1970 on a record of early music under the name of Francesco da Milano.

verdict: A great hoax story, but the answer is a name nobody knows; adding the fake 'Francesco da Milano' as a trap makes the hoax part of the game.

rewrite.q_ru: Мелодию «Города золотого» выдали за старинную итальянскую. Кто, как считается, её автор?
rewrite.q_en: The tune of The Golden City was passed off as old Italian music. Who is believed to have written it?
options: Франческо да Милано | Francesco da Milano
rewrite.why_better: The fake Italian name the record used becomes a trap, so players live through the hoax and the reveal explains how they were fooled.

original.ru: Как поначалу называлась песня «Подмосковные вечера»?
original.en: What was the song "Moscow Nights" first called?
original.fact: Leningrad became Moscow for a film about a sports festival; the world learned the tune from the 1961 jazz hit Midnight in Moscow.

verdict: Good story, but one distractor is the song's own title (absurd as an answer to 'first called') and the 'X Evenings' pattern makes it a pure elimination guess.

rewrite.q_ru: Песня «Подмосковные вечера» сначала была о другом городе. О каком?
rewrite.q_en: The song Moscow Nights was first about a different city. Which one?
rewrite.why_better: Four big Soviet cities are equally singable, so it is a real guess, and the reveal about the sports film and the jazz hit still lands.

original.ru: На какой гитаре в основном играл Высоцкий?
original.en: What kind of guitar did Vysotsky mostly play?
original.fact: The seven-string Russian guitar is tuned to a G major chord; Okudzhava, Galich, Vizbor and many other bards played it.

verdict: Many assume a normal six-string, so the 'Russian' seven-string surprises; the electric-guitar option is filler.

original.ru: Какой ВИА пел «Вологду» и «Косил Ясь конюшину»?
original.en: Which Soviet band sang "Vologda" and "Yas Was Mowing Clover"?
original.fact: In 1976 Pesniary became the first Soviet pop-rock band to tour the United States.

verdict: A medium-slot band-name recall: easy for the older players, opaque for the younger ones, with a modest US-tour reveal; Syabry is a clever trap but cannot rescue it.

original.ru: «Арлекино», прославившая Пугачёву, — переделка песни из какой страны?
original.en: "Arlekino", the song that made Pugacheva famous, was a cover of a song from which country?
original.fact: Bulgarian singer Emil Dimitrov wrote it, and Pugacheva won the Golden Orpheus grand prix in Bulgaria with it.

verdict: Most would guess Italy (Harlequin, commedia dell'arte), so Bulgaria surprises and the Golden Orpheus story completes it.

original.ru: В каком году Андрей Макаревич со школьными друзьями основал «Машину времени»?
original.en: In what year did Andrei Makarevich and school friends found Mashina Vremeni?
original.fact: At first the band had English names, The Kids and Time Machines; the Russian name came only in 1973.

verdict: A band founding year: estimable for older players, joyless for all; it uses the same formula as ru_music_048 in the same topic.

original.ru: В каком году Борис Гребенщиков основал «Аквариум»?
original.en: In what year did Boris Grebenshchikov found Aquarium?
original.fact: He started it with his friend, poet Anatoly "George" Gunitsky; their first official record came out only in the late 1980s.

verdict: Same 'founding year of a rock band' formula as ru_music_041, with a flatter reveal.

original.ru: Кого называли «королём вальса»?
original.en: Who was known as the Waltz King?
original.fact: His Blue Danube is the encore at every Vienna New Year's Concert, and Richard Strauss is no relation at all.

verdict: Easy recognition, but the correct option is the only full name with 'сына', a strong tell; the 'Richard Strauss is no relation' fact is good. KEEP with balanced options.

rewrite.q_ru: Кого называли «королём вальса»?
rewrite.q_en: Who was known as the Waltz King?
rewrite.why_better: Full names for every composer remove the length tell, so players recall the answer instead of spotting it.

original.ru: С кем сражается Щелкунчик в балете Чайковского?
original.en: Whom does the Nutcracker fight in Tchaikovsky's ballet?
options: Со Снежной королевой | The Snow Queen
* С Мышиным королём | The Mouse King
original.fact: For the Sugar Plum Fairy he secretly brought a brand new celesta from Paris so rivals could not use it first.

verdict: Easy recognition from the New Year ballet; the secret-celesta fact is a good payoff. KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Каким инструментом Бах прославился как исполнитель?
original.en: Which instrument made Bach famous as a performer?
original.fact: At 20 he walked some 450 km to Lübeck just to hear the organist Buxtehude play.

verdict: Most know Bach's organ (Toccata), so it is easy; the 450 km walk is a memorable reveal. KEEP as an easy question.

original.ru: Что вдохновило Мусоргского на «Картинки с выставки»?
original.en: What inspired Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition?
options: * Выставка умершего друга | A late friend's art show
original.fact: It was a memorial show for the artist Viktor Hartmann; Ravel's 1922 orchestration became the best known version.

verdict: Feels like a music-school test; the 'late friend' option stands out as the only personal one, and Hartmann/Ravel is a dry reveal.

original.ru: Бетховен посвятил Третью симфонию, а потом в гневе снял посвящение. Кому?
original.en: Beethoven dedicated his Third Symphony to someone, then angrily withdrew it. Who?
original.fact: On hearing in 1804 that Napoleon had made himself emperor, Beethoven tore the title page in half in a rage.

verdict: 'In anger' plus 1804 lets players reason to Napoleon, and tearing the title page is a vivid reveal; Mozart is a weak option.

original.ru: Какое сочинение 15 минут повторяет одни и те же две мелодии, только всё громче?
original.en: Which piece repeats the same two tunes for about 15 minutes, only getting louder?
original.fact: Ravel himself called it an experiment: "orchestral tissue without music."

verdict: Players can hum it to confirm, distractors are all famous pieces, and Ravel calling it 'orchestral tissue without music' is a fun reveal.

original.ru: Кто из этих композиторов НЕ входил в «Могучую кучку»?
original.en: Which of these composers was NOT in the Mighty Handful?
original.fact: Critic Stasov coined the name in 1867; Borodin, one of the five, was also a professor of chemistry.

verdict: A music-history exam question with NOT wording; the Borodin-was-a-chemist fact deserves its own question instead.

original.ru: Шопен умер в Париже. Где хранится его сердце?
original.en: Chopin died in Paris. Where is his heart kept?
options: В его могиле в Париже | In his Paris grave
* В костёле в Варшаве | In a Warsaw church
original.fact: As he wished, his sister smuggled it to Poland in a jar, said to be filled with cognac.

verdict: Gruesome-romantic surprise, all options plausible, and the jar of cognac smuggled by his sister makes everyone retell it.

original.ru: Сколько раз подряд принято играть пьесу Эрика Сати «Раздражения» (Vexations)?
original.en: How many times in a row is Erik Satie's piece Vexations traditionally played?
original.fact: Satie left a puzzling number on the score; in 1963 a relay of pianists led by John Cage took over 18 hours to play it.

verdict: Wonderful absurd fact, but the piece is unknown and the number cannot be estimated; giving the 18-hour marathon in the question gives players something to reason from.

rewrite.q_ru: Пьесу Сати «Раздражения» в 1963 году пианисты играли по очереди 18 часов. Сколько раз подряд?
rewrite.q_en: In 1963 a relay of pianists spent 18 hours playing Satie's Vexations. How many times in a row?
rewrite.why_better: The 18-hour marathon is both the hook and a clue (a short piece, over and over), so guesses become estimates and the number lands.

original.ru: Сколько секунд длится «тихая» пьеса Джона Кейджа, где музыкант ничего не играет?
original.en: How many seconds long is John Cage's silent piece, where the performer plays nothing?
original.fact: Its title gives it away: 4′33″. The music is whatever the hall supplies: coughs, rustles, breathing.

verdict: Funny premise (a piece of silence); those who know '4′33″' can compute it, others estimate, and the reveal lands.

original.ru: Что «растекается» на картине Сальвадора Дали «Постоянство памяти»?
original.en: What is melting in Salvador Dali's The Persistence of Memory?
original.fact: Dali said the idea came to him from a Camembert cheese melting in the heat.

verdict: Famous image, easy answer, but the melting camembert reveal makes it worth asking.

original.ru: Чего не хватает у статуи Венеры Милосской?
original.en: What is the Venus de Milo missing?
original.fact: She was found on the island of Milos in 1820 already armless; what her hands held is still debated.

verdict: Everyone knows she is armless; 'head' and 'wings' are fair nods to Nike of Samothrace. KEEP only as a deliberate easy warm-up.

original.ru: Что делают люди на картине Репина «Бурлаки на Волге»?
original.en: What are the men doing in Repin's Barge Haulers on the Volga?
original.fact: The man in front is Kanin, a real hauler and a defrocked priest, whom Repin painted from life.

verdict: The painting's title ('бурлаки') answers the question; the defrocked-priest fact is good. KEEP only as a free easy point.

original.ru: Как Леонардо да Винчи писал в своих тетрадях?
original.en: How did Leonardo da Vinci write in his notebooks?
options: * Зеркально, справа налево | In mirror script, right to left
Цифровым шифром | In a number code
original.fact: Leonardo was left-handed; perhaps this way his hand did not smudge the fresh ink.

verdict: Many half-remember mirror writing, the code and Latin options are credible, and left-handedness explains it.

original.ru: Что написано под трубкой на картине Рене Магритта?
original.en: What is written under the pipe in Rene Magritte's painting?
options: * «Это не трубка» | This is not a pipe
«Это не картина» | This is not a painting
original.fact: Magritte's answer: try stuffing it with tobacco; it is only a picture of a pipe.

verdict: A famous paradox that players can reason to via surrealism, and Magritte's 'try stuffing it with tobacco' is a witty reveal.

original.ru: Кто написал «Девочку с персиками»?
original.en: Who painted Girl with Peaches?
original.fact: The painter was 22, and 11-year-old Vera Mamontova sat for him for over a month.

verdict: A textbook painter-name match; those who know, know, others guess, and the age facts are mild.

original.ru: Почему картину Рембрандта называют «Ночной дозор»?
original.en: Why is Rembrandt's painting called The Night Watch?
options: * Её затемнил лак, а сцена дневная | Varnish darkened a daytime scene
Рембрандт писал её ночами | Rembrandt painted it at night
Её прятали от воров ночью | It was hidden at night from thieves
Так звали отряд стражи | That was the guard unit's name
original.fact: The name came over a century later, after dark varnish had hidden the daylight in the scene.

verdict: Real 'wait, seriously?': the Night Watch is a daytime scene; the correct option is the longest and gives the twist away, cheap to fix.

rewrite.q_ru: Почему картину Рембрандта называют «Ночной дозор»?
rewrite.q_en: Why is Rembrandt's painting called The Night Watch?
options: * Её затемнил лак | Varnish darkened it
Её писали ночами | It was painted at night
Её прятали ночью | It was hidden at night
Так звался отряд | The unit had that name
rewrite.why_better: Equal-length options hide the twist until the reveal says the scene is actually in daylight.

original.ru: Из чего Микеланджело высек своего «Давида»?
original.en: What did Michelangelo carve his David from?
options: * Из брошенной глыбы мрамора | An abandoned block of marble
Из гранитной скалы | A granite cliff
Из ствола дуба | An oak trunk
Из десятка мраморных частей | A dozen marble pieces
original.fact: Other sculptors had spoiled the block and it lay in the cathedral yard for 25 years.

verdict: Lovely 'reject block becomes masterpiece' story, but 'abandoned' is the only option with a twist, while the others are just other materials.

rewrite.q_ru: Из какого мрамора Микеланджело высек своего «Давида»?
rewrite.q_en: What marble did Michelangelo carve his David from?
options: * Из глыбы, испорченной другими | A block others had spoiled
Из колонны античного храма | A column from an ancient temple
Из глыбы, подаренной папой | A block the Pope gave him
Из обломков старой статуи | Pieces of an old statue
rewrite.why_better: Every option now tells a backstory, so the 'spoiled reject' is one credible story among four and the 25-years-in-the-yard reveal surprises.

original.ru: Сколько картин с кувшинками написал Клод Моне в своём саду в Живерни?
original.en: How many water lily paintings did Claude Monet make in his garden at Giverny?
original.fact: He made the pond himself by diverting a stream, and painted it for the last 30-odd years of his life.

verdict: Famous series, but there is little to anchor a guess; moving the '30 years' from the fact into the question gives an estimation path.

rewrite.q_ru: Моне больше 30 лет писал пруд в своём саду в Живерни. Сколько картин с кувшинками вышло?
rewrite.q_en: Monet painted his pond at Giverny for over 30 years. How many water lily paintings came of it?
rewrite.why_better: '30 years' lets players reason 'a few a year' and land near 250, turning a blind number into an estimate.

original.ru: Сколько картин написал Иван Айвазовский за свою жизнь?
original.en: How many paintings did Ivan Aivazovsky make in his lifetime?
original.fact: He painted almost to his last day: an unfinished canvas was left on his easel.

verdict: A staggering number everyone underestimates, and the generous tolerance rewards bold guesses; the fact is a mild coda.

original.ru: Из чего сделаны красные грани звёзд на башнях Московского Кремля?
original.en: What are the red faces of the Moscow Kremlin's tower stars made of?
original.fact: They are lit from inside by lamps; until 1935 four of those towers were topped with double-headed eagles.

verdict: Everyone knows the Kremlin stars, and glass vs copper vs granite gives a fair guess; 'Plastic' is a throwaway and the eagle fact is only a mild payoff.

original.ru: Какой замок вдохновил замок Спящей красавицы в Диснейленде?
original.en: Which castle inspired Sleeping Beauty Castle at Disneyland?
original.fact: King Ludwig II lived in his fairy-tale castle for just 172 days; paying tourists were let in within weeks of his death.

verdict: Satisfying recognition: everyone knows the Disney logo and photos of Neuschwanstein, Bran (Dracula) is a good trap, and 172 days in his own castle is a nice payoff. Note rulers_015 reuses the 'opened to tourists weeks after his death' fact.
