original.ru: Чьи лица высечены в скале горы Рашмор?
original.en: Whose faces are carved into Mount Rushmore?
options: * Четырёх президентов США | Four US presidents
Четырёх индейских вождей | Four Native American chiefs
Четырёх первых астронавтов | Four early astronauts
Четырёх английских королей | Four English kings
original.fact: They were meant to be carved down to the waist, but the money ran out in 1941, leaving just the 18-metre heads.

verdict: Easy recognition question; astronauts and English kings are absurd for a US mountain, so it is a free point, but the 'meant to be carved to the waist' fact pays off. Fine as a deliberate warm-up; swapping the absurd options for US generals and inventors would add a moment of thought.

original.ru: Писатель Мопассан, ненавидевший Эйфелеву башню, часто обедал в её ресторане. Почему?
original.en: Maupassant hated the Eiffel Tower yet often ate in its restaurant. Why?
options: * Только оттуда её не видно | It was the one spot he couldn't see it
Эйфель кормил его бесплатно | Eiffel fed him for free
Там работал его брат-повар | His brother was the chef
Это был самый дешёвый обед | It was the cheapest lunch in Paris
original.fact: So the story goes; he had signed the protest against the 'useless and monstrous' tower with Gounod and Garnier, the Opéra's architect.

verdict: A great 'why' question: the punchline (the only spot he could not see it) is guessable by wit, every distractor is a credible joke, and the room laughs at the reveal.

original.ru: Из какой страны был архитектор Сиднейского оперного театра?
original.en: Where was the architect of the Sydney Opera House from?
original.fact: Jørn Utzon quit in 1966 after rows with the government and never saw the finished building in person.

verdict: The Australia trap works and Denmark surprises, but the question itself is a dry nationality lookup; the better story (Utzon never saw it finished) is hidden in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Архитектор Сиднейской оперы так и не увидел её готовой. Откуда он был родом?
rewrite.q_en: The Sydney Opera House's architect never saw it finished. Where was he from?
rewrite.why_better: The hook puts the drama up front, so the answer lands as part of a story rather than a passport check.

original.ru: Шпиль Нотр-Дама, рухнувший при пожаре 2019 года, был построен в каком веке?
original.en: The Notre-Dame spire that fell in the 2019 fire dated from which century?
original.fact: The medieval spire came down in the late 1700s; Viollet-le-Duc built the new one in 1859 and gave an apostle statue at its base his own face.

verdict: Most assume the spire was medieval, so '19th century' is a real 'wait, seriously?', and the architect putting his own face on an apostle is a great payoff.

original.ru: Что построили в котловане недостроенного Дворца Советов в Москве?
original.en: What was built in the foundation pit of Moscow's never-finished Palace of Soviets?
original.fact: The palace was meant to replace the demolished Cathedral of Christ the Saviour; after the pool closed, the cathedral was rebuilt there.

verdict: The Palace of Soviets pit becoming a pool is a story the older players will tell around the table, and the cathedral coming full circle is a strong payoff; Rossiya and Zaryadye are credible traps.

original.ru: Что Наполеон увёз в Париж с Бранденбургских ворот в 1806 году?
original.en: What did Napoleon take from Berlin's Brandenburg Gate to Paris in 1806?
options: * Колесницу с богиней на крыше | The chariot statue on top
Сами створки ворот | The gates themselves
Часы с фасада | The clock on the front
original.fact: The quadriga came back in 1814 after Napoleon's defeat, and the goddess's staff has carried an Iron Cross and eagle since.

verdict: The stolen quadriga is a decent fact, but the correct option is the only long descriptive one (telegraphed) and 'Bells' is weak filler.

rewrite.q_ru: Какой трофей Наполеон увёз в Париж с Бранденбургских ворот в 1806 году?
rewrite.q_en: What trophy did Napoleon take to Paris from Berlin's Brandenburg Gate in 1806?
options: * Колесницу с богиней | The goddess's chariot
Часы с фасада | The front clock
rewrite.why_better: Balanced, equally concrete options stop the answer from being spotted by its length.

original.ru: Сколько лет прошло от закладки до завершения Кёльнского собора?
original.en: How many years passed from start to finish of Cologne Cathedral?
original.fact: Work stalled in 1473, and for some 400 years a medieval crane stood on the unfinished south tower.

verdict: Everyone knows cathedrals took ages, so there is a reasoning path, and 632 years plus a crane left up for 400 years is a fun reveal; the range and tolerance are fair.

original.ru: Сколько лет пирамида Хеопса оставалась самым высоким сооружением, построенным людьми?
original.en: For how many years was the Great Pyramid the tallest structure built by people?
original.fact: Only in the Middle Ages did an English cathedral spire beat it, and that spire later fell; the pyramid still stands.

verdict: A brilliant scale question: everyone knows the pyramid, the answer (about 3,800 years) is genuinely staggering, and the fallen English spire is a perfect kicker.

original.ru: Луковицу какого цветка в Голландии 1630-х продавали по цене дома?
original.en: In the 1630s Dutch buyers paid the price of a house for a bulb of which flower?
original.fact: Streaked tulips were the craze, and bulbs were resold while still in the ground until the market crashed in 1637.

verdict: Tulip mania is fairly well known so it is close to recognition, but the 'price of a house' framing is fun and the bulbs traded while still in the ground make a good payoff.

original.ru: Английское salary (зарплата) происходит от латинского слова, означающего…
original.en: The word salary comes from the Latin word for…
original.fact: Soldier comes from money too: from the solidus, a Roman gold coin, as a soldier was a man who served for pay.

verdict: A classic word-origin question with a satisfying 'salt' reveal and credible distractors; the soldier/solidus fact doubles the payoff.

original.ru: В честь чего названа нью-йоркская Уолл-стрит?
original.en: What is New York's Wall Street named after?
options: * Настоящей стены поселенцев | A real settlers' wall
Банкира по фамилии Уолл | A banker named Wall
Стены первой биржи | The wall of the first exchange
Стены злых кредиторов | A wall of angry creditors
original.fact: In the 1650s the Dutch built a wooden wall around New Amsterdam; it came down in 1699 but the street kept its name.

verdict: Good literal-name reveal, but 'real settlers' wall' gives itself away with the word 'real' and 'a wall of angry creditors' is a throwaway.

rewrite.q_ru: В честь чего названа нью-йоркская Уолл-стрит?
rewrite.q_en: What is New York's Wall Street named after?
options: Банкира Уолла | A banker named Wall
Стены биржи | The stock exchange wall
Капитана Уолла | A captain named Wall
rewrite.why_better: Short parallel options with two tempting 'someone named Wall' traps make the literal answer a real surprise.

original.ru: В какой стране работает старейший из ныне действующих банков, основанный в 1472 году?
original.en: The oldest bank still operating was founded in 1472. In which country?
original.fact: Siena's Monte dei Paschi began as a mount of piety, a charitable pawnshop that saved the poor from loan sharks.

verdict: Italy is guessable via Renaissance banking, but a bare country answer is flat; the pawnshop-for-the-poor origin is the better hook and is buried in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Старейший действующий банк мира (1472) начинался как ломбард для бедных. В какой стране?
rewrite.q_en: The oldest bank still operating (1472) began as a pawnshop for the poor. In which country?
rewrite.why_better: The surprising pawnshop origin moves into the question, so players react before the country is even revealed.

original.ru: Что изображено на мостах с банкнот евро?
original.en: What do the bridges on euro banknotes show?
options: Мосты столиц еврозоны | Bridges of eurozone capitals
Мосты стран-основательниц | Bridges of the founding nations
original.fact: They were invented so no country felt left out; later the Dutch town of Spijkenisse built real copies.

verdict: Most players have held a euro note and never noticed the bridges are fictional; the Dutch town building real copies is a lovely, tellable payoff.

original.ru: Из чего были сделаны первые в мире монеты, отчеканенные в Лидии в VII веке до н. э.?
original.en: What were the world's first coins, struck in Lydia in the 7th century BC, made of?
options: * Сплава золота и серебра | A gold and silver alloy
original.fact: The natural alloy electrum was panned from the river Pactolus, and Lydia's king Croesus became a byword for wealth.

verdict: Lydia means little to most players, the long date-laden question reads like a textbook, and the correct option is the only two-part answer (telegraphed). Croesus is the hook worth using.

rewrite.q_ru: Из чего чеканили первые монеты в мире — в Лидии, на родине богача Крёза?
rewrite.q_en: What were the world's first coins made of, in Lydia, the land of rich King Croesus?
options: * Золото с серебром | Gold mixed with silver
Медь с оловом | Copper and tin
Серебро со свинцом | Silver and lead
Железо с никелем | Iron and nickel
rewrite.why_better: 'Rich as Croesus' gives players a foothold, and four parallel two-metal alloys remove the length tell.

original.ru: Копейка получила название по тому, что было на ней изображено. Что это?
original.en: The kopeck is named after what was pictured on it. What?
options: * Всадник с копьём | A rider with a spear
Двуглавый орёл | A double headed eagle
Пучок колосьев | A sheaf of wheat
original.fact: From 1535, under regent Elena Glinskaya, the coin showed the grand prince on horseback holding a spear (kopyo).

verdict: Kopeck/kopyo makes the answer almost self-evident, so there is little surprise, but Russian players enjoy confirming it and the Elena Glinskaya detail adds a bit. Acceptable as an easy recognition question.

original.ru: Какой была самая крупная купюра Зимбабве, выпущенная в 2009 году?
original.en: What was Zimbabwe's biggest banknote, issued in 2009?
original.fact: After two redenominations it equalled 10²⁷ original Zimbabwe dollars; by April 2009 the currency was abandoned.

verdict: The Zimbabwe trillion note is a known meme yet still makes people gasp at the exact size, and 10^27 original dollars is a great payoff.

original.ru: Сколько пенни было в британском фунте до 1971 года?
original.en: How many pennies were there in a British pound before 1971?
original.fact: A pound was 20 shillings of 12 pence each, until Britain went decimal with 100 pence in 1971.

verdict: 240 is surprising, and players who half-remember shillings can reason toward it; the 20 x 12 explanation is satisfying.

original.ru: Сколько раз долларовую купюру можно согнуть туда-обратно, прежде чем она порвётся?
original.en: How many times can a dollar bill be folded back and forth before it tears?
original.fact: A bill bends almost like cloth rather than paper, which is why one note can pass from hand to hand for years.

verdict: A fun 'who would test that?' number, but there is nothing to estimate from, so it is near pure guessing; the cloth-not-paper fact is the clue that should be in the question.

rewrite.q_ru: Долларовая купюра гнётся почти как ткань. Сколько сгибов туда-обратно она выдержит?
rewrite.q_en: A dollar bill bends almost like cloth. How many back-and-forth folds can it take?
rewrite.why_better: The cloth clue (from the fact) gives players a reason to guess high, turning a blind number into an estimation argument.

original.ru: «Мишленовские звёзды» ресторанам раздаёт компания, которая делает…
original.en: The Michelin stars for restaurants come from a company that makes…
original.fact: In 1900 the guide was free: the more people drove out to eat, the faster they wore out their tyres.

verdict: A top-tier reveal: the tyre company behind the most prestigious restaurant award, with a clever business reason in the fact. Some already know it, but it still starts conversations.

original.ru: Из какой страны компания Nokia?
original.en: Which country is Nokia from?
original.fact: It is named after the Finnish town of Nokia; one theory says the old Finnish word meant sables.

verdict: Nokia = Finland is widely known, so this is a free warm-up; the sables etymology is a mild bonus. Fine as a deliberate easy recognition question.

original.ru: В честь кого назван Nike?
original.en: Who is Nike named after?
options: * Греческой богини победы | The Greek goddess of victory
Римской богини охоты | The Roman goddess of hunting
original.fact: Employee Jeff Johnson dreamt up the name; founder Phil Knight wanted to call the firm Dimension Six.

verdict: Familiar recognition with a good trap (the Roman goddess of hunting), and the 'Dimension Six' near-miss name is a fun payoff. The 'named after' formula recurs in the bank but the fact does not repeat.

original.ru: Как изначально расшифровывалось название LG?
original.en: What did LG originally stand for?
original.fact: Two firms: Lak-Hui ("Lucky") made face cream and GoldStar made radios; "Life's Good" came later.

verdict: Everyone knows 'Life's Good', so the trap is perfect and 'Lucky Goldstar' (face cream plus radios) is a real surprise.

original.ru: С чего начиналась Nokia в 1865 году?
original.en: What did Nokia start out making in 1865?
options: * Бумажная масса | Wood pulp for paper
original.fact: First a pulp mill; rubber boots and cables came with a 1967 merger, and mobile phones only in the 1980s.

verdict: Nokia making paper pulp (and later rubber boots) is a classic 'wait, seriously?' with solid distractors. Note brands_013 is also about Nokia; consider not drawing both in one evening.

original.ru: Что создатель тубы Pringles завещал сделать со своим прахом?
original.en: What did the man who designed the Pringles can want done with his ashes?
options: Отправить в космос | Sent into space
Развеять над картофельным полем | Scattered over a potato field
* Похоронить в банке Pringles | Buried in a Pringles can
Замуровать в стену завода | Sealed in the factory wall
original.fact: Chemist Fredric Baur died in 2008; on the way to the funeral his children bought a can at a shop.

verdict: Absurd-but-true: the correct answer is the funniest option, so groups laugh as they pick it, and the children buying the can on the way to the funeral is a perfect kicker. The option repeats 'Pringles' from the question, a mild clue.

original.ru: Из чего сложено название IKEA?
original.en: What is the name IKEA made of?
options: * Имя основателя, ферма и деревня | Founder, his farm and village
Имена четырёх детей основателя | Founder's four children
Аббревиатура мебельной фабрики | A furniture factory acronym
original.fact: Ingvar Kamprad, Elmtaryd farm, Agunnaryd village; dyslexic Kamprad also gave products names, not numbers.

verdict: IKEA is universally familiar and the acronym reveal is satisfying, though the correct option is the most specific one; the dyslexia/names-not-numbers fact lifts the payoff.

original.ru: Чем торговала Samsung, когда открылась в 1938 году?
original.en: What did Samsung trade in when it opened in 1938?
options: * Сушёной рыбой и лапшой | Dried fish and noodles
original.fact: It was a grocery trader in Daegu; electronics came in the late 1960s, starting with a black and white TV.

verdict: A great surprise (Samsung began with dried fish), but the correct answer is the only two-item option, which telegraphs it as in the carrot anchor.

rewrite.q_ru: Чем торговала Samsung, когда открылась в 1938 году?
rewrite.q_en: What did Samsung trade in when it opened in 1938?
rewrite.why_better: Single-item options remove the length tell so the fish answer becomes a real surprise.

original.ru: С какого года строит храмы японская Kongō Gumi — её называют старейшей компанией мира?
original.en: Since what year has Japan's Kongō Gumi, often called the oldest company, built temples?
original.fact: Its craftsmen came from Korea to build the Shitennō-ji temple; the firm stayed independent until 2006.

verdict: Kongō Gumi is unknown to most players and a founding year is hard to estimate; the 1,400-year lifespan is the real wow but only emerges if players also know it closed in 2006.

rewrite.q_ru: Японская фирма Kongō Gumi оставалась самостоятельной до 2006 года. В каком году её основали?
rewrite.q_en: Japan's temple builder Kongō Gumi stayed independent until 2006. In what year was it founded?
rewrite.why_better: Anchoring the 2006 end date makes the founding year land as a jaw-dropping 1,400-year lifespan, and the wider tolerance rewards a bold early guess.

original.ru: В каком году в Киото основали компанию Nintendo?
original.en: In what year was Nintendo founded in Kyoto?
original.fact: Fusajiro Yamauchi founded it in the 19th century; Nintendo only turned to video games in the 1970s.

verdict: Most gamers are surprised Nintendo predates cars and films, and the range invites reasoning; the payoff would be stronger if the fact mentioned it began by making hanafuda playing cards.

original.ru: Что должна была охранять Терракотовая армия в Китае?
original.en: What was China's Terracotta Army made to guard?
options: * Гробницу первого императора | The first emperor's tomb
original.fact: The clay soldiers were buried by Qin Shi Huang's tomb to serve him after death, and each has its own face.

verdict: Easy recognition question with a guessable answer; the 'every soldier has its own face' fact is a decent payoff. Fine as a warm-up.

original.ru: Какое число римляне не могли записать своими цифрами?
original.en: Which number could the Romans not write with their numerals?
original.fact: Zero as a number reached Europe from India, via Arab mathematicians, only in the Middle Ages.

verdict: Most adults know the Romans had no zero, so it is an easy recognition point; 'One' is an absurd option. Acceptable as a warm-up, with a cheap distractor fix.

rewrite.q_ru: Какое число римляне не могли записать своими цифрами?
rewrite.q_en: Which number could the Romans not write with their numerals?
rewrite.why_better: 'A thousand' (is it M?) and 'Four' (IIII or IV?) make players hesitate and argue instead of eliminating instantly.

original.ru: Тело какого животного у Большого сфинкса в Гизе?
original.en: The Great Sphinx of Giza has the body of which animal?
original.fact: Napoleon's troops did not shoot off its nose: a drawing from 1737 already shows it missing.

verdict: Almost everyone knows the Sphinx is a lion, so the question itself is free; the Napoleon nose myth-buster is the real payoff. Keep only as an easy warm-up.

original.ru: Что такое термополий в Помпеях?
original.en: What was a thermopolium in Pompeii?
options: * Уличная закусочная | A street food counter
original.fact: It was Rome's fast food: people in apartment blocks, often without kitchens, bought ready meals there.

verdict: 'Thermo' plus Pompeii gives a reasoning path, the distractors are credible, and Roman fast food for kitchenless flats is a fun modern parallel.

original.ru: Что должен был проверить Архимед, когда крикнул «Эврика!»?
original.en: What was Archimedes trying to test when he shouted "Eureka!"?
options: * Из чистого ли золота корона | If a crown was pure gold
Круглая ли Земля | If the Earth was round
Глубину моря | How deep the sea was
Прочность моста | How strong a bridge was
original.fact: Getting into a bath he saw the water rise, a way to compare volumes; Vitruvius says he ran home naked.

verdict: Everyone knows 'Eureka!' and the bath, few know why; the naked run home is a great payoff. The correct option is much longer than the others (telegraphed).

rewrite.q_ru: Что должен был проверить Архимед, когда крикнул «Эврика!»?
rewrite.q_en: What was Archimedes trying to test when he shouted "Eureka!"?
options: * Из золота ли корона | If a crown was pure gold
Кругла ли Земля | If the Earth was round
Глубоко ли море | How deep the sea was
Прочен ли мост | If a bridge was strong
rewrite.why_better: Parallel 'is it X' options of equal length remove the length tell.

original.ru: Что сделал Ксеркс, когда буря разрушила его мост через Геллеспонт?
original.en: What did Xerxes do when a storm wrecked his bridge over the Hellespont?
options: Принёс в жертву коня | Sacrificed his horse
Отменил поход | Called off the war
* Велел высечь море плетьми | Had the sea whipped
original.fact: Herodotus says the water got 300 lashes and a pair of shackles thrown in, and the bridge was built again.

verdict: Whipping the sea is absurd and true, the other options are sensible-sounding, and 300 lashes plus shackles is a laugh-out-loud payoff.

original.ru: Какой древний народ обозначал ноль значком в виде раковины?
original.en: Which ancient people wrote zero with a sign shaped like a shell?
original.fact: Mesoamericans came up with zero on their own, apart from India, and the Maya used it to count dates over millennia.

verdict: The shell-shaped zero is a nice detail, but the distractors are weak: the Vikings are absurd and the Romans had no zero at all (ancient_004 even teaches that), so Maya wins by elimination.

rewrite.q_ru: Какой древний народ обозначал ноль значком в виде раковины?
rewrite.q_en: Which ancient people wrote zero with a sign shaped like a shell?
rewrite.why_better: Four credible ancient peoples (the seafaring Phoenicians are a tempting 'shell' trap) replace two give-away eliminations.

original.ru: Для чего римляне собирали мочу из общественных уборных?
original.en: What did the Romans collect urine from public toilets for?
original.fact: Its ammonia brightened wool; Vespasian taxed it, and that gave us the saying: money does not smell.

verdict: Gross, surprising and educational: urine for laundry gets a groan and a laugh, and 'money does not smell' is a payoff people will repeat.

original.ru: До скольких лет дожил первый римский император Август?
original.en: How old was Augustus, the first Roman emperor, when he died?
original.fact: He ruled for over 40 years, and the month of August was named after him while he was still alive.

verdict: An emperor's age at death is an exam-style number with a dull reveal; the hook (August named after him while alive) sits in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Месяц август назван в честь императора Августа ещё при его жизни. До скольких лет он дожил?
rewrite.q_en: August was named after Emperor Augustus in his lifetime. How old was he when he died?
rewrite.why_better: The month hook makes the subject instantly familiar and hints that he lived long enough to see it.

original.ru: Сколько тысяч человек, по оценкам историков, жило в Риме в эпоху расцвета?
original.en: How many thousand people lived in Rome at its peak, by historians' estimates?
original.fact: Rome may have been one of the first cities in history to reach a million people, alongside China's Chang'an.

verdict: Rome reaching a million is a decent fact, but 'thousand people' as the unit is awkward and there is nothing in the question or fact to estimate from. Better rebuilt as a multiple-choice question ('which was likely the first city to reach a million people?').

original.ru: Чем Один заплатил за глоток из источника мудрости?
original.en: What did Odin pay for a drink from the well of wisdom?
options: * Своим глазом | One of his eyes
Своей рукой | One of his hands
original.fact: The eye stayed in the giant Mimir's well; the god who lost a hand was Tyr, bitten off by the wolf Fenrir.

verdict: Odin's missing eye is familiar from Marvel and mythology, the distractors are plausible sacrifices, and the Tyr hand twist is a good payoff.

original.ru: Кицунэ из японских легенд — это хитрый волшебный...
original.en: In Japanese legend, a kitsune is a cunning magical...
original.fact: The older and stronger a kitsune, the more tails: legend says a new one grows every hundred years, and the mightiest have nine.

verdict: Kitsune = fox is easy for the anime-literate younger players and guessable for the rest; the nine tails fact is a nice bonus. Fine as an easy recognition question.

original.ru: В кого влюбился Нарцисс?
original.en: Who did Narcissus fall in love with?
options: * В своё отражение | His own reflection
В нимфу Эхо | The nymph Echo
В богиню Геру | The goddess Hera
В мраморную статую | A marble statue
original.fact: It was the nymph Echo who loved him in vain and wasted away until only her voice was left, hence the word echo.

verdict: The word 'narcissism' gives it away, though Echo is a good trap; acceptable as a deliberate easy warm-up.

original.ru: Кем по ремеслу были лепреконы в ирландском фольклоре?
original.en: In Irish folklore, what was the leprechaun's trade?
original.fact: Already in a medieval Irish saga, captured leprechauns buy their freedom with three wishes; the pot of gold came later.

verdict: Leprechauns are familiar and 'shoemaker' surprises; the buckled-shoe image gives a faint reasoning path. Solid.

original.ru: Как японские боги выманили богиню солнца Аматэрасу из пещеры?
original.en: How did the Japanese gods lure the sun goddess Amaterasu out of her cave?
options: * Устроили шумное веселье | They threw a noisy party
Пообещали ей рис | They promised her rice
Устроили землетрясение | They caused an earthquake
Притворились спящими | They pretended to sleep
original.fact: The goddess Uzume danced so comically the gods roared with laughter; Amaterasu peeked out and saw herself in a mirror.

verdict: Amaterasu is half-familiar, but 'the gods threw a party' is a delightful answer and the mirror trick is a great payoff.

original.ru: Как, по японским поверьям, одолеть водяного каппу?
original.en: In Japanese folklore, how can you beat a kappa, the river imp?
options: * Низко ему поклониться | Bow deeply to it
Посмотреть ему в глаза | Stare it in the eye
Спеть ему песню | Sing it a song
Бросить в него рыбу | Throw a fish at it
original.fact: The polite kappa bows back, spills the water from the dish on top of its head and loses all its strength.

verdict: Beating a monster by bowing to it is a wonderful twist, the distractors are credible folklore moves, and the spilled-water explanation is a perfect payoff.

original.ru: Каким мифическим существам обязаны своим названием слова «музей» и «музыка»?
original.en: Which mythical beings gave us the words 'museum' and 'music'?
original.fact: The Mouseion, 'shrine of the Muses', in Alexandria was a research centre with a great library, and music was the 'art of the Muses'.

verdict: The words 'museum' and 'music' both contain 'mus', so the answer is self-evident; it works only as an easy warm-up (consider moving it to easy).

original.ru: Велеса летописи называют «скотьим богом». Чем ещё он ведал?
original.en: The chronicles call Veles the 'god of cattle'. What else did he rule?
original.fact: Cattle were the main measure of wealth in old times, so the 'cattle god' also looked after prosperity and trade.

verdict: The 'cattle god' hint makes wealth guessable, which is nice, but the distractors (war, sun, fire) are generic and the reveal is mild.

rewrite.q_ru: Летописи называют Велеса «скотьим богом». Чему ещё он покровительствовал?
rewrite.q_en: The chronicles call Veles the 'god of cattle'. What else did he rule over?
rewrite.why_better: Thunder (Perun's domain) is a tempting Slavic trap, so players who know a little mythology must think rather than eliminate.

original.ru: Сколько примерно двустиший-шлок в индийском эпосе «Махабхарата»?
original.en: About how many couplets, or shlokas, are in the Indian epic, the Mahabharata?
original.fact: That is about 1.8 million words, roughly ten times the Iliad and the Odyssey put together.

verdict: Nobody can estimate couplets in the Mahabharata and the number means nothing on its own; the real wow (about ten times the Iliad and Odyssey combined) needs a different question with a different answer.

original.ru: В каком году Джордж Смит объявил, что нашёл на табличке о Гильгамеше рассказ о потопе?
original.en: In which year did George Smith announce he had found a flood story on a Gilgamesh tablet?
original.fact: Colleagues said that on reading the tablet Smith rushed around the room in delight and began taking off his clothes.

verdict: George Smith is unknown and the year is arbitrary; the fun part is that he started undressing in excitement, which deserves its own multiple-choice question rather than a date.

original.ru: Кто был главным противником Ричарда Львиное Сердце в Третьем крестовом походе?
original.en: Who was Richard the Lionheart's great rival in the Third Crusade?
original.fact: They never met face to face, yet they swapped gifts, and Richard called Saladin the greatest leader in the Muslim world.

verdict: Saladin is a fair recognition answer, but Sinbad and Harun al-Rashid are throwaways and the correct option is much shorter than the rest; the gift-swapping rivalry is the better hook.

rewrite.q_ru: Ричард Львиное Сердце в Крестовом походе получал подарки от главного врага. От кого?
rewrite.q_en: On crusade, Richard the Lionheart received gifts from his great enemy. Who was it?
rewrite.why_better: The 'gifts from the enemy' hook adds surprise, and four similar Muslim rulers' names remove the Sinbad giveaway.

original.ru: Кто добрался до Северной Америки примерно за 500 лет до Колумба?
original.en: Who reached North America about 500 years before Columbus?
original.fact: Tree rings in wood they cut show that Vikings were working in Newfoundland in the year 1021.

verdict: A familiar, guessable question with a tree-ring payoff that feels like detective work; fine.

original.ru: Кто около 1450 года начал печатать книги наборным шрифтом в Европе?
original.en: Who began printing books with movable type in Europe around 1450?
options: Леонардо да Винчи | Leonardo da Vinci
original.fact: Europe was late: China had movable type around 1040, and Korea printed a book with metal type in 1377.

verdict: Gutenberg is a school-exam answer next to Columbus and Galileo; the interesting part (China and Korea were centuries earlier) is hidden in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Китай печатал наборным шрифтом с 1040 года. Кто начал так печатать в Европе около 1450-го?
rewrite.q_en: China printed with movable type from 1040. Who started doing it in Europe around 1450?
options: Леонардо да Винчи | Leonardo da Vinci
rewrite.why_better: The China hook adds a 'Europe was late' surprise, and Fyodorov (a real printer) plus Dürer (an engraver) are credible traps.

original.ru: Где стояла столица ацтеков Теночтитлан?
original.en: Where did the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan stand?
options: * На острове посреди озера | On an island in a lake
На вершине вулкана | On top of a volcano
В пещерах под землёй | In caves underground
На берегу океана | On the ocean shore
original.fact: The Spanish compared the city of causeways and canals to Venice; Mexico City now stands on the drained lake.

verdict: The island city is a good fact, but 'in caves underground' is filler and the question reads like a geography quiz; the Venice comparison is a better way in.

rewrite.q_ru: Испанцы сравнивали столицу ацтеков Теночтитлан с Венецией. Почему?
rewrite.q_en: The Spanish compared the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan to Venice. Why?
options: * Стояла на острове в озере | It stood on an island in a lake
Славилась стеклом и масками | It was famous for glass and masks
Была построена на морских сваях | It was built on piles in the sea
Её заложили итальянцы | Italians had founded it
rewrite.why_better: Players reason from what they know about Venice, and the drained-lake payoff about Mexico City lands harder.

original.ru: К какому веку относятся первые описания чумного доктора в маске с клювом?
original.en: From which century do the first descriptions of the beaked plague doctor mask come?
original.fact: Nobody wore it during the Black Death: a doctor to Louis XIII described the costume during a plague outbreak in 1619.

verdict: Busts the Black Death image everyone has: the beaked mask is 300 years later, a real 'wait, seriously?'.

original.ru: Монголы построили по всей империи сеть станций «ям». Для чего она была?
original.en: The Mongols built a network of yam stations across their empire. What was it for?
options: * Для почты и гонцов | Mail and messengers
Для слежки за звёздами | Watching the stars
original.fact: Riders changed horses at stations every 30 to 60 km; the Russian word yamshchik, a coachman, comes from yam.

verdict: The yamshchik link is a great hook for Russian players but it is only in the fact, and 'watching the stars' is a throwaway.

rewrite.q_ru: Монгольские «ямы» подарили русскому языку слово «ямщик». Чем они были?
rewrite.q_en: The Mongol yam gave Russian the word yamshchik, a coachman. What were the yams?
rewrite.why_better: The familiar Russian word gives a reasoning path and an 'aha', and 'prison pits' is a fun literal-minded trap.

original.ru: Какой из этих городов монголы так и НЕ взяли?
original.en: Which of these cities did the Mongols NEVER take?
original.fact: In 1242 the Mongol army turned back from Central Europe, usually explained by news that the Great Khan Ögedei had died.

verdict: Good reasoning question for Russians who know Kyiv fell in 1240; the NOT wording is clear. The turn-back story is a modest payoff.

original.ru: Чьё паломничество в Мекку в 1324 году, говорят, обрушило цену золота в Каире?
original.en: Whose pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324 is said to have crashed the price of gold in Cairo?
options: * Мансы Мусы, правителя Мали | Mansa Musa of Mali
Короля Англии | The King of England
original.fact: He gave gold away so freely that, a chronicler wrote, it stayed cheaper in Egypt for at least twelve years.

verdict: Same 1324 Cairo gold story as rulers_021 (and per the script money_027), and here the correct option is the only named specific ruler among vague titles; keep rulers_021 instead.

original.ru: Сколько миллионов квадратных километров занимала Монгольская империя на пике?
original.en: How many million square kilometres did the Mongol Empire cover at its peak?
original.fact: That is about the size of North America: the empire stretched from Korea to Eastern Europe.

verdict: A pure area estimate with no anchor; players have no feel for millions of square kilometres unless given a comparison.

rewrite.q_ru: Россия занимает 17 млн км². Сколько миллионов км² занимала Монгольская империя на пике?
rewrite.q_en: Russia covers 17 million km². How many million km² did the Mongol Empire cover at its peak?
rewrite.why_better: Russia's size (about 17 million km², school knowledge) is a number every player in this family knows, so the guess becomes a real 'bigger or smaller than Russia?' debate.

original.ru: Какой длины гобелен из Байё, вышитая история завоевания Англии в 1066 году?
original.en: How long is the Bayeux Tapestry, the stitched story of the conquest of England in 1066?
original.fact: Almost 70 metres, and it is not really a tapestry: the pictures are embroidered on linen, not woven.

verdict: Nice 'it is not even a tapestry' payoff, but the length is a blind guess for most and the question reads dry.

rewrite.q_ru: Гобелен из Байё — вышитый «комикс» о завоевании Англии. Какой он длины в метрах?
rewrite.q_en: The Bayeux Tapestry is an embroidered comic strip of the conquest of England. How long is it, in metres?
rewrite.why_better: Calling it a comic strip makes players picture a long scroll of panels, a better basis for a guess.

original.ru: В каком году затонул «Титаник»?
original.en: In which year did the Titanic sink?
original.fact: Fourteen years earlier the novel Futility described an "unsinkable" liner called Titan that sinks after hitting an iceberg.

verdict: Everyone knows 1912, so the question is free, but the 'Futility' novel predicting the sinking is a superb payoff. Keep as a deliberate easy recognition question.

original.ru: В каком году люди впервые прошлись по Луне?
original.en: In which year did people first walk on the Moon?
original.fact: Apollo 11's guidance computer had about 4 KB of working memory, a million times less than a modern smartphone.

verdict: 1969 is common knowledge, so it is an exam warm-up; the 4 KB computer fact gives some payoff. Keep only as a deliberate easy recognition question.

original.ru: Огромную надпись HOLLYWOOD на холмах Лос-Анджелеса поставили в 1923 году. Что она рекламировала?
original.en: The giant HOLLYWOOD sign went up in the Los Angeles hills in 1923. What was it advertising?
options: * Новый жилой посёлок | A new housing estate
original.fact: It first read HOLLYWOODLAND, the name of the estate; the last four letters only came down in 1949.

verdict: Everyone knows the sign, almost nobody knows it was a real-estate ad, and HOLLYWOODLAND is a great tellable reveal; the film-studio trap is perfect.

original.ru: Кто первым в истории получил две Нобелевские премии?
original.en: Who was the first person ever to win two Nobel Prizes?
original.fact: Her notebooks are still radioactive: they are kept in lead-lined boxes and readers must wear protective clothing.

verdict: Curie is a known answer for many, but Einstein and Bohr are credible traps and the radioactive notebooks are a memorable payoff.

original.ru: В честь кого назван плюшевый мишка Тедди?
original.en: Who is the teddy bear named after?
options: * Президента США Теодора Рузвельта | US President Theodore Roosevelt
Медведя из Лондонского зоопарка | A bear at London Zoo
Мастерицы Маргарете Штайфф | Toymaker Margarete Steiff
Русского циркового медведя | A Russian circus bear
original.fact: In 1902 Roosevelt refused to shoot a bear tied up for him on a hunt, and a newspaper cartoon made the story famous.

verdict: Familiar subject with a good Steiff trap, and the 'refused to shoot a tied bear' story is satisfying.

original.ru: Каким был первый радиосигнал через Атлантику, который, по словам Маркони, он принял в 1901 году?
original.en: What was the first radio signal across the Atlantic that Marconi said he received, in 1901?
options: * Буква S азбуки Морзе | The Morse letter S
original.fact: Three faint clicks came through a telephone receiver, and the 150-metre aerial was held up in the sky by a kite.

verdict: The SOS trap is good, but the question is long and clunky to read, and the kite-held aerial (the fun bit) is hidden in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Маркони поднял антенну на воздушном змее. Какой сигнал он принял через Атлантику в 1901-м?
rewrite.q_en: Marconi flew his aerial on a kite. What signal did he say he got across the Atlantic in 1901?
options: * Букву S азбуки Морзе | The Morse letter S
rewrite.why_better: Shorter and opens with a vivid image, so the 'just three clicks' reveal feels charming rather than technical.

original.ru: Какой канал открылся в 1914 году?
original.en: Which canal opened in 1914?
original.fact: A voyage from New York to San Francisco was more than halved: no more sailing round the tip of South America.

verdict: Matching a canal to its opening year is a pure school exam question, and the 'halved the voyage' fact is predictable.

original.ru: В какой стране в 1989 году прошла «бархатная революция»?
original.en: Which country had the Velvet Revolution in 1989?
original.fact: Playwright Václav Havel was still in prison in spring 1989, and by the end of that year he was president.

verdict: A known name-the-country question; the much better story (a jailed playwright became president within months) is buried in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Весной 1989-го драматург сидел в тюрьме, а к концу года стал президентом. Какой страны?
rewrite.q_en: In spring 1989 a playwright was in prison; by the end of the year he was president. Of which country?
rewrite.why_better: The prison-to-presidency twist creates surprise and invites reasoning about which 1989 revolution was led by artists.

original.ru: Сколько спасательных шлюпок было на «Титанике»?
original.en: How many lifeboats did the Titanic carry?
original.fact: That was more than the law required: lifeboat rules went by a ship's tonnage, not by how many people it carried.

verdict: Everyone knows there were too few lifeboats, so players reason toward a small number; 'more than the law required' is a good twist.

original.ru: Какой была средняя продолжительность жизни в мире в 1900 году?
original.en: What was the average life expectancy in the world in 1900?
original.fact: The average was so low mainly because so many children died young; by the century's end it had roughly doubled.

verdict: Most will guess far higher, the number is estimable, and the child-mortality explanation turns the surprise into insight.

original.ru: Сколько этажей чаще всего было в хрущёвке?
original.en: How many storeys did a typical Khrushchyovka block have?
original.fact: Under the norms of the day, anything over five floors needed a lift, and lifts were an expense to avoid.

verdict: Instant recognition for this family, and the 'no lift above five floors' reason turns a known fact into an 'aha'.

original.ru: Сколько соток обычно давали семье под садовый участок?
original.en: How many "sotkas" (100 m² each) was a typical Soviet garden plot?
original.fact: A sotka is 100 m², so the famous "six sotkas" were just 600 m², about twenty by thirty metres.

verdict: 'Six sotkas' is a household phrase, so it is a nostalgic free point; 25 and 50 are implausible. Keep as a deliberate easy recognition question.

original.ru: Чей портрет был на октябрятской звёздочке?
original.en: Whose portrait was on the Little Octobrist star badge?
options: * Маленького Ленина | Lenin as a child
original.fact: A class of Octobrists was split into "little stars", at first of five children, one per point of the star.

verdict: A warm nostalgia question for the 40-50 group (less so for 23-year-olds); the distractors are credible Soviet icons and the five-pointed 'stars' detail is a small payoff. Fine as easy recognition.

original.ru: Сколько пассажирских авиакомпаний было в СССР?
original.en: How many passenger airlines did the USSR have?
options: 15, по одной на республику | 15, one per republic
original.fact: Aeroflot held a monopoly and was one of the world's largest airlines; it also sprayed crops and ran air ambulances.

verdict: 'Just one airline' surprises the younger players and the crop-spraying, air-ambulance Aeroflot is a good payoff; 'about fifty' is weak.

original.ru: Как попрощался олимпийский Мишка на закрытии Игр-80?
original.en: How did Misha the bear say goodbye at the 1980 Olympics closing ceremony?
options: * Улетел на воздушных шарах | Flew off on balloons
Уплыл по Москве-реке | Sailed off down the Moskva
Уехал на тройке | Rode off on a troika
Ушёл спать в берлогу | Went off to hibernate
original.fact: Just before, the crowd held up coloured cards to form a picture of Misha with a tear rolling down his cheek.

verdict: An iconic, emotional memory for the older players, and the crying-Misha card mosaic is a lovely payoff; the distractors are playful but credible.

original.ru: Сколько весила советская монета в 5 копеек образца 1961 года?
original.en: How much did a Soviet 5-kopeck coin of the 1961 type weigh?
original.fact: The 1, 2, 3 and 5 kopeck coins weighed as many grams as they were worth, so change could be counted on scales.

verdict: A coin weighing its own value is a neat 'wait, really?', the matching number gives a smart reasoning path, and the 'count change on scales' payoff is great.

original.ru: Для кого изначально создавали «Докторскую» колбасу в 1936 году?
original.en: Who was Doktorskaya sausage originally created for in 1936?
options: * Для больных и ослабленных | The sick and frail
Для врачей на дежурствах | Doctors on night shifts
Для детей в яслях | Children in nurseries
original.fact: It was meant for those "whose health was undermined by the Civil War and tsarist despotism".

verdict: Everyone knows Doktorskaya, 'for doctors on night shift' is a perfect trap, and the 'tsarist despotism' quote is a laugh.

original.ru: Как называлась главная государственная фирма грамзаписи СССР?
original.en: What was the Soviet Union's main state record label called?
original.fact: By 1973 Melodiya was pressing around 200 million records a year.

verdict: Older players know Melodiya instantly, younger ones guess from the name; the 200 million records fact is a flat payoff with no surprise.

original.ru: Сколько километров проехал по Луне «Луноход-1»?
original.en: How many kilometres did Lunokhod 1 drive on the Moon?
original.fact: It was driven from Earth via a delayed TV picture and kept going for almost 11 months instead of three.

verdict: Lunokhod is familiar, but players have nothing to estimate the distance from; the 11-month run is the clue that should be in the question.

rewrite.q_ru: «Луноход-1» колесил по Луне почти 11 месяцев. Сколько километров он проехал?
rewrite.q_en: Lunokhod 1 roamed the Moon for almost 11 months. How many kilometres did it cover?
rewrite.why_better: Knowing it drove for 11 months makes the tiny distance a real surprise and gives a basis for reasoning about speed.

original.ru: В каком году в СССР перешли на пятидневку с двумя выходными?
original.en: In what year did the USSR switch to a five-day week with two days off?
original.fact: Until then people worked six days a week, and Saturday was an ordinary working day.

verdict: A year to recall, with a dull fact; framing it around working Saturdays makes it personal for the family's elders.

rewrite.q_ru: До какого года суббота в СССР была обычным рабочим днём?
rewrite.q_en: Until what year was Saturday an ordinary working day in the USSR?
rewrite.why_better: 'Working Saturdays' is something parents and grandparents remember, so the year sparks stories instead of a date quiz.

original.ru: Кто спел «My Heart Will Go On» — главную песню «Титаника»?
original.en: Who sang My Heart Will Go On, the big song from Titanic?
original.fact: Cameron felt a pop song would be wrong for the ending, so composer James Horner waited for the right moment to play him Dion's demo.

verdict: Céline Dion is common knowledge, but the Horner-sneaking-the-demo payoff is good; keep as a deliberate easy recognition question.

original.ru: Где в 1991 году заработал первый в мире сайт?
original.en: Where did the world's first website go live in 1991?
options: * В ЦЕРН под Женевой | At CERN near Geneva
original.fact: Tim Berners-Lee invented the web so scientists could share data; in August 1991 it was opened to the whole internet.

verdict: CERN is a fair surprise vs MIT, but the MIT option is cut off in Russian ('Массачусетском технологическом' with no noun) and Microsoft is not a credible web birthplace.

rewrite.q_ru: Где в 1991 году заработал первый в мире сайт?
rewrite.q_en: Where did the world's first website go live in 1991?
options: * В ЦЕРН под Женевой | At CERN near Geneva
В Кремниевой долине | In Silicon Valley
rewrite.why_better: Fixes the broken MIT option and replaces Microsoft with Silicon Valley, the instinctive wrong guess.

original.ru: Какой чемпион мира по шахматам в 1997 году проиграл матч компьютеру IBM Deep Blue?
original.en: Which world chess champion lost a match to IBM's Deep Blue in 1997?
original.fact: A year earlier Kasparov had beaten the same machine 4-2; after losing he demanded a rematch, but IBM refused.

verdict: Kasparov is a gimme for a Russian family, but the 'won the year before, IBM refused a rematch' payoff is good; keep as easy recognition.

original.ru: Чья песня звучала в рекламе запуска Windows 95?
original.en: Whose song launched Windows 95 in the adverts?
original.fact: Start Me Up was chosen to sell the brand new Start button.

verdict: Start Me Up for the Start button is a great pun, but players do not know which song was used, so it is a band guess; give them the song title and it becomes recognition plus an 'aha'.

rewrite.q_ru: Рекламу Windows 95 и кнопки «Пуск» озвучила песня «Start Me Up». Чья она?
rewrite.q_en: Windows 95 and its Start button were launched to the song Start Me Up. Whose song is it?
rewrite.why_better: Players can now hum and reason their way to the band, and the Start/Start pun lands in the question itself.

original.ru: В какой стране в 1999 году появилось первое реалити-шоу «Большой брат»?
original.en: In which country did the first Big Brother reality show air, in 1999?
original.fact: The name comes from Orwell's novel 1984, where Big Brother watches everyone.

verdict: Most will say UK or USA, so the Netherlands is a fair surprise with excellent distractors; the Orwell fact is well known and a weak payoff.

original.ru: Какая организация в 1999 году запретила приносить на работу игрушку Furby?
original.en: Which organisation banned Furby toys from its premises in 1999?
options: * Агентство нацбезопасности США | The US National Security Agency
original.fact: They feared it would learn and repeat secrets, though Furby could not record sound at all.

verdict: The NSA banning a Furby is hilarious and the payoff (it could not record anything) is perfect; only the correct option's length gives it away.

rewrite.q_ru: Какая организация в 1999 году запретила приносить на работу игрушку Furby?
rewrite.q_en: Which organisation banned Furby toys from its premises in 1999?
options: Банк Англии | The Bank of England
rewrite.why_better: Equal-length options keep the absurd answer from being spotted by its size.

original.ru: Какой порошковый напиток рекламировали словами «Просто добавь воды!»?
original.en: Which powdered drink was sold with the slogan 'Just add water!'?
original.fact: Its creator Sergei Vykhodtsev modelled Invite on Drink-o-pop, a drink he brought back from Africa by the suitcase.

verdict: Pure nostalgia recognition: anyone who grew up in the 90s shouts 'Invite!', and Yupi and Zuko are perfect traps; younger players may struggle. The Africa-suitcase fact is a nice payoff. Keep only if re-tagged as easy recognition.

original.ru: Что называли «ножками Буша»?
original.en: What were 'Bush legs' in Russia?
options: * Американские куриные окорочка | American frozen chicken legs
Американские ковбойские сапоги | American cowboy boots
Танец из американского клипа | A dance from a US music video
Узкие американские джинсы | Skinny American jeans
original.fact: The name came from a 1990 deal for chicken supplies signed by US President George H. W. Bush.

verdict: Every Russian adult knows the phrase and it gets a laugh, though it is mostly recognition; the 1990 trade-deal fact explains the name nicely.

original.ru: Сколько посетителей обслужил первый московский «Макдоналдс» в день открытия, 31 января 1990-го?
original.en: How many customers did Moscow's first McDonald's serve on its opening day, 31 January 1990?
original.fact: With 900 seats it was the biggest McDonald's in the world, and the queue stretched for kilometres.

verdict: The legendary queue is familiar and the number is estimable from it; a great reveal. The script links it to brands_050: if that question asks the same opening-day figure, keep only one.

original.ru: Какой юбилей Москва пышно отмечала в 1997 году?
original.en: Which anniversary did Moscow celebrate in grand style in 1997?
original.fact: The count starts in 1147, when Yuri Dolgoruky wrote to an ally, 'Come to me, brother, in Moscow': the city's first mention.

verdict: Older players remember the 850th celebrations and can count from 1147, so it is close to recognition, and a tolerance of 30 makes it easy for a hard question; the 'Come to me, brother' line is the best part and sits only in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: «Приди ко мне, брате, в Москов» — первое упоминание Москвы. Какой юбилей она отмечала в 1997-м?
rewrite.q_en: 'Come to me, brother, in Moscow' is the city's first mention. Which anniversary did Moscow mark in 1997?
rewrite.why_better: The chronicle quote turns a date sum into a story, and the tighter tolerance means remembering 1147 actually pays.

original.ru: Как называлось войско Ивана Грозного, возившее у седла собачью голову и метлу?
original.en: What was Ivan the Terrible's guard called, riders with a dog's head and a broom at the saddle?
original.fact: The emblems meant 'gnaw out and sweep away treason', and the oprichniki dressed in black like monks.

verdict: Oprichniki is a school-level answer and the musketeers are absurd, but the 'gnaw out and sweep away treason' payoff is vivid. Keep as easy recognition.

original.ru: Что Пётр I обложил особым налогом, чтобы подданные выглядели по-европейски?
original.en: What did Peter the Great tax to make Russians look more European?
original.fact: Payers got a copper 'beard token'; a peasant paid a kopeck for his beard every time he entered a town.

verdict: The beard tax is well known but fun, the balalaika and samovar options are playful, and the copper beard token is a good payoff.

original.ru: Какой царь отменил крепостное право в России?
original.en: Which tsar abolished serfdom in Russia?
original.fact: His 1861 manifesto came two years before Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation freed slaves in the US.

verdict: A school-test question; the genuinely surprising angle (Russia freed serfs before the US freed slaves) is buried in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Какой царь отменил крепостное право за два года до освобождения рабов в США?
rewrite.q_en: Which tsar abolished serfdom two years before Lincoln freed the slaves in the US?
rewrite.why_better: The US comparison adds a 'wait, earlier than America?' moment to a school fact.

original.ru: Откуда пошла история о «потёмкинских деревнях» — декорациях для Екатерины II?
original.en: Where did the story of 'Potemkin villages', fake sets for Catherine the Great, come from?
options: Из мемуаров самой Екатерины | Catherine's own memoirs
Из донесения самого Потёмкина | Potemkin's own report
* Из очерков саксонского дипломата | A Saxon diplomat's writings
Из комедии Гоголя | A comedy by Gogol
original.fact: The new towns were real; the tale came from the Saxon envoy Helbig, who was not on the trip, and historians call it a myth.

verdict: A good myth-buster, but 'a comedy by Gogol' is a throwaway and the options are long and uneven.

rewrite.q_ru: Кто пустил байку о «потёмкинских деревнях» для Екатерины II?
rewrite.q_en: Who spread the tale of 'Potemkin villages' built to fool Catherine the Great?
rewrite.why_better: Shorter, balanced options; the reveal that a foreigner who was not even there invented it lands cleanly.

original.ru: Как в 1480 году закончилось ордынское иго?
original.en: How did the Horde's rule over Russia end in 1480?
options: * Войска постояли на реке и разошлись | The armies faced off and left
Куликовской битвой | With the Battle of Kulikovo
Взятием Казани | With the capture of Kazan
Мирным договором с Ордой | A peace treaty with the Horde
original.fact: This was the Great Stand on the Ugra: Khan Akhmat failed to cross the river and led his army away.

verdict: Kulikovo is a great trap, but the correct option is a descriptive sentence among named events, which telegraphs it, and the grammar does not match the question.

rewrite.q_ru: Как в 1480 году закончилось ордынское иго?
rewrite.q_en: How did the Horde's rule over Russia end in 1480?
options: * Стоянием на реке | A stand-off at a river
Куликовской битвой | The Battle of Kulikovo
Взятием Казани | The capture of Kazan
rewrite.why_better: Parallel noun-phrase options remove the tell, so players must actually remember the Ugra.

original.ru: За кого выдавал себя Емельян Пугачёв?
original.en: Who did Yemelyan Pugachev claim to be?
original.fact: Catherine's husband, who died after the 1762 coup, became the favourite mask of pretenders: there were about forty.

verdict: Peter III is a school answer from 'The Captain's Daughter'; the fun fact (about forty pretenders used his name) is hidden.

rewrite.q_ru: Пугачёв — лишь один из сорока самозванцев под этим именем. За кого он себя выдавал?
rewrite.q_en: Pugachev was just one of about forty pretenders using this name. Who did he claim to be?
rewrite.why_better: 'Forty pretenders' is a surprising hook and makes Tsarevich Dmitry (another favourite mask) an even better trap.

original.ru: Почему Москву называют «белокаменной»?
original.en: Why is Moscow called 'white-stone Moscow'?
options: Дома белили известью к праздникам | Houses were whitewashed for feasts
Город стоит на меловых горах | The city stands on chalk hills
Снег лежит там полгода | Snow lies there half the year
* Кремль когда-то был из белого камня | The Kremlin was once white stone
original.fact: Dmitry Donskoy built a white limestone Kremlin in 1367; today's red brick walls were built by Italians under Ivan III.

verdict: Good plausible distractors, but the correct option is the longest and most specific, and the question gives little to argue about.

rewrite.q_ru: Откуда у Москвы прозвище «белокаменная»?
rewrite.q_en: Why is Moscow nicknamed 'white-stone'?
options: * От белого каменного Кремля | Its white stone Kremlin
От побелённых домов | Its whitewashed houses
От меловых холмов | Its chalk hills
От долгих снежных зим | Its long snowy winters
rewrite.why_better: Balanced options mean players must weigh four sensible theories, and 'the red Kremlin was once white' lands as a surprise.

original.ru: Под каким именем Пётр I ездил по Европе с Великим посольством?
original.en: Under what name did Peter the Great travel Europe with his Grand Embassy?
options: Граф Северный | Count of the North
original.fact: A two-metre 'sergeant' was easy to spot, yet he really worked as a carpenter at a Dutch shipyard.

verdict: 'Count of the North' (Paul I's alias) is a smart trap, but 'Ivan Ivanov' is a joke option; the shipyard carpenter fact is a good payoff.

rewrite.q_ru: Под каким именем Пётр I ездил по Европе с Великим посольством?
rewrite.q_en: Under what name did Peter the Great travel Europe with his Grand Embassy?
options: Граф Северный | Count of the North
rewrite.why_better: 'Pyotr Alekseyev' (his real patronymic) is a far more tempting trap than 'Ivan Ivanov'.

original.ru: Сколько дней Наполеон пробыл в занятой Москве в 1812 году?
original.en: How many days did Napoleon stay in occupied Moscow in 1812?
original.fact: He waited for Alexander I to sue for peace, got no answer, and left as his army ran out of food.

verdict: Everyone knows Napoleon took Moscow and left; the number is estimable and the range fair, with a decent 'waited for a peace offer' payoff.

original.ru: Сколько лет, по традиционному счёту, длилось ордынское иго на Руси?
original.en: By the traditional count, how many years did the Horde's yoke over Rus last?
original.fact: It is counted from Batu's invasion of 1237–1240 to the Great Stand on the Ugra in 1480.

verdict: Subtracting 1240 from 1480 is a school arithmetic exercise with a bare-number reveal, and the Ugra is already covered by ru_history_025.

original.ru: Кто возглавил первое советское правительство — Совнарком — в 1917 году?
original.en: Who headed the first Soviet government, the Council of People's Commissars, in 1917?
original.fact: The Bolsheviks found 'minister' too bourgeois and used 'people's commissar'; ministries only came back in 1946.

verdict: Lenin is a free answer; the 'minister sounded too bourgeois' fact is a nice payoff. Keep only as a deliberate easy recognition question.

original.ru: Каким соглашением в декабре 1991 года было объявлено, что СССР прекращает существование?
original.en: Which December 1991 agreement declared that the USSR had ceased to exist?
options: Брестским миром | The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
original.fact: Leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus signed it on 8 December 1991 at a hunting lodge in the Belovezha Forest.

verdict: Belovezha is well known to this family; credible distractors and a hunting-lodge payoff. Keep as easy recognition.

original.ru: Кто стал первым президентом России?
original.en: Who was the first President of Russia?
original.fact: Yeltsin was elected by popular vote on 12 June 1991 and won outright in the first round with 57%.

verdict: Yeltsin is a gimme (Gorbachev is a decent trap) and the 57% fact is dry; keep only as a deliberate easy warm-up.

original.ru: Какое из этих слов НЕ было лозунгом Горбачёва?
original.en: Which of these was NOT one of Gorbachev's slogans?
original.fact: 'The Thaw' was the name for Khrushchev's time, taken from Ilya Ehrenburg's 1954 novel.

verdict: A satisfying recognition question: Thaw vs Perestroika slogans is fair reasoning and the Ehrenburg origin is a small payoff. Keep only if re-tagged as easy recognition.

original.ru: Чья настоящая фамилия была Скрябин?
original.en: Whose real surname was Skryabin?
original.fact: Kirov was born Kostrikov and Trotsky was born Bronstein, while Kaganovich kept his own name.

verdict: Molotov born Skryabin is surprising, but players have little to reason from; the composer link is the hook to use.

rewrite.q_ru: Кто из советских вождей родился Скрябиным, как знаменитый композитор?
rewrite.q_en: Which Soviet leader was born Skryabin, like the famous composer?
rewrite.why_better: The composer link makes the name familiar and turns a surname lookup into a funny contrast.

original.ru: Сколько конституций было у Советского Союза?
original.en: How many constitutions did the Soviet Union have?
original.fact: Those of 1924, 1936 ('Stalin's') and 1977 ('Brezhnev's'); the 1918 one belonged to Soviet Russia, before the USSR existed.

verdict: Counting constitutions is a dry exam question with a list-of-years payoff, and the RSFSR 1918 nuance invites 'it depends' arguments.

original.ru: За что в 1964 году судили поэта Иосифа Бродского?
original.en: What was the poet Joseph Brodsky convicted of in 1964?
original.fact: When the judge asked who had made him a poet, Brodsky replied: 'I think it comes from God.'

verdict: Familiar to the family, 'social parasitism' surprises the young, and Brodsky's 'from God' reply is a powerful payoff.

original.ru: По легенде, восставшие в 1825 году солдаты кричали «Константин и Конституция!». Кем они считали Конституцию?
original.en: Legend says the rebel soldiers of 1825 cried 'Constantine and Constitution!'. Who did they think Constitution was?
original.fact: It is most likely just a legend, but it shows how new and strange the word 'constitution' was to most people.

verdict: The 'Constitution was Constantine's wife' legend is hilarious and guessable, but the question is over 100 characters.

rewrite.q_ru: В 1825 году солдаты кричали «Константин и Конституция!». Кем, по легенде, они считали Конституцию?
rewrite.q_en: In 1825 soldiers shouted 'Constantine and Constitution!'. Who, legend says, did they think Constitution was?
rewrite.why_better: Same joke, shorter setup, so it reads in time.

original.ru: В каком году столицу перенесли из Петрограда в Москву?
original.en: In which year was the capital moved from Petrograd to Moscow?
original.fact: The government moved almost in secret in March 1918, fearing German troops could reach Petrograd.

verdict: 1918 is close to common knowledge and the tolerance of 8 makes it easy; the 'moved almost in secret, fearing the Germans' story is the better hook.

rewrite.q_ru: Боясь немцев, правительство тайком переехало из Петрограда в Москву. В каком году?
rewrite.q_en: Fearing the Germans, the government quietly moved from Petrograd to Moscow. In which year?
rewrite.why_better: The secret flight is a better story, and the tighter tolerance makes knowing the year actually count.

original.ru: Сколько миллионов членов было в КПСС в конце 1980-х?
original.en: How many million members did the Soviet Communist Party have in the late 1980s?
original.fact: That was roughly one adult in ten: without a party card many careers simply went nowhere.

verdict: An estimable number for those who lived it, but the framing is dry and the tolerance of 7 on a 1-60 range is generous.

rewrite.q_ru: Без партбилета карьера не складывалась. Сколько миллионов членов было в КПСС в конце 1980-х?
rewrite.q_en: Without a party card careers stalled. How many million members did the Soviet Communist Party have in the late 1980s?
rewrite.why_better: The 'party card' hook prompts memories and arguments, and a tighter tolerance rewards the ones who remember.

original.ru: На что баварский король Людвиг II потратил своё состояние?
original.en: What did King Ludwig II of Bavaria spend his fortune on?
options: * На сказочные замки | Fairy tale castles
original.fact: Within weeks of the king's mysterious death, Neuschwanstein was opened to paying visitors.

verdict: Repeats landmarks_014 (Neuschwanstein, opened to tourists weeks after his death) almost word for word, and 'fairy tale castles' is obvious to anyone who just saw that question.

original.ru: Как прозвали французского короля Людовика XIV?
original.en: What was Louis XIV of France nicknamed?
original.fact: At 14 he danced Apollo in the Royal Ballet of the Night, rising like the sun, and the image stayed with him for life.

verdict: The Sun King is common knowledge (the Lion King option gets a smile); the ballet origin is a good payoff. Keep as easy recognition.

original.ru: В память о ком император Шах-Джахан построил Тадж-Махал?
original.en: In memory of whom did the emperor Shah Jahan build the Taj Mahal?
options: О любимом слоне | His favourite elephant
original.fact: Mumtaz Mahal died giving birth to their 14th child, and her tomb took 22 years to build.

verdict: A known story with a fun elephant option, and the 14th child plus 22 years of building is a strong payoff.

original.ru: Что случилось, когда правитель Мали Манса Муса проехал через Каир?
original.en: What happened when Mansa Musa, ruler of Mali, passed through Cairo?
options: * Золото в Каире подешевело | Gold lost value in Cairo
В городе кончилась вода | The city ran out of water
Город сдался без боя | The city surrendered
Его не пустили в город | He was refused entry
original.fact: According to the historian al-Umari, he handed out so much gold in 1324 that it stayed cheaper there for 12 years.

verdict: Gold getting cheaper because one man spent too much is a wonderful 'wait, seriously?', and it is guessable from Mansa Musa's wealth. It repeats medieval_023 (and money_027): keep this version, drop the other.

original.ru: Каким ремеслом увлекался Людовик XVI?
original.en: Which craft was Louis XVI's hobby?
original.fact: The king had his own workshop at Versailles, where he loved to make locks.

verdict: A locksmith king is a fun irony, but the options are mixed crafts and the payoff ('he loved to make locks') just restates the answer.

rewrite.q_ru: Что Людовик XVI любил мастерить в своей мастерской в Версале?
rewrite.q_en: What did Louis XVI love to make in his own workshop at Versailles?
rewrite.why_better: Concrete objects make the picture of a king at a workbench vivid, so the locks answer gets a bigger smile.

original.ru: Что означает прозвище римского императора Калигулы?
original.en: What does the Roman emperor Caligula's nickname mean?
original.fact: As a small boy he lived in his father's army camps, dressed by his mother in a mini soldier's outfit with tiny boots, caligae.

verdict: 'Little boot' for a tyrant is a delightful contrast, the animal-cub distractors are credible, and the toddler-in-uniform payoff is charming.

original.ru: Какое насекомое Наполеон выбрал символом своей империи?
original.en: Which insect did Napoleon choose as a symbol of his empire?
original.fact: Golden bees were found in the Frankish king Childeric's tomb, linking Napoleon to France's first kings.

verdict: Bees are a surprising choice for Napoleon, the other insects are credible, and the Childeric tomb link is a satisfying explanation.

original.ru: Как провёл последние годы Шах-Джахан, построивший Тадж-Махал?
original.en: How did Shah Jahan, who built the Taj Mahal, spend his last years?
options: В путешествиях по Европе | Travelling in Europe
Монахом в горах | As a monk in the mountains
В изгнании в Персии | In exile in Persia
* Узником собственного сына | As his own son's prisoner
original.fact: His son Aurangzeb locked him in Agra Fort, from where the old emperor could gaze at the Taj Mahal.

verdict: A tragic twist (the Taj Mahal builder imprisoned by his own son, gazing at it) gets a real reaction; the correct option is slightly the longest.

original.ru: Сколько внуков было у королевы Виктории?
original.en: How many grandchildren did Queen Victoria have?
original.fact: Her grandchildren included the German Kaiser, the last Russian empress and queens of Spain, Norway, Romania and Greece.

verdict: Players know she had many children and can reason up to about 40, and 'the grandmother of Europe' payoff is great.

original.ru: Каким по счёту сыном Рамсеса II был фараон Мернептах, унаследовавший его трон?
original.en: Merneptah inherited Ramesses II's throne. What number son was he?
original.fact: Ramesses II reigned for 66 years and lived into his nineties, outliving twelve older sons.

verdict: Merneptah is unknown and his birth order cannot be estimated; the fun part (Ramesses outlived twelve sons) needs another framing. The unit field is also empty (' | ').

original.ru: «Эффект Манделы» назван так, потому что многие «помнили», будто Нельсон Мандела…
original.en: The 'Mandela effect' got its name because many people 'remembered' that Nelson Mandela…
options: был американским пастором | was an American pastor
жил в изгнании в Париже | lived in exile in Paris
никогда не сидел в тюрьме | was never in prison
* умер в тюрьме в 1980-х | died in prison in the 1980s
original.fact: Fiona Broome found hundreds shared her 'memory'; in fact Mandela was freed in 1990, became president and died in 2013.

verdict: The Mandela effect is well known and the 'died in prison' false memory is a satisfying reveal, with a cheeky 'never in prison' option.

original.ru: Для чего на самом деле в 1955 году построили «Зону 51»?
original.en: What was Area 51 actually built for in 1955?
options: Прятать летающую тарелку | To hide a flying saucer
* Испытывать самолёт-шпион U-2 | To test the U-2 spy plane
Укрыть президента от войны | To shelter the president
original.fact: The U-2 flew above 18 km, and airline pilots who saw its silver wings glint at sunset reported UFOs.

verdict: The flying-saucer option tempts, the U-2 is a good reveal, and 'pilots reported its glinting wings as UFOs' is a perfect payoff.

original.ru: Какого режиссёра конспирологи обвиняют в том, что он снял высадку на Луну в павильоне?
original.en: Which film director do Moon hoax believers say staged the landing in a studio?
original.fact: The rumour feeds on his 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968), yet observatories still bounce lasers off mirrors Apollo left on the Moon.

verdict: Kubrick is the famous answer and the other directors are credible; the laser mirrors on the Moon fact is a strong rebuttal payoff.

original.ru: Как критики прозвали пулю, которая, по официальной версии, ранила и Кеннеди, и губернатора Коннэлли?
original.en: What did critics nickname the bullet that, officially, hit both Kennedy and Governor Connally?
original.fact: Its path looked impossible, but Connally sat lower and further inboard, and reconstructions showed the path was possible.

verdict: 'Magic bullet' is a name lookup with no surprise, the other metals are filler, and the ballistics explanation is technical.

original.ru: Какой знаменитый учёный был уверен, что пьесы Шекспира написал граф Оксфорд?
original.en: Which famous scientist was convinced the Earl of Oxford wrote Shakespeare's plays?
original.fact: Freud was won over by a 1920 book by J. Thomas Looney; yes, that really was the author's name.

verdict: Freud as an Oxfordian is a genuine surprise, and the author literally named Looney is a perfect payoff (it lands best in English; the Russian fact explains it).

original.ru: Чьё существование отрицает «гипотеза фантомного времени» Хериберта Илига?
original.en: Whose existence does Heribert Illig's 'phantom time hypothesis' deny?
original.fact: Illig declared a whole era fake, yet Charlemagne left coins, charters, letters and a biography by a man of his court.

verdict: The theory is fun, but naming Heribert Illig hides it behind an unknown name, and Julius Caesar is not even medieval.

rewrite.q_ru: По одной теории, 300 лет Средневековья выдуманы, а с ними и знаменитый правитель. Кто?
rewrite.q_en: One theory says 300 years of the Middle Ages were invented, along with a famous ruler. Who?
options: Ричард Львиное Сердце | Richard the Lionheart
rewrite.why_better: Leading with the outrageous claim instead of an unknown theorist makes it a 'wait, seriously?', and four medieval rulers make players reason about dates.

original.ru: Через какие пояса, по словам конспирологов, экипажи «Аполлонов» не пролетели бы живыми из-за радиации?
original.en: Which belts, hoaxers say, would have killed Apollo crews with radiation?
options: * Пояса Ван Аллена | The Van Allen belts
original.fact: The ships crossed the belts in a couple of hours, and the average crew dose was what we get on Earth in about three years.

verdict: The Kuiper and asteroid belts are credible traps and Orion's Belt is a joke, but the question is over 100 characters and the answer is a technical name.

rewrite.q_ru: Какие пояса, по словам конспирологов, «Аполлоны» не пролетели бы живыми из-за радиации?
rewrite.q_en: Which belts, say hoaxers, would have killed the Apollo crews with radiation?
options: * Пояса Ван Аллена | The Van Allen belts
rewrite.why_better: Shorter and readable in time; the content is unchanged.

original.ru: Физик Дэвид Граймс подсчитал, через сколько раскрылась бы подделка высадки на Луну. Его ответ?
original.en: Physicist David Grimes worked out how soon a faked Moon landing would leak. His answer?
options: * Меньше чем через 4 года | In under 4 years
original.fact: In 2016 he modelled leaks among hundreds of thousands of NASA staff and got about 3.7 years: a secret that big can't hold.

verdict: A fun scientific twist on the moon hoax with an interesting payoff; 'under 4 years' is more specific than the round distractors.

rewrite.q_ru: Физик Дэвид Граймс подсчитал, через сколько раскрылась бы подделка высадки на Луну. Его ответ?
rewrite.q_en: Physicist David Grimes worked out how soon a faked Moon landing would leak. His answer?
options: * Примерно через 4 года | In about 4 years
Примерно через 40 лет | In about 40 years
Примерно через 400 лет | In about 400 years
Не раскрылась бы никогда | It would never leak
rewrite.why_better: Parallel 'about N' options remove the specificity tell.

original.ru: Плоскоземельцы купили лазерный гироскоп за 20 тысяч долларов. Сколько градусов в час он показал?
original.en: Flat-earthers bought a $20,000 laser gyroscope. What rotation, in degrees per hour, did it detect?
original.fact: Exactly Earth's spin, 360° in 24 hours; it was caught on camera in the 2018 documentary Behind the Curve.

verdict: Flat-earthers' own gyroscope proving the Earth spins gets a big laugh, and 360/24 gives a satisfying reasoning path.

original.ru: Сколько лет истории, по Хериберту Илигу, придумали и вписали в Средневековье?
original.en: How many years of history does Heribert Illig say were invented and slipped into the Middle Ages?
original.fact: Illig says 614 to 911 never happened; eclipse records, coins and thousands of documents from those years say otherwise.

verdict: Same as the calibration anchor: an unknown theorist and a number nobody can estimate; it also repeats the phantom-time theory of conspiracy_020.

original.ru: Куда направлена главная ось Стоунхенджа?
original.en: What is the main axis of Stonehenge lined up with?
options: * На восход в день летнего солнцестояния | Sunrise on the summer solstice
На Полярную звезду | The North Star
На восход полной Луны в марте | The full Moon rising in March
На вершину Бен-Невиса | The peak of Ben Nevis
original.fact: The other way it faces midwinter sunset, which may have mattered even more to its builders.

verdict: Solstice is a known answer, and the correct option is by far the longest and most specific; the 'midwinter sunset may matter more' twist is the better story.

rewrite.q_ru: Куда смотрит главная ось Стоунхенджа?
rewrite.q_en: What is the main axis of Stonehenge lined up with?
options: На Полярную звезду | The North Star
rewrite.why_better: Short balanced options with a summer-vs-winter trap make players think, and the reveal's sunset twist fits the trap.

original.ru: Чью могилу так и не нашли, хотя её ищут даже со спутников?
original.en: Whose grave has never been found, even with satellite searches?
original.fact: Legend says horses trampled the burial site flat, and many Mongolians feel it should never be disturbed.

verdict: A familiar mystery with a vivid payoff (horses trampling the grave), though Napoleon's and Peter's graves are well known, which makes it an easy elimination.

original.ru: Где в 2012 году нашли останки английского короля Ричарда III?
original.en: Where were the remains of England's King Richard III found in 2012?
options: * Под парковкой | Under a car park
В Темзе | In the River Thames
Под футбольным полем | Under a football pitch
В подвале Тауэра | In the Tower's cellar
original.fact: The car park stood on a lost friary church; in 2015 he was reburied in Leicester Cathedral.

verdict: 'Under a car park' is a brilliant, absurd and true answer that gets a laugh; strong.

original.ru: Какое первое слово прочли в 2023 году в сгоревшем свитке из Геркуланума?
original.en: What was the first word read in 2023 from a charred scroll from Herculaneum?
original.fact: The scroll was charred by Vesuvius in AD 79; a student read the word by training an AI on CT scans of it.

verdict: Reading a charred scroll with AI is a great story, but the first word is random, so the question is a coin toss; rebuild it around how the word was read.

original.ru: Как власти Страсбурга сначала «лечили» танцевальную чуму 1518 года?
original.en: How did the authorities of Strasbourg first try to cure the dancing plague of 1518?
options: * Наняли музыкантов для танцоров | Hired musicians to keep them dancing
Обливали людей холодной водой | Doused the dancers in cold water
Закрыли городские ворота | Locked the city gates
original.fact: They thought the dancers had to dance it out and built a stage; today it is seen as mass hysteria in a famine year.

verdict: Hiring musicians to cure a dancing plague is absurd and true; the reveal gets a laugh and the 'built a stage' detail is a great payoff.

original.ru: Какое реальное бедствие часто называют прообразом гибели Атлантиды?
original.en: Which real disaster is often named as the inspiration for the sinking of Atlantis?
options: * Извержение вулкана на Санторини | The eruption on Santorini
Гибель Помпей | The destruction of Pompeii
Извержение Кракатау | The eruption of Krakatoa
original.fact: The blast around 1600 BC buried the town of Akrotiri under ash and sent tsunamis onto the coast of Crete.

verdict: A fair 'real Atlantis' question, but Pompeii and Lisbon are easy to rule out and the reveal is mild.

rewrite.q_ru: Какое реальное бедствие часто называют прообразом гибели Атлантиды?
rewrite.q_en: Which real disaster is often named as the inspiration for the sinking of Atlantis?
options: * Взрыв вулкана Санторини | The Santorini eruption
Извержение Везувия | The eruption of Vesuvius
Извержение Этны | The eruption of Etna
Извержение Кракатау | The eruption of Krakatoa
rewrite.why_better: Four volcanoes make players reason (Plato wrote before Vesuvius and Krakatoa erupted), a real deduction path.

original.ru: Что на самом деле издало загадочный подводный звук «Блуп», записанный в 1997 году?
original.en: What was really behind the mysterious underwater sound called the Bloop, recorded in 1997?
