original.fact: Sensors nearly 5,000 km apart picked it up; matching sounds were later recorded in Antarctic waters as icebergs broke up.

verdict: The Bloop has internet fame and the Cthulhu option is a fun laugh, but most players have never heard of it and the question is a bit long.

rewrite.q_ru: В 1997 году датчики в океане записали загадочный звук «Блуп». Что его издало?
rewrite.q_en: In 1997 ocean sensors recorded a mysterious sound, the Bloop. What made it?
rewrite.why_better: Simpler phrasing and parallel options; the monster-vs-ice contrast stays.

original.ru: Что говорят о Бермудском треугольнике страховщики «Ллойдс» и береговая охрана США?
original.en: What do Lloyd's insurers and the US Coast Guard say about the Bermuda Triangle?
options: * Он не опаснее других морей | It is no worse than other seas
Страховка там вдвое дороже | Insurance there costs double
Там отказывают компасы | Compasses fail there
Суда обязаны его обходить | Ships must sail around it
original.fact: It is a busy sea with hurricanes and the Gulf Stream; ships do not vanish there more often than elsewhere.

verdict: Everyone knows the Bermuda Triangle legend, and 'insurers say it is no worse than anywhere' is a satisfying myth-buster.

original.ru: Сколько страниц в рукописи Войнича?
original.en: How many pages does the Voynich manuscript have?
original.fact: Some leaves are lost; the rest show plants nobody can identify, star charts and bathing women.

verdict: The Voynich manuscript is half-known at best and its page count is an arbitrary number with no estimation path or payoff.

original.ru: Сколько бронзовых шестерёнок сохранилось в Антикитерском механизме — древнегреческом «компьютере»?
original.en: How many bronze gears survive in the Antikythera mechanism, the ancient Greek computer?
original.fact: Found in a shipwreck in 1901, it predicted eclipses; nothing as complex was built for over a thousand years.

verdict: The Antikythera mechanism is fascinating, but the count of surviving gears is an arbitrary number; the 'computer of antiquity' angle deserves another question.

original.ru: За что в итоге посадили гангстера Аль Капоне?
original.en: What was gangster Al Capone finally jailed for?
options: За кражу картины | Stealing a painting
original.fact: Nothing else could be proved, so in 1931 he got 11 years for not paying his taxes.

verdict: The tax-evasion answer is widely known but still satisfying; keep as easy recognition.

original.ru: Откуда родом Эркюль Пуаро?
original.en: Where does Hercule Poirot come from?
original.fact: Poirot is the only fictional character ever given an obituary on the front page of The New York Times.

verdict: Belgium vs France is the perfect trap (Poirot's annoyance at being called French), and the NYT front-page obituary is a superb payoff.

original.ru: Сколько сравнительно честных способов отъёма денег знал Остап Бендер?
original.en: How many relatively honest ways of taking people's money did Ostap Bender know?
original.fact: Ilf and Petrov drew lots on whether Bender survived the first novel, then brought him back in the second.

verdict: A beloved quote for this family that people will shout out; the drawn-lots fact is a good payoff. Keep as recognition.

original.ru: Пилтдаунский человек, «недостающее звено» из Англии (1912), оказался подделкой. Из чего его собрали?
original.en: Piltdown Man, a 1912 'missing link' found in England, was a fake. What was it made of?
options: Череп гориллы и кости овцы | Gorilla skull, sheep bones
* Череп человека и челюсть орангутана | Human skull, orangutan jaw
Гипс и дерево | Plaster and wood
original.fact: The bones were stained to look old and the teeth filed down; the fake was only exposed in 1953.

verdict: Human plus ape is the natural guess for a 'missing link', so the answer is not surprising, and 'bear bones' is vague filler.

rewrite.q_ru: Пилтдаунский человек (1912) оказался подделкой. Из чего его собрали?
rewrite.q_en: Piltdown Man (1912) turned out to be a fake. What was it made from?
options: * Человек и орангутан | A human and an orangutan
Горилла и овца | A gorilla and a sheep
Неандерталец и медведь | A Neanderthal and a bear
Гипс и дерево | Plaster and wood
rewrite.why_better: Shorter question and parallel 'X and Y' options make each choice a credible forgery recipe.

original.ru: Какой знаменитой фразы НЕТ ни в одном рассказе Конан Дойла о Холмсе?
original.en: Which famous line never appears in Conan Doyle's Holmes stories?
options: «Вы были в Афганистане» | 'You have been in Afghanistan'
original.fact: Holmes says 'Elementary' and 'my dear Watson', but the full line was born later, in plays, parodies and films.

verdict: Most players 'know' the line, especially from the Soviet Holmes films, so learning Doyle never wrote it is a real surprise; the real quotes are clever distractors.

original.ru: Зачем голландец Хан ван Мегерен в 1945 году писал «Вермеера» на глазах у свидетелей?
original.en: Why did Dutchman Han van Meegeren paint a 'Vermeer' in front of witnesses in 1945?
options: Сдать экзамен в академию | To pass an art academy exam
* Доказать, что он фальсификатор | To prove he was a forger
Для съёмок фильма | For a film shoot
По заказу королевы | On the Queen's orders
original.fact: He was charged with selling a national treasure to Göring, a capital crime; proving it a fake saved him.

verdict: A forger proving his guilt to escape a treason charge is a wonderful twist with a strong payoff.

original.ru: Откуда бежал Анри Шарьер по прозвищу «Мотылёк» (Papillon)?
original.en: Where did Henri Charrière, 'Papillon', escape from?
options: С каторги в Австралии | A penal colony in Australia
С каторги на Сахалине | A penal colony on Sakhalin
Из тюрьмы на Корсике | A prison on Corsica
* С каторги во Французской Гвиане | A penal colony in French Guiana
original.fact: His memoir became a bestseller, but researchers think many of its adventures were borrowed from other convicts.

verdict: Papillon is familiar to the older group, but the correct option is the longest and the 'French' name hints at French Guiana; Sakhalin is a token Russian option.

rewrite.q_ru: Откуда бежал Анри Шарьер по прозвищу «Мотылёк» (Papillon)?
rewrite.q_en: Where did Henri Charrière, 'Papillon', escape from?
rewrite.why_better: New Caledonia, another French penal colony, is a much stronger trap, and shorter options remove the length tell.

original.ru: На чём якобы зарабатывал Чарльз Понци в 1920 году?
original.en: What did Charles Ponzi claim his 1920 profits came from?
options: На акциях железных дорог | Railway shares
* На почтовых купонах | Postal reply coupons
original.fact: Coupons bought cheaply in Italy could be swapped for pricier US stamps: a real profit, but a tiny one.

verdict: Postal coupons are a surprising engine for the original Ponzi scheme, and the tulip option is a nice wink at money_013.

original.ru: На сколько лет осудили Берни Мейдоффа в 2009 году за крупнейшую известную финансовую пирамиду?
original.en: How many years in prison did Bernie Madoff get in 2009 for the largest known Ponzi scheme?
original.fact: The sentence was symbolic: he died in prison in 2021, having served about 12 years.

verdict: 150 years is absurd and fun, but the range of 0-1000 gives little to reason from.

rewrite.q_ru: Мейдофф построил крупнейшую финансовую пирамиду. Сколько лет тюрьмы дал ему суд в 2009-м?
rewrite.q_en: Madoff ran the biggest known Ponzi scheme. How many years in prison did the court give him in 2009?
rewrite.why_better: A tighter range and the 'biggest ever' hook push players toward absurdly long sentences and a satisfying reveal.

original.ru: Сколько золотых слитков унесли грабители со склада Brink's-Mat у Хитроу в 1983 году?
original.en: How many gold bars did robbers take from the Brink's-Mat warehouse at Heathrow in 1983?
original.fact: About three tonnes of gold, when the robbers expected around £1 million in Spanish pesetas.

verdict: The number of bars is unguessable without knowing bar weight; the fun part (they expected cash and found three tonnes of gold) needs a different question.
fact_check_note: Not certain of the detail that the robbers expected 'about £1 million in Spanish pesetas'; my recollection is that they expected around £3 million in cash. Check before reusing the fact.
lead_check: Lead check (web): Wikipedia (the cited source) says they expected about £1 million in pesetas; other accounts say about £3 million in cash. Safer fact wording: "they expected cash, not gold".

original.ru: Какую часть мозга человек на самом деле использует?
original.en: How much of the brain does a person really use?
options: * Практически весь | Practically all of it
original.fact: Scans show every part of the brain at work over a day, and damage to almost any area causes problems.

verdict: The 10% myth is the whole point, but "на самом деле" tells everyone it is a myth, so "practically all" is a gimme; "exactly half" is a throwaway.

rewrite.q_ru: Какую часть своего мозга использует человек?
rewrite.q_en: How much of their brain does a person use?
options: * Почти весь | Nearly all of it
rewrite.why_better: Without "really" the famous 10% myth becomes a genuine trap instead of a signpost to the answer.

original.ru: Какого цвета кровь в венах человека?
original.en: What colour is the blood in human veins?
original.fact: Veins only look blue through skin, because of how skin scatters light and how the eye judges colour. Blood is always red.

verdict: Well-known myth bust; "Синяя" and "Голубая" are the same answer twice and the only red option stands alone.

rewrite.q_ru: Какого цвета кровь в венах человека?
rewrite.q_en: What colour is the blood in human veins?
rewrite.why_better: Removes the duplicate blue pair and gives the trap the same "dark" wording, so the answer no longer stands alone.

original.ru: Как дикобраз защищается иглами?
original.en: How does a porcupine use its quills?
options: Стреляет ими во врага | It shoots them at enemies
* Они отрываются и застревают | They come loose and stick in
Впрыскивает ими яд | It injects venom with them
Роет ими нору | It digs its burrow with them
original.fact: The quills come out easily and have tiny barbs, so a predator leaves with a face full of them.

verdict: Good myth trap ("it shoots them"), but the correct option switches subject to "Они", which grammatically singles it out.

rewrite.q_ru: Как дикобраз защищается иглами?
rewrite.q_en: How does a porcupine use its quills?
options: Стреляет ими во врага | It shoots them at enemies
* Оставляет их в обидчике | It leaves them stuck in the attacker
Впрыскивает ими яд | It injects venom with them
Роет ими нору | It digs its burrow with them
rewrite.why_better: All four options now share the same verb-first form, so only knowledge or the myth decides.

original.ru: Почему старинные оконные стёкла часто толще внизу?
original.en: Why is old window glass often thicker at the bottom?
options: Стекло веками стекало вниз | The glass flowed down over centuries
* Их делали неровными | Panes were made uneven
Низ укрепляли от ветра | The bottom was thickened for wind
Нарос иней и не сошёл | Frost built up and stayed
original.fact: Glass does not flow at room temperature. Uneven panes were simply more often set thick edge down.

verdict: Strong myth bust: "glass flows" is a believable trap and the plain truth is a nice anticlimax.

original.ru: Что показали слепые опыты про сахар и поведение детей?
original.en: What did blind trials find about sugar and children's behaviour?
options: Сахар делает их гиперактивными | Sugar makes them hyperactive
Так действует только шоколад | Only chocolate does that
Сахар их успокаивает | Sugar calms them down
* Разницы с пустышкой нет | No difference from a placebo
original.fact: Yet mothers told their son had eaten sugar rated him as wilder, though every child had only had sweetener.

verdict: Everyone believes the sugar rush; the placebo result and the mothers who imagined wilder sons make a great reveal. "Only chocolate" is a little weak.

original.ru: Чем в основном питаются ежи?
original.en: What do hedgehogs mostly eat?
options: Яблоками и грушами | Apples and pears
* Насекомыми, червями, слизнями | Insects, worms and slugs
original.fact: The hedgehog carrying fruit on its spines goes back to Pliny the Elder, almost 2,000 years ago: his gathered grapes.

verdict: Cartoon hedgehogs with apples make a perfect trap for a Russian family, but the correct option is the only three-item list and much longer.

rewrite.q_ru: Чем в основном питаются ежи?
rewrite.q_en: What do hedgehogs mostly eat?
options: Яблоками и грушами | Apples and pears
Грибами и ягодами | Mushrooms and berries
* Жуками и червями | Beetles and worms
Орехами и семенами | Nuts and seeds
rewrite.why_better: Every option is now a two-item pair of similar length, so the apples stay a pure trap.

original.ru: Правда ли, что Санта-Клауса одела в красное «Кока-Кола»?
original.en: Did Coca-Cola dress Santa Claus in red?
options: Да, в рекламе 1931 года | Yes, in its 1931 ads
* Нет, красный Санта был раньше | No, red Santas came earlier
Да, в телерекламе 1950-х | Yes, in 1950s TV ads
Нет, до 1990-х он был зелёным | No, he was green until the 1990s
original.fact: The 1931 ads made the jolly plump Santa famous, but magazines drew him in a red coat decades earlier.

verdict: A famous "fact" that turns out false; the 1931 ad option is a strong trap and the reveal sparks discussion.

original.ru: За что Эйнштейн получил Нобелевскую премию?
original.en: What did Einstein win his Nobel Prize for?
options: За теорию относительности | The theory of relativity
* За объяснение фотоэффекта | Explaining the photoelectric effect
За формулу E = mc² | The formula E = mc²
За атомную бомбу | The atomic bomb
original.fact: Relativity still seemed too controversial to the committee, so the 1921 prize went for his work on light.

verdict: Relativity and E=mc² are perfect traps and the "too controversial" reason is a good payoff; the "similar to people_029" flag is only the Nobel formula, not a repeated fact.

original.ru: Цезарь появился на свет вовсе не кесаревым сечением. Сколько лет после его рождения прожила его мать?
original.en: Caesar was not born by C-section. How many years did his mother live after his birth?
original.fact: Back then only dying mothers were cut open, yet Aurelia lived until 54 BC and saw her son become a great general.

verdict: Nice myth (Caesar not born by C-section), but the text is over 100 characters with a NOT framing and 46 years cannot be estimated on a 0-150 slider.

rewrite.q_ru: Цезарь вряд ли родился кесаревым: его мать выжила. Сколько лет она прожила после родов?
rewrite.q_en: Caesar was hardly born by C-section: his mother survived. How many years did she live after his birth?
rewrite.why_better: Positive framing, shorter text and a tighter range let players reason from "she lived to see him famous".

original.ru: Алмазы — не сжатый уголь. На какой глубине в км образовалось большинство из них?
original.en: Diamonds are not squeezed coal. At what depth in km did most of them form?
original.fact: Most diamonds are older than the first land plants, so they cannot come from coal: they formed in the mantle 150 to 250 km down.

verdict: The coal myth and "older than land plants" are good, but a depth in km from 0 to 1000 has no everyday anchor to estimate from.

rewrite.q_ru: Алмазы — не сжатый уголь. Марианская впадина — 11 км. На какой глубине в км рождаются алмазы?
rewrite.q_en: Diamonds are not squeezed coal. The Mariana Trench is 11 km deep. At what depth in km do most diamonds form?
rewrite.why_better: A familiar depth gives players a yardstick, so the surprise is "far deeper than anything I know".

original.ru: Что мы на самом деле задеваем, когда ударяемся локтем и «бьёт током»?
original.en: What are you really hitting when you bang your elbow and feel an electric jolt?
original.fact: The ulnar nerve runs right under the skin there, with no muscle or fat to shield it.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition: most people sense it is a nerve; the fact adds little. Fine as a warm-up.

original.ru: Сколько зубов у взрослого человека, если выросли все до одного?
original.en: How many teeth does an adult have once every one has grown in?
original.fact: Children have 20 milk teeth; the last four adult ones are wisdom teeth, which come at 17 to 25 or never at all.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition question; 32 is widely known, so no surprise. Acceptable warm-up only.

original.ru: Сколько костей в скелете взрослого человека?
original.en: How many bones are in an adult human skeleton?
original.fact: Over half are in the hands and feet: 27 in each hand and 26 in each foot.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition: 206 is school knowledge and the x06 pattern helps; the hands-and-feet fact is a decent payoff.

original.ru: Одинаковые ли отпечатки пальцев у однояйцевых близнецов?
original.en: Do identical twins have the same fingerprints?
options: Да, точь-в-точь | Yes, exactly the same
Совпадают только большие пальцы | Only the thumbs match
Да, но только до 10 лет | Yes, but only until age 10
original.fact: The pattern forms in the womb and depends on tiny differences around each finger, so twins' prints are similar but never the same.

verdict: Relatable question with a believable trap ("identical twins, identical prints"); solid if not stunning.

original.ru: Какое лёгкое у человека больше?
original.en: Which of your lungs is bigger?
options: Они одинаковые | They are the same
Зависит от того, правша ли ты | Depends if you are right handed
original.fact: The left lung makes room for the heart, so it has two lobes while the right has three.

verdict: Answerable by reasoning about where the heart sits; mild surprise, clean options.

original.ru: В какое время суток человек выше всего ростом?
original.en: At what time of day are you tallest?
options: Рост весь день одинаковый | The same all day
original.fact: During the day the discs in your spine squash down, so by evening you are about 1.5 cm shorter.

verdict: Relatable and surprising; players will want to measure themselves tonight.

original.ru: Где находится самая маленькая кость человека?
original.en: Where is the smallest bone in the human body?
options: В мизинце ноги | In the little toe
В пальце руки | In a finger
original.fact: The stirrup in the middle ear is about 3 mm long, smaller than a grain of rice, and passes sound on.

verdict: Textbook fact most adults remember from school (the stirrup in the ear); little surprise and the reveal is just a size.

original.ru: Какой длины ДНК из одной клетки человека, если её размотать?
original.en: How long is the DNA from one human cell when unwound?
original.fact: It is packed into a nucleus under a hundredth of a millimetre wide, like 20 km of thread in a tennis ball.

verdict: Two metres of DNA per cell is a real "wait, seriously?", and the order-of-magnitude options make a good guess.

original.ru: Сколько у человека генов, в которых записаны белки?
original.en: How many protein-coding genes does a human have?
original.fact: Scientists expected 50,000 to 140,000; we have about as many as a worm one millimetre long.

verdict: The worm comparison is a great payoff, but a gene count from 0 to 200,000 gives nothing to reason from.

rewrite.q_ru: Учёные ждали у человека 50–140 тысяч генов белков. Сколько оказалось на самом деле?
rewrite.q_en: Scientists expected humans to have 50,000 to 140,000 protein-coding genes. How many are there really?
rewrite.why_better: The expectation gives an anchor and sets up the "far fewer than we thought" surprise.

original.ru: Сколько раз за день, пока не спит, моргает человек?
original.en: How many times does a person blink in a waking day?
original.fact: That is 15 to 20 times a minute; at a screen we blink several times less, hence dry, tired eyes.

verdict: Estimable from blinks per minute, fair range, and the screen tip is useful.

original.ru: Красно-белый столб у парикмахерской напоминает о прежнем втором ремесле цирюльников. Каком?
original.en: A barber's red and white pole recalls the barbers' old second trade. Which?
original.fact: Barbers let blood and did small operations; the stripes, the popular story goes, are blood and bandages.

verdict: Bloodletting is a fun surprise, but distractors like "sewing flags" are random rather than tempting.

rewrite.q_ru: Красно-белый столб у парикмахерской напоминает о втором ремесле цирюльников. Каком?
rewrite.q_en: A barber's red and white pole recalls the barbers' old second trade. Which?
rewrite.why_better: A plausible red-and-white trade (dyeing cloth) replaces house painting, and the question is a little shorter.

original.ru: Что клали в клюв маски чумного доктора?
original.en: What was put inside the beak of a plague doctor's mask?
original.fact: Plague was blamed on bad air. And the costume itself dates from the 1600s, not the Middle Ages.

verdict: Iconic costume, guessable from "bad air", and the 17th-century twist is a good payoff; the correct option is longer than the one-word distractors.

rewrite.q_ru: Что клали в клюв маски чумного доктора?
rewrite.q_en: What was put inside the beak of a plague doctor's mask?
rewrite.why_better: Two-word options of equal weight remove the length tell.

original.ru: Нехватка какого витамина вызывает цингу, бич моряков?
original.en: Lack of which vitamin causes scurvy, the curse of sailors?
original.fact: Most animals make vitamin C themselves, but humans, like guinea pigs, lost the knack.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition question; the guinea pig fact rescues the reveal a little.

original.ru: Что Игнац Земмельвейс в 1847 году потребовал от врачей роддома?
original.en: What did Ignaz Semmelweis demand of maternity doctors in 1847?
options: * Мыть руки хлоркой | Wash hands in chlorine
Не пить кофе | Stop drinking coffee
original.fact: Deaths of mothers plunged, but colleagues mocked him: the idea that a doctor's hands carry disease offended them.

verdict: Answerable by common sense and the mocked-hero story is a good payoff, but the obscure name leads and "no coffee" is a throwaway.

rewrite.q_ru: Что венский врач Земмельвейс в 1847 году потребовал от акушеров?
rewrite.q_en: What did Viennese doctor Semmelweis demand of obstetricians in 1847?
options: * Мыть руки хлоркой | Wash hands in chlorine
rewrite.why_better: A plausible hygiene distractor replaces the joke option, so players weigh real alternatives.

original.ru: Откуда взялось «спир» в названии «аспирин»?
original.en: Where does the spir in Aspirin come from?
options: * От растения таволги | From the meadowsweet plant
От слова «спирт» | From the word spirit
От слова «спираль» | From the word spiral
От фамилии химика | From a chemist's surname
original.fact: Salicylic acid was taken from meadowsweet (Spiraea), and long before that people chewed willow bark.

verdict: Nice wordplay with the "спирт" trap; the meadowsweet answer is obscure but the plant option invites a guess.

original.ru: Кому принадлежит патент на вакцину от полиомиелита, спросили Джонаса Солка. Он ответил: «Разве можно запатентовать…»
original.en: Asked who owned the patent on his polio vaccine, Jonas Salk replied: Could you patent…
original.fact: Salk took no patent, so any maker in the world could produce the vaccine.

verdict: Famous quote with elegant options, but the question is over 100 characters and hard to read in time.

rewrite.q_ru: Джонас Солк не стал патентовать вакцину от полиомиелита: «Разве можно запатентовать…»
rewrite.q_en: Jonas Salk refused to patent his polio vaccine: "Could you patent…"
rewrite.why_better: Shorter and clearer, and the refusal framing makes the punchline easier to feel.

original.ru: Ботулизм, а с ним и ботокс, назван по латинскому слову, означающему…
original.en: Botulism, and so Botox, is named after the Latin word for…
original.fact: In the 1820s German doctor Justinus Kerner linked the poisonings to badly made sausages.

verdict: Botox named after sausage is a pure "wait, seriously?"; the wrinkle and poison traps are well chosen.

original.ru: Зачем хирург Холстед в 1889 году заказал первые резиновые перчатки?
original.en: Why did surgeon William Halsted order the first rubber surgical gloves in 1889?
options: * Берёг руки любимой медсестры | To spare his favourite nurse's hands
Чтобы руки не мёрзли | To keep his hands warm
Скрывал обручальное кольцо | To hide his wedding ring
Так велел закон | The law required it
original.fact: Her skin could not stand the antiseptics. They married a year later; gloves against germs came after.

verdict: A love story behind surgical gloves: surprising, funny and very retellable.

original.ru: В каком году ВОЗ объявила, что оспа побеждена во всём мире?
original.en: In what year did the WHO declare smallpox wiped out worldwide?
original.fact: It is the only human disease ever eradicated; the last natural case was in Somalia in 1977.

verdict: A bare date with a generous tolerance; the strong part (the only disease ever eradicated) is hidden in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Оспа — единственная болезнь человека, побеждённая полностью. В каком году ВОЗ это объявила?
rewrite.q_en: Smallpox is the only human disease ever wiped out. In what year did the WHO declare it?
rewrite.why_better: Leading with "the only disease ever beaten" gives the date a reason to matter and a slightly tighter tolerance.

original.ru: В каком году в Бостоне впервые публично провели операцию под эфирным наркозом?
original.en: In what year was an operation first done under ether in public, in Boston?
original.fact: The hall is still called the Ether Dome, and after the operation surgeon John Collins Warren said: Gentlemen, this is no humbug.

verdict: A historical date with an obscure Boston setting; the "no humbug" quote is a good payoff but the question is an exam item.

rewrite.q_ru: В каком году хирурги впервые публично усыпили пациента эфиром?
rewrite.q_en: In what year did surgeons first put a patient under with ether in public?
rewrite.why_better: Drops the obscure place and widens the range so the "surgery without anaesthesia until when?" intuition does the work.

original.ru: Что на самом деле такое «падающая звезда»?
original.en: What is a 'shooting star' really?
options: Звезда, сорвавшаяся с неба | A star falling from the sky
* Пылинка, сгорающая в воздухе | Dust burning up in the air
original.fact: Most are bits the size of a grain of sand that slam into the air and glow white hot about 100 km up.

verdict: Familiar sight with a surprising scale (a grain of sand); solid.

original.ru: Что сказал Юрий Гагарин в момент старта?
original.en: What did Yuri Gagarin say at lift-off?
original.fact: 'Key to start' was the command from the bunker and 'Seagull' was Tereshkova's call sign; Gagarin's was 'Cedar'.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition for a Russian family; the call sign fact is a nice bonus.

original.ru: Кто стал первой женщиной в космосе?
original.en: Who was the first woman in space?
original.fact: She flew in 1963 and is still the only woman ever to fly into space alone.

verdict: Every Russian knows Tereshkova, and Marie Curie is a throwaway; the best part ("only woman ever to fly solo") is buried in the fact.

rewrite.q_ru: Кто до сих пор единственная женщина, слетавшая в космос в одиночку?
rewrite.q_en: Who is still the only woman ever to fly into space alone?
rewrite.why_better: Same answer, but the "still the only one" angle surprises and all four women are real cosmonauts or astronauts.

original.ru: На какой планете сутки длиннее года?
original.en: On which planet is a day longer than a year?
original.fact: Venus takes 243 Earth days to spin once but only 225 to orbit the Sun, and it spins backwards too.

verdict: A day longer than a year is a genuine paradox; Venus is reachable by reasoning.

original.ru: На какой планете самый высокий вулкан Солнечной системы?
original.en: Which planet has the tallest volcano in the Solar System?
original.fact: Olympus Mons rises about 22 km, some two and a half times the height of Everest.

verdict: Recognisable (Olympus Mons) with a good height comparison; solid if not surprising.

original.ru: Какого цвета закат на Марсе?
original.en: What colour is a sunset on Mars?
original.fact: Fine Martian dust scatters blue light forward, so a blue glow surrounds the setting Sun.

verdict: Blue sunsets on the red planet are a great reversal of expectation.

original.ru: Что такое Большое красное пятно на Юпитере?
original.en: What is the Great Red Spot on Jupiter?
options: След от удара астероида | An asteroid impact scar
Море раскалённой лавы | A sea of molten lava
original.fact: A century or more ago three Earths would have fit across this storm; it has shrunk to about one, and nobody quite knows why.

verdict: Widely known as a storm; the shrinking mystery is the interesting part but it only appears after the reveal.

rewrite.q_ru: Большое красное пятно на Юпитере за век сжалось втрое. Что это такое?
rewrite.q_en: Jupiter's Great Red Spot has shrunk to about a third in a century. What is it?
options: След от удара астероида | An asteroid impact scar
Море раскалённой лавы | A sea of molten lava
rewrite.why_better: The shrinking hook adds intrigue up front and makes the volcano and lava options feel more tempting.

original.ru: Как сам Гагарин вернулся на Землю?
original.en: How did Gagarin himself get back down to Earth?
options: * Сам, на своём парашюте | On his own parachute
В капсуле, в море | In the capsule, into the sea
В капсуле, на сушу | In the capsule, on land
Сел на полосу, как самолёт | On a runway, like a plane
original.fact: He ejected about 7 km up; this was kept quiet for years, as record rules said a pilot must land inside his craft.

verdict: A hidden Soviet secret about a national hero: surprising, plausible options, great for this family.

original.ru: Сколько земных дней длится год на Марсе?
original.en: How many Earth days does a year on Mars last?
original.fact: Almost two of ours: Mars is farther from the Sun, so its orbit is longer and it moves along it more slowly.

verdict: Estimable but feels like an astronomy lesson; the fact just restates the reasoning.

rewrite.q_ru: Сколько земных дней пришлось бы ждать следующего дня рождения на Марсе?
rewrite.q_en: How many Earth days would you wait for your next birthday on Mars?
rewrite.why_better: Same number, but a birthday framing makes it personal and funnier to argue about.

original.ru: Сколько планет размером с Землю встало бы в ряд между Землёй и Луной?
original.en: How many Earths would fit in a row between the Earth and the Moon?
original.fact: When the Moon is at its farthest, even all the other planets of the Solar System fit into that gap.

verdict: Hard to imagine but estimable, and the "all planets fit" fact is a wow.

original.ru: Астронавт на Луне уронил молоток и перо одновременно. Что упало первым?
original.en: An astronaut on the Moon dropped a hammer and a feather at once. Which landed first?
options: Перо улетело вверх | The feather floated up
original.fact: David Scott did it on Apollo 15 in 1971: with no air, everything falls at the same rate, just as Galileo said.

verdict: Many know the vacuum answer, but the real Apollo 15 demo is a nice payoff; "feather floated up" is a throwaway.

original.ru: Как микроволновка греет еду?
original.en: How does a microwave oven heat food?
options: * Раскачивает молекулы воды | It makes water molecules jiggle
Скрытой спиралью | With a hidden heating coil
Сначала греет тарелку | It heats the plate first
Ультрафиолетовой лампой | With an ultraviolet lamp
original.fact: It was found by accident: in 1945 engineer Percy Spencer noticed a working radar set had melted the candy bar in his pocket.

verdict: Familiar appliance; answer known to many, but the melted candy bar story is a good reveal.

original.ru: Зачем на мостах оставляют зазоры с металлическими «гребёнками»?
original.en: Why do bridges have gaps with metal 'combs' in the road?
options: * Мост удлиняется от жары | The bridge grows in the heat
Чтобы стекала вода | To let rain drain away
Чтобы будить водителей | To keep drivers awake
Так дешевле строить | It is cheaper to build
original.fact: Steel and concrete expand when warm; without expansion joints a long bridge would buckle and crack in summer.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition question with a fun distractor ("to keep drivers awake"); reasoning gets you there.

original.ru: Где звук распространяется быстрее всего?
original.en: Where does sound travel fastest?
original.fact: Sound runs about 6 km a second in steel, 17 times faster than in air, so you hear a train in the rails first.

verdict: School physics; "in a vacuum" is a throwaway, though the train-in-the-rails fact is good; the rewrite is only a partial fix, the ceiling is the fact itself.

rewrite.q_ru: Где звук распространяется быстрее всего?
rewrite.q_en: Where does sound travel fastest?
rewrite.why_better: Ice replaces the vacuum, so there are three plausible solids and liquids to weigh.

original.ru: При какой температуре вода самая плотная?
original.en: At what temperature is water at its densest?
original.fact: Water at +4 °C sinks to the bottom, so in winter the bed of a deep lake stays above freezing under the ice.

verdict: Reads like a physics exam item; the frozen-lake consequence is the interesting part.

rewrite.q_ru: Какая температура зимой у дна глубокого озера, если сверху лёд?
rewrite.q_en: In winter, with ice on top, what temperature is the bottom of a deep lake?
rewrite.why_better: Same answer through a real-world puzzle that players can reason about instead of recalling a textbook number.

original.ru: Какой металл окрашивает салют в зелёный цвет?
original.en: Which metal makes fireworks glow green?
original.fact: Each metal glows its own colour when hot: strontium red, sodium yellow like old street lamps, copper blue.

verdict: Pure chemistry memorisation with no reasoning path; the colour list in the fact is mildly interesting at best.

original.ru: По законам магнетизма магнитный полюс Земли в Арктике — это…
original.en: In terms of magnet physics, Earth's magnetic pole in the Arctic is…
options: Вообще не полюс | Not a pole at all
То северный, то южный каждый день | North one day, south the next
original.fact: A compass needle's north end is drawn to an opposite pole, so Earth's 'north' magnetic pole is really a south pole.

verdict: A good brain teaser, but the wording is technical, everyday language calls it the North Magnetic Pole, and the last option is a throwaway.

rewrite.q_ru: Северный конец стрелки компаса тянется в Арктику. Какой там полюс по законам магнетизма?
rewrite.q_en: A compass needle's north end points to the Arctic. What pole is there in magnet terms?
rewrite.why_better: The compass clue gives players the reasoning path (opposites attract) and removes the naming ambiguity.

original.ru: Какой буквы нет ни в одном символе таблицы Менделеева?
original.en: Which letter appears in no symbol of the periodic table?
original.fact: X is in xenon (Xe), Z in zinc (Zn), and W is tungsten from its old name wolfram. Besides J, Q is missing too.

verdict: A neat puzzle players can work out by recalling symbols, and the "Q is missing too" fact adds a twist.

original.ru: До какой температуры молния раскаляет воздух?
original.en: How hot does lightning make the air?
original.fact: About 30,000 °C, five times hotter than the Sun's surface. The air expands explosively, and that bang is the thunder.

verdict: Surprising number, but a 0 to 100,000 slider gives no anchor to estimate from.

rewrite.q_ru: Поверхность Солнца — около 5500 °C. До скольких градусов молния раскаляет воздух?
rewrite.q_en: The Sun's surface is about 5,500 °C. How hot does lightning make the air?
rewrite.why_better: A familiar reference temperature lets players reason and makes "hotter than the Sun" land as a shock.

original.ru: Сколько килограммов весит весь воздух в комнате 4 × 5 м с потолком 2,5 м?
original.en: How many kilograms does all the air in a 4 × 5 m room with a 2.5 m ceiling weigh?
original.fact: A cubic metre of air weighs about 1.2 kg, and the room holds 50 of them: as heavy as an adult.

verdict: An everyday room, a calculable answer and a shock (as heavy as an adult); excellent estimation question.

original.ru: Кем работал Ласло Биро, изобретатель шариковой ручки?
original.en: What was László Bíró, inventor of the ballpoint pen, by trade?
original.fact: He noticed that newspaper ink dried at once while fountain pen ink smudged.

verdict: Good link between job and invention, but nothing in the question lets players reason toward journalism.

rewrite.q_ru: Идею шариковой ручки Ласло Биро подсказала его работа. Кем он работал?
rewrite.q_en: László Bíró's job gave him the idea for the ballpoint pen. What was he?
rewrite.why_better: Hinting that his job inspired the pen gives players something to reason with, and the newspaper ink fact then clicks.

original.ru: Кем был Сэмюэл Морзе, прежде чем придумал свою азбуку?
original.en: What was Samuel Morse before he devised his code?
original.fact: He painted US presidents and taught painting; he only took up the telegraph in his forties.

verdict: A painter inventing a code is a nice surprise, but "telegraph operator" is anachronistic before the telegraph existed and repeats the question's idea.

rewrite.q_ru: Кем был Сэмюэл Морзе, прежде чем придумал свою азбуку?
rewrite.q_en: What was Samuel Morse before he devised his code?
rewrite.why_better: A plausible technical trade replaces the self-referential distractor.

original.ru: Что показал Элиша Отис в 1854 году, велев перерубить трос?
original.en: What did Elisha Otis show off in 1854 by having the rope cut?
original.fact: He stood on the platform as the rope was cut and his safety brake held it; skyscrapers became possible.

verdict: The rope-cutting stunt is vivid and leads to the answer by reasoning; the skyscraper link is a good payoff.

original.ru: Первый моторный пылесос 1901 года был так велик, что...
original.en: The first powered vacuum cleaner of 1901 was so big that...
options: * его везла лошадь, шланг шёл в окно | a horse pulled it, hoses went in windows
его ставили на крышу | it was set up on the roof
им чистили только корабли | it only cleaned ships
его тянул паровоз | a steam engine towed it
original.fact: Hubert Booth used it on Westminster Abbey's carpets before Edward VII's coronation.

verdict: A horse-drawn vacuum cleaner is funny and surprising, but the correct option is twice as long as the rest.

rewrite.q_ru: Первый моторный пылесос 1901 года был так велик, что...
rewrite.q_en: The first powered vacuum cleaner of 1901 was so big that...
options: * его возила лошадь | a horse pulled it
его ставили на крышу | it sat on the roof
им чистили лишь корабли | it only cleaned ships
его тянул паровоз | a steam engine towed it
rewrite.why_better: Equal-length endings remove the tell while the horse stays the funniest answer.

original.ru: Маргарет Найт отсудила патент у мужчины, укравшего её идею. Что делала её машина?
original.en: Margaret Knight won her patent back from a man who copied her. What did her machine make?
original.fact: Her rival claimed a woman could not grasp such machinery; she brought her drawings and won the patent in 1871.

verdict: The sexism story is a good payoff, but the setup is wordy and "paper bags" is the longest option; the rewrite is only a partial fix, the ceiling is the obscure inventor.

rewrite.q_ru: Изобретательница в 1871-м отсудила патент у мужчины. Что делала её машина?
rewrite.q_en: In 1871 a woman inventor won her patent back from a man. What did her machine make?
rewrite.why_better: Shorter question with four balanced everyday products.

original.ru: Кто в 1596 году описал в книге смывной унитаз собственной конструкции?
original.en: Who described his own flushing toilet in a book in 1596?
options: * Крестник Елизаветы I | Queen Elizabeth I's godson
