verdict: Classification with a modest reveal; the jellyfish trap is fine but the payoff is thin compared with the rest of the sea topic.

original.ru: У кого самые большие глаза среди ныне живущих животных?
original.en: Which living animal has the biggest eyes?
options: У синего кита | The blue whale
* У глубоководного кальмара | A deep sea squid
original.fact: A colossal squid's eye is up to 30 cm across, like a dinner plate, probably to spot a hunting sperm whale far off in the dark.

verdict: Dinner-plate eyes for spotting sperm whales is a great payoff; the correct option is the longest.

rewrite.q_ru: У кого самые большие глаза среди ныне живущих животных?
rewrite.q_en: Which living animal has the biggest eyes?
options: У синего кита | The blue whale
rewrite.why_better: Short, equal options keep the whales as the trap without a length tell.

original.ru: Что происходит с глазами камбалы, пока она растёт?
original.en: What happens to a flounder's eyes as it grows up?
options: * Один переползает на другую сторону | One moves to the other side
Один глаз отмирает | One eye dies off
Вырастает третий глаз | It grows a third eye
Они срастаются в один | They merge into one
original.fact: The young fish swims like any other, then lies on its side, and the lower eye migrates to the top.

verdict: A migrating eye is a real "wait, seriously?", but the correct option is much longer than the rest.

rewrite.q_ru: Что происходит с глазами камбалы, пока она растёт?
rewrite.q_en: What happens to a flounder's eyes as it grows up?
options: * Один переползает на другой бок | One moves to the other side
Один зарастает кожей | One grows over with skin
Между ними растёт третий | A third grows between them
Они срастаются в один | They merge into one
rewrite.why_better: Balanced lengths remove the tell.

original.ru: Кого учёные называют «бессмертным»?
original.en: Which animal do scientists call immortal?
original.fact: When old or injured, this jellyfish turns back into a young polyp and starts its life over again.

verdict: An immortal jellyfish is a wow fact; the Latin name hints a little but the reveal pays off.

original.ru: На какой глубине лежат обломки «Титаника»?
original.en: How deep does the wreck of the Titanic lie?
original.fact: That depth is why the wreck was only found in 1985, 73 years after the sinking.

verdict: Everyone knows Titanic; estimable depth with a fair range.

original.ru: Какова глубина Марианской впадины в самой глубокой точке?
original.en: How deep is the Mariana Trench at its deepest point?
original.fact: Drop Mount Everest in there and there would still be about two kilometres of water above its peak.

verdict: Many know "about 11 km", the range is loose, and it repeats sea_004 (also the Mariana Trench) in the same topic; the Everest image is the payoff.

rewrite.q_ru: Какова глубина Марианской впадины в самой глубокой точке, в метрах?
rewrite.q_en: How deep is the Mariana Trench at its deepest point, in metres?
rewrite.why_better: A tighter range and tolerance make the guess a real estimate; with sea_004 dropped the trench appears less often.

original.ru: Кем на самом деле был вымерший тасманийский тигр?
original.en: What was the extinct Tasmanian tiger really?
original.fact: The thylacine carried its young in a pouch like a kangaroo; the last known one died in Hobart Zoo in 1936.

verdict: Most think it was a dog or cat; "marsupial" is a good reveal.

original.ru: Что такое янтарь?
original.en: What is amber?
options: * Окаменевшая смола деревьев | Fossilised tree resin
Кристаллы морской соли | Sea salt crystals
original.fact: Resin keeps whatever it traps: in 2016 a small dinosaur's tail, feathers and all, turned up in a lump of amber from Myanmar.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition question; the feathered dinosaur tail in amber is an excellent payoff.

original.ru: Где чаще всего находят мамонтов с сохранившейся шерстью и мясом?
original.en: Where are mammoths with their fur and flesh still intact usually found?
options: В джунглях Амазонки | In the Amazon jungle
original.fact: Permafrost works like a freezer: in 2007 a baby mammoth, Lyuba, was found in Yamal some 42,000 years after she died.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition for a Russian family; Sahara and Amazon are throwaways.

rewrite.q_ru: Где чаще всего находят мамонтов с сохранившейся шерстью и мясом?
rewrite.q_en: Where are mammoths with their fur and flesh still intact usually found?
rewrite.why_better: Cold places as distractors make players think instead of discarding three deserts and jungles.

original.ru: Какое вымирание было самым массовым в истории Земли?
original.en: Which was the biggest mass extinction in Earth's history?
options: * Пермское, 252 млн лет назад | The Permian, 252 million years ago
Гибель динозавров | The end of the dinosaurs
Конец ледникового периода | The end of the Ice Age
Триасовое, 201 млн лет назад | The Triassic, 201 million years ago
original.fact: The 'Great Dying' wiped out about 80% of sea species and 70% of land vertebrates, probably after giant volcanic eruptions in Siberia.

verdict: The dinosaur trap is good and the Siberian volcano link is great for this family, but the dated options read like a geology exam.

rewrite.q_ru: Какое вымирание погубило больше всего видов за всю историю Земли?
rewrite.q_en: Which extinction killed the most species in Earth's history?
options: Конец ледникового периода | The end of the Ice Age
rewrite.why_better: Without dates the options read evenly and the dinosaur trap pulls harder.

original.ru: Что такое копролит?
original.en: What is a coprolite?
options: Камень из желудка ящера | A stomach stone
Вид янтаря | A kind of amber
original.fact: Fossil dung shows who ate what: coprolites thought to come from tyrannosaurs hold bone fragments of their prey.

verdict: Poop is always a crowd-pleaser and the copro- root gives a reasoning path; bone shards in T. rex dung are a good payoff.

original.ru: Кем саблезубый тигр смилодон приходился настоящему тигру?
original.en: How was the sabre toothed tiger Smilodon related to the real tiger?
options: Тем же видом | The same species
Родным братом льва | The lion's brother
original.fact: Sabre tooths were a separate branch of cats that split from the ancestors of tigers and lions some 20 million years ago.

verdict: "The same species" and "the lion's brother" are weak, and the reveal is a dry taxonomy point.

rewrite.q_ru: Саблезубый «тигр» смилодон — кем он приходился настоящему тигру?
rewrite.q_en: The sabre-toothed "tiger" Smilodon: what was it to a real tiger?
options: Тем же видом | The same species
rewrite.why_better: Quoting "tiger" hints the name misleads, inviting a guess, and the lion option is a cleaner trap.

original.ru: Какой хищный динозавр был длиннее тираннозавра и ловил рыбу?
original.en: Which meat eating dinosaur was longer than T. rex and caught fish?
original.fact: Sail backed, crocodile snouted Spinosaurus grew up to about 14 metres and hunted in the rivers of North Africa.

verdict: Jurassic Park fans may know it, but the small dinosaurs are easy to discard and the fact repeats the question.

rewrite.q_ru: Какой хищный динозавр с парусом на спине был длиннее тираннозавра и ловил рыбу?
rewrite.q_en: Which meat-eating dinosaur with a sail on its back was longer than T. rex and caught fish?
rewrite.why_better: The sail clue lets anyone who saw Jurassic Park III recognise it.

original.ru: Кто ближайшие живые родственники птицы додо?
original.en: Who are the dodo's closest living relatives?
original.fact: The dodo was a huge flightless pigeon from Mauritius; its closest living relative is the Nicobar pigeon.

verdict: A dodo being a giant pigeon surprises everyone.

original.ru: Каким был размах крыльев кецалькоатля, одного из крупнейших летающих ящеров?
original.en: What was the wingspan of Quetzalcoatlus, one of the biggest flying reptiles?
original.fact: About 10 to 11 metres, like a small plane; standing on the ground it was as tall as a giraffe.

verdict: The species name is unknown to most; the giraffe and small plane images are the payoff.

rewrite.q_ru: Каким был размах крыльев самых больших летающих ящеров, в метрах?
rewrite.q_en: What was the wingspan of the biggest flying reptiles, in metres?
rewrite.why_better: Dropping the unknown name and tightening the range turns it into an estimate anyone can try.

original.ru: Какой длины самый большой найденный зуб тираннозавра вместе с корнем?
original.en: How long is the biggest T. rex tooth ever found, root included?
original.fact: About 30 cm, bigger than a banana; T. rex kept replacing its teeth all its life, a new one growing in for each one lost.

verdict: Easy to picture and estimate; the banana comparison helps.

original.ru: Как называют расплавленную породу, пока она ещё под землёй?
original.en: What is molten rock called while it is still underground?
original.fact: Magma rises because it is lighter than the rock around it; it is only called lava once it breaks out.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition question; the lava trap works but there is no surprise.

original.ru: Почему молнию мы видим раньше, чем слышим гром?
original.en: Why do we see lightning before we hear the thunder?
options: * Свет быстрее звука | Light is faster than sound
Гром рождается позже молнии | Thunder is made later
Глаза быстрее ушей | Eyes react faster than ears
original.fact: Count the seconds to the thunder and divide by three: that is how many kilometres away the storm is.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition question with a joke option; the count-to-three tip is useful.

original.ru: Какой камень может плавать в воде?
original.en: Which rock can float on water?
original.fact: Pumice is frozen volcanic froth full of bubbles; after eruptions, rafts of it drift across oceans for years.

verdict: Many have seen pumice in a bathroom; drifting pumice rafts are a nice payoff.

original.ru: Где произошло самое сильное землетрясение за всю историю измерений?
original.en: Where was the strongest earthquake ever recorded?
original.fact: Magnitude about 9.5: the ground shook for some ten minutes and the tsunami crossed the Pacific to Hawaii and Japan.

verdict: Japan 2011 and Indonesia 2004 are strong traps from memory; Chile is a good surprise.

original.ru: Чем ураган отличается от тайфуна?
original.en: What is the difference between a hurricane and a typhoon?
options: * Только местом, где он бушует | Only where it happens
original.fact: Over the Atlantic it is a hurricane, in the western Pacific a typhoon, in the Indian Ocean a cyclone.

verdict: A word difference many never questioned; tidy reveal with the cyclone extra.

original.ru: Какую форму на самом деле имеет крупная падающая капля дождя?
original.en: What shape is a large falling raindrop really?
options: * Булочки, сплюснутой снизу | A bun, flat underneath
original.fact: Oncoming air flattens its bottom; it only looks like a teardrop while it clings to a tap.

verdict: The teardrop myth is busted by a bun; great, but the correct option is longest.

rewrite.q_ru: Какую форму на самом деле имеет крупная падающая капля дождя?
rewrite.q_en: What shape is a large falling raindrop really?
rewrite.why_better: One-word options remove the length tell.

original.ru: В 2010 году в США упала градина-рекордсменка. Какого она была размера?
original.en: A record-breaking hailstone fell in the USA in 2010. How big was it?
options: С грецкий орех | Like a walnut
С теннисный мяч | Like a tennis ball
* С волейбольный мяч | Like a volleyball
original.fact: It was 20 cm across and weighed almost 900 g; the heaviest on record, over a kilogram, fell in Bangladesh in 1986.

verdict: Hail the size of a volleyball is vivid, though "record" telegraphs the biggest option.

original.ru: Что измеряет шкала Бофорта?
original.en: What does the Beaufort scale measure?
original.fact: British naval officer Francis Beaufort devised it in 1805: from 0, dead calm, to 12, hurricane.

verdict: A definition question with an unknown name; nobody reacts to "wind strength".

original.ru: Сколько градусов мороза зафиксировали на станции «Восток» в Антарктиде в 1983 году?
original.en: How many degrees below zero (°C) were recorded at Vostok Station in Antarctica in 1983?
original.fact: −89.2°C is colder than dry ice, which turns to gas at −78.5°C.

verdict: Russians know "minus 89" and the dry ice comparison is vivid.

original.ru: Какой температуры свежая базальтовая лава, как на Гавайях?
original.en: How hot is fresh basalt lava, like that of Hawaii?
original.fact: Hawaii gave geologists two words for lava: smooth pahoehoe and rough, jagged a'a.

verdict: A bare temperature with a fact about lava names that has nothing to do with the answer.

original.ru: Какое хищное растение можно найти на болотах России?
original.en: Which carnivorous plant grows wild in Russian bogs?
original.fact: Sundew leaves bear hairs tipped with sticky drops that look like dew; an insect gets stuck and the hairs slowly bend over it and digest it.

verdict: Good for a Russian family; the famous Venus flytrap is a fair trap.

original.ru: Зачем венерина мухоловка ловит насекомых?
original.en: Why does a Venus flytrap catch insects?
options: * Почва, где она растёт, бедна азотом | Its soil is poor in nitrogen
У неё нет листьев для фотосинтеза | It has no leaves to photosynthesise
Так она защищает свои цветы | To protect its flowers
Из насекомых она берёт воду | To get water from them
original.fact: It grows in Carolina bogs with almost no nitrogen and gets it from prey; it still makes its own sugar like any plant.

verdict: Reasonable deduction, but the options are long and it feels like a biology lesson; the rewrite is only a partial fix.

rewrite.q_ru: Зачем венерина мухоловка ловит насекомых?
rewrite.q_en: Why does a Venus flytrap catch insects?
options: * Почва бедна азотом | Its soil lacks nitrogen
У неё нет листьев | It has no leaves
Так она охраняет цветы | To guard its flowers
Ей нужна их вода | It needs their water
rewrite.why_better: Shorter options read in time and keep the "it still makes its own sugar" reveal.

original.ru: Где созревает арахис?
original.en: Where do peanuts ripen?
original.fact: Peanuts flower above ground, then the stalk bends down and pushes the young pod into the soil to ripen there.

verdict: Many have never pictured peanuts growing; the burying flower is a nice payoff.

original.ru: Куда смотрят взрослые цветущие подсолнухи?
original.en: Which way do mature sunflowers in bloom face?
options: * На восток, весь день | East, all day
Вслед за солнцем весь день | They follow the sun all day
На запад, весь день | West, all day
Каждый куда придётся | Each one any way at all
original.fact: Only young sunflowers track the sun; once in bloom they stay facing east, where the morning sun warms them and draws more bees.

verdict: Everyone "knows" sunflowers follow the sun; the east-facing truth is a great reversal.

original.ru: Какого цвета была морковь, когда её только начали выращивать?
original.en: What colour were the first cultivated carrots?
options: * Фиолетовой или жёлтой | Purple or yellow
original.fact: Carrots were first grown in Persia and Afghanistan in purple and yellow; today's orange ones were bred in the Netherlands in the 1500s and 1600s.

verdict: Great fact, but the correct option is the only two-part answer (telegraphed) and "Blue" is a throwaway.

rewrite.q_ru: Какого цвета была морковь, когда её только начали выращивать?
rewrite.q_en: What colour were the first cultivated carrots?
rewrite.why_better: Single colours remove the two-part tell and every option sounds plausible.

original.ru: Сколько листьев за всю жизнь вырастает у вельвичии из пустыни Намиб?
original.en: How many leaves does Welwitschia of the Namib desert grow in its whole life?
options: Новые каждую весну | New ones every spring
original.fact: Its two leaves keep growing from the base all its life, which can last over 1,000 years; wind shreds them so it looks like many.

verdict: Two leaves for a thousand years is a wow, but the plant name is unknown and "Два" stands out as the only small number.

rewrite.q_ru: Сколько листьев за всю жизнь вырастает у вельвичии, растения пустыни, живущего тысячу лет?
rewrite.q_en: How many leaves does Welwitschia, a desert plant that lives 1,000 years, grow in its whole life?
rewrite.why_better: The thousand-year lifespan sharpens the paradox and the number options are evenly spread.

original.ru: Кто ближайший родственник помидора из этого списка?
original.en: Which of these is the tomato's closest relative?
original.fact: Tomato and potato share a genus: graft one onto the other and you get tomatoes on top and potatoes in the ground.

verdict: Tomato and potato as siblings surprises, and the graft fact is fun; the similar-to flag (sea_028) is only the "closest relative" formula.

original.ru: Чем тупайи полезны хищному непентесу Лоу с Борнео?
original.en: How do tree shrews help the carnivorous pitcher plant Nepenthes lowii of Borneo?
options: * Оставляют в кувшине помёт | They leave droppings in it
Опыляют его цветки | They pollinate its flowers
Разносят его семена | They spread its seeds
Загоняют в него насекомых | They chase insects into it
original.fact: The tree shrew licks sweet stuff off the pitcher's lid and leaves droppings in it, which give the plant over half of its nitrogen.

verdict: A plant using a shrew as a toilet is hilarious, but two obscure names make the question hard to read.

rewrite.q_ru: Зверёк тупайя лижет сладкое с крышки хищного растения-кувшина. Чем он ему полезен?
rewrite.q_en: A tree shrew licks sweet stuff off a carnivorous pitcher plant's lid. How does it help the plant?
options: * Оставляет в нём помёт | It leaves droppings in it
Опыляет его цветки | It pollinates its flowers
Разносит его семена | It spreads its seeds
Загоняет в него мух | It herds flies into it
rewrite.why_better: A vivid scene replaces the Latin name, so the toilet punchline lands for everyone.

original.ru: В каком году в Голландии рухнули цены в разгар «тюльпаномании»?
original.en: In what year did the Dutch 'tulip mania' collapse?
original.fact: In February 1637 bulb prices, which had reached ten times a craftsman's yearly pay, collapsed within days.

verdict: Tulip mania is a great story, but the question is a bare year.

rewrite.q_ru: В каком году в Голландии лопнул тюльпанный пузырь, один из первых в истории?
rewrite.q_en: In what year did the Dutch tulip bubble, one of history's first, burst?
rewrite.why_better: Calling it a bubble connects it to modern crashes and gives players an era to reason from.

original.ru: Сколько лет назад индейцы Мексики одомашнили кукурузу?
original.en: About how many years ago was maize domesticated in Mexico?
original.fact: Maize's ancestor teosinte has a tiny ear of about a dozen hard kernels; thousands of years of selection made the cob.

verdict: Thousands of years is hard to place on a 0-30,000 slider with no reference point.

rewrite.q_ru: Пирамидам Египта около 4500 лет. Сколько лет назад в Мексике одомашнили кукурузу?
rewrite.q_en: The pyramids of Egypt are about 4,500 years old. How many years ago was maize domesticated in Mexico?
rewrite.why_better: A familiar ancient landmark gives players a yardstick.

original.ru: Ниагарский водопад стоит на границе США и какой страны?
original.en: Niagara Falls sit on the border of the USA and which country?
original.fact: The biggest of its three falls, the Horseshoe, is mostly Canadian, which is why the best view is from Canada.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition question; Cuba and Greenland are throwaways, but the Horseshoe fact is a nice payoff.

original.ru: С какой страной Аляска соседствует через Берингов пролив?
original.en: Across the Bering Strait, which country is Alaska's neighbour?
original.fact: Russia's Big Diomede and America's Little Diomede are 3.8 km apart, yet their clocks are almost a day apart.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition for a Russian family; the islands a day apart are an excellent payoff.

original.ru: Крошечное Монако с трёх сторон окружено какой страной?
original.en: Tiny Monaco is surrounded on three sides by which country?
original.fact: Monaco is the most densely populated country on Earth, and smaller than New York's Central Park.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition question; the Sokolniki comparison is a fun reveal.

original.ru: Кто порой оказывается ближе всех к точке Немо — самому удалённому от суши месту океана?
original.en: Who are sometimes the closest people to Point Nemo, the ocean spot farthest from land?
options: * Космонавты на МКС | Astronauts on the ISS
original.fact: The nearest land is about 2,700 km away, while the ISS passes overhead only about 400 km up.

verdict: The nearest humans are in space: a perfect "wait, seriously?".

original.ru: В городке Барле граница проходит прямо через дома и кафе. Каких двух стран?
original.en: In the town of Baarle the border runs through houses and cafés. Between which two countries?
options: * Бельгии и Нидерландов | Belgium and the Netherlands
Франции и Испании | France and Spain
Германии и Австрии | Germany and Austria
Швеции и Норвегии | Sweden and Norway
original.fact: Over twenty Belgian enclaves sit inside the Netherlands there, and one house has the border through its front door.

verdict: A door split by a border is delightful; the guess is mostly luck.

original.ru: Какая страна — самая большая в мире, где нет ни одной постоянной реки?
original.en: Which is the largest country in the world with no permanent river?
original.fact: It has only wadis, dry beds that fill after rare storms; most drinking water comes from desalination plants.

verdict: Egypt and Australia are good traps; the wadis fact is solid.

original.ru: В какой стране есть настоящий город Батман?
original.en: Which country has a real city called Batman?
original.fact: The village of Iluh became the city of Batman only in 1957, later than the comic hero, but its name comes from the local Batman River.

verdict: A real city called Batman gets a laugh and the river explanation lands.

original.ru: Где на самом деле южная оконечность Африки?
original.en: Where is the real southern tip of Africa?
options: Мыс Доброй Надежды | Cape of Good Hope
original.fact: The Cape of Good Hope is more famous, but Agulhas lies further south and marks where the Atlantic meets the Indian Ocean.

verdict: Good of Hope trap, but Cape Horn is in South America and is easy to discard.

rewrite.q_ru: Где на самом деле южная оконечность Африки?
rewrite.q_en: Where is the real southern tip of Africa?
options: Мыс Доброй Надежды | Cape of Good Hope
rewrite.why_better: All four capes are now African, so geography knowledge rather than elimination decides.

original.ru: Какова ширина Гибралтарского пролива между Европой и Африкой в самом узком месте, в километрах?
original.en: How wide is the Strait of Gibraltar between Europe and Africa at its narrowest, in km?
original.fact: About 14 km: on a clear day you can see Morocco's mountains from Spain, and ferries cross in under an hour.

verdict: Estimable and the "see Morocco from Spain" image is nice.

original.ru: Какую долю всей суши Земли занимает Россия, в процентах?
original.en: What share of all the Earth's land does Russia cover, in percent?
original.fact: About 11%: Russia's 17 million square kilometres are almost exactly the whole surface area of Pluto.

verdict: Estimable via "one sixth of the land" and the Pluto comparison is superb, but it repeats ussr_044 (USSR share of land); do not play both in one evening.

original.ru: Какой город — столица Австралии?
original.en: Which city is the capital of Australia?
original.fact: Sydney and Melbourne would not let each other win, so a new capital was built between them.

verdict: Classic Sydney/Melbourne trap that still catches people, and the fact explains why the capital is a compromise city. Many adults already know Canberra, so the surprise is modest.

original.ru: В какой стране овец больше, чем людей?
original.en: In which country do sheep outnumber people?
original.fact: At the 1982 peak there were 70 million sheep, more than twenty for every New Zealander.

verdict: Easy and guessable (New Zealand is the famous sheep country); Japan and the Netherlands are weak decoys. The 'twenty sheep per person' fact gives a good little payoff.

original.ru: Что означает название «Австралия»?
original.en: What does the name 'Australia' mean?
original.fact: Austria is unrelated: its German name, Österreich, means 'eastern realm'.

verdict: The Latin 'australis' makes it guessable, but 'Kangaroo land' is a throwaway and the Austria fact has no decoy to connect to. Making 'Eastern land' (Austria's real meaning) a distractor turns the fact into a payoff.

rewrite.q_ru: Что означает название «Австралия»?
rewrite.q_en: What does the name 'Australia' mean?
rewrite.why_better: Four parallel 'X land' options remove the throwaway, and the 'Eastern land' decoy is exactly Austria's meaning, so the fact lands as a twist.

original.ru: На флаге какой страны изображён дракон?
original.en: Which country has a dragon on its flag?
original.fact: Bhutanese call their land Druk Yul, 'land of the thunder dragon': mountain thunder was its roar.

verdict: China is a strong trap (dragons are Chinese, but its flag has none) and all distractors are credible Asian countries. The thunder-dragon fact gives a nice image.

original.ru: У какой страны единственный в мире непрямоугольный флаг?
original.en: Which country has the world's only non-rectangular national flag?
original.fact: The two-pennant flag is so tricky that Nepal's constitution gives step-by-step geometry for drawing it.

verdict: Nepal's two-pennant flag is visually memorable, so players feel they know it; the constitution-as-geometry-manual fact is a good tell-someone payoff.

original.ru: На флаге какой страны изображён храм?
original.en: Which country's flag shows a temple?
original.fact: Angkor Wat, the world's largest religious monument, has been on Cambodian flags since around 1875.

verdict: Third 'which country's flag shows X' question in this topic (with dragon and Nepal). Anyone who links Angkor Wat to Cambodia gets it, and Greece/Egypt are eliminated by knowing their flags; the fact restates the answer.

original.ru: Название какой страны придумали как сокращение из названий её областей?
original.en: Which country's name was invented as an acronym of its regions?
original.fact: In 1933 Cambridge student Rahmat Ali built it from Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh and Baluchistan.

verdict: Nice surprise that a country name was invented by a student as an acronym; Afghanistan and Bangladesh are credible 'stan/desh' decoys. Fact lists the regions, which is the payoff.

original.ru: Символа какой части Великобритании нет на её флаге?
original.en: Which nation of the UK has no symbol on the Union Jack?
original.fact: When the first Union Flag appeared in 1606, Wales was already part of the Kingdom of England.

verdict: Everyone can picture the Union Jack and the Welsh dragon is famous, so the 'Wales is missing' reveal starts a discussion. All four nations are credible options.

original.ru: В каком году у Канады появился флаг с кленовым листом?
original.en: In what year did Canada get its maple leaf flag?
original.fact: Before that Canada flew a red flag with the British Union Jack in the corner.

verdict: The surprise (the maple leaf is only from 1965) is hidden behind a bare date question, and the fact barely adds anything. Framing it around how long the Union Jack stayed on the flag makes the late date the point.

rewrite.q_ru: До какого года на флаге Канады в углу был британский «Юнион Джек»?
rewrite.q_en: Until what year did Canada's flag carry the British Union Jack in the corner?
rewrite.why_better: Asking how long Canada kept the British flag invites a 'surely long ago' guess, so the 1965 answer surprises instead of just being a date.

original.ru: В каком году Нигерия перенесла столицу из Лагоса в Абуджу?
original.en: In what year did Nigeria move its capital from Lagos to Abuja?
original.fact: Abuja was picked as neutral ground in the middle of the country, home to none of the big ethnic groups.

verdict: An arbitrary relocation year for a capital most of the family cannot place; there is nothing to reason from and nobody will care about the number. The neutral-ground fact is mildly interesting but not enough.

original.ru: На какой реке стоит Новосибирск?
original.en: Which river is Novosibirsk on?
original.fact: The city grew in 1893 out of a camp for the workers building the Trans-Siberian bridge over the Ob.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition question for a Russian family; zero surprise, but the bridge-builders' camp origin is a decent small payoff. Fine as a warm-up.

original.ru: В какое море впадает Волга?
original.en: Into which sea does the Volga flow?
options: В Азовское | The Sea of Azov
original.fact: The Caspian is really a huge lake, so Europe's longest river never reaches the ocean at all.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition (school geography); the fact that the Caspian is a lake, so Europe's longest river never reaches the ocean, rescues it. One of four river questions in this topic.

original.ru: Как назывался Калининград до 1946 года?
original.en: What was Kaliningrad called before 1946?
original.fact: It was the capital of East Prussia: the philosopher Immanuel Kant lived there all his life and is buried there.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition: most know Königsberg, but the decoys are all real Prussian cities, which makes it feel fair. Kant fact is familiar rather than surprising.

original.ru: Какой город России считается самым древним — ему больше 2000 лет?
original.en: Which Russian city is considered the oldest, at over 2,000 years old?
original.fact: Derbent guarded the narrow pass between the Caucasus and the Caspian; its Persian name means 'closed gates'.

verdict: Good trap: most will pick Novgorod or Staraya Ladoga, and Derbent being over 2,000 years old surprises. The 'closed gates' fact is a solid payoff.

original.ru: Какая река — единственная, что вытекает из Байкала?
original.en: Which river is the only one that flows out of Lake Baikal?
original.fact: About 330 rivers flow in; legend says father Baikal hurled a rock after his daughter Angara as she ran off to the Yenisei.

verdict: Known school fact (Angara is the only outflow) and one of four river questions; the Yenisei decoy is clever. The legend in the fact is the best part, so lead with it.

rewrite.q_ru: По легенде, у Байкала была дочь-река, сбежавшая к Енисею. Как её звали?
rewrite.q_en: Legend says Baikal had a river daughter who ran off to the Yenisei. What was her name?
rewrite.why_better: The runaway-daughter legend turns a geography fact into a story, and players can still reason that the river leaving Baikal flows to the Yenisei.

original.ru: Какая река России самая полноводная?
original.en: Which river in Russia carries the most water?
original.fact: The Yenisei splits Siberia in two: flat West Siberian plain on the left bank, mountains and plateaus on the right.

verdict: Fourth river question in the topic; the Volga trap is decent but the reveal is a dry geography lecture about Siberian plains. Nothing to tell anyone afterwards.

original.ru: В честь кого назван город Тольятти?
original.en: Who is the city of Tolyatti named after?
options: Инженера ВАЗа | A VAZ car engineer
Героя войны 1812 года | A hero of the 1812 war
original.fact: Until 1964 it was Stavropol; it was renamed after Palmiro Togliatti, head of the Italian Communist Party.

verdict: The city name sounds Italian, which gives a real reasoning path, and 'a VAZ engineer' is a great trap given the Fiat link. Togliatti the communist is a satisfying reveal.

original.ru: Какой крупный город целиком стоит на вечной мерзлоте?
original.en: Which large city stands entirely on permafrost?
original.fact: Buildings there stand on stilts so their warmth does not thaw the ground beneath them.

verdict: Solved by picking the coldest, most northern city in the list, so there is no real choice, and the stilts fact is fairly well known. Northern decoys such as Norilsk would also sit on permafrost and make it ambiguous, so it cannot be fixed with the same fact.

original.ru: Сколько глав (куполов) у Преображенской церкви в Кижах?
original.en: How many domes does the Church of the Transfiguration at Kizhi have?
original.fact: The 37 m wooden church of 1714 needed nails only for its roof and the shingles of its domes.

verdict: People have seen Kizhi on postcards, so estimating domes from memory is possible, but the framing is dry. Inviting players to picture the postcard and tightening the range makes it a visual-memory game.

rewrite.q_ru: Вспомните открытку с Кижами: сколько куполов у Преображенской церкви?
rewrite.q_en: Picture the Kizhi postcard: how many domes does the Church of the Transfiguration have?
rewrite.why_better: Invites everyone to picture a familiar image and count, which turns a memorised number into a visual estimate.

original.ru: Какова наибольшая глубина Байкала?
original.en: What is the greatest depth of Lake Baikal?
original.fact: Even three Ostankino TV towers stacked on top of each other would vanish completely under Baikal's water.

verdict: Everyone knows Baikal is the deepest lake, so the guess starts from real knowledge; the fair range and tolerance reward it. Three stacked Ostankino towers is a vivid payoff.

original.ru: Какой из этих языков пишут справа налево?
original.en: Which of these languages is written right to left?
original.fact: Yet numbers inside Arabic text still run left to right, just like ours.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition: almost everyone knows Arabic goes right to left. The numbers-run-left-to-right fact is a genuinely nice twist.

original.ru: Из какого языка пришло слово «бутерброд»?
original.en: Which language gave Russian the word 'buterbrod' (open sandwich)?
original.fact: German 'Butterbrot' literally means 'butter bread', so a Russian 'buterbrod with butter' says butter twice.

verdict: Guessable from 'Butter' + 'Brot', and the 'buterbrod with butter says butter twice' line gets a laugh at the table.

original.ru: Закончите знаменитый палиндром: «А роза упала на лапу…»
original.en: Finish the famous Russian palindrome: 'A roza upala na lapu…' (a rose fell on the paw of…)
original.fact: It is credited to the poet Fet; in 'The Golden Key' Malvina dictates it to Buratino. It reads the same both ways.

verdict: Everyone knows the phrase, and those who don't can solve it by reversing the letters, which is a fun group moment. The Malvina and Fet facts are a pleasant payoff.

original.ru: Откуда в русском взялось слово «вокзал»?
original.en: Where does the Russian word 'vokzal' (railway station) come from?
options: * От лондонского сада развлечений | A London pleasure garden
От немецкого «зал ожидания» | German for 'waiting hall'
От фамилии инженера | An engineer's surname
original.fact: The 1838 station at Pavlovsk was named 'Voksal' after London's Vauxhall Gardens, with music and strolling crowds.

verdict: Real 'wait, seriously?' etymology: a Russian station named after a London pleasure garden. Decoys are believable; the Pavlovsk story makes a great reveal.

original.ru: Как выглядит вопросительный знак в греческом языке?
original.en: What does a question mark look like in Greek?
options: * Как наша точка с запятой | Like our semicolon
Как перевёрнутый «?» | Like an upside down '?'
original.fact: And the job of a semicolon in Greek is done by a dot raised to the top of the line.

verdict: Surprising and easy to picture; the Spanish upside-down '?' is a smart decoy. The raised-dot semicolon fact doubles the oddity.

original.ru: Откуда взялось выражение «не в своей тарелке»?
original.en: Where does the Russian idiom 'not in one's own plate' (feeling out of sorts) come from?
options: * Неточный перевод с французского | A mistranslation from French
Боярский застольный обычай | A boyars' table custom
original.fact: French 'assiette' means both a plate and a state of mind, and Russian ended up with the plate.

verdict: Everyone uses the idiom and nobody knows it is a mistranslation; 'assiette' meaning both plate and state of mind is a satisfying reveal. The NOT script flag is a false positive (the 'не' is part of the idiom).

original.ru: Что ещё значит «babushka» в английском, кроме бабушки?
original.en: Besides 'grandmother', what does 'babushka' mean in English?
options: * Платок, завязанный под подбородком | A headscarf tied under the chin
original.fact: English speakers named the scarf after the Russian grandmothers who wore it tied that way.

verdict: Fun angle on how English borrowed a Russian word, but the correct option is far longer and more detailed than the rest. A short 'headscarf' option fixes the telegraph cheaply.

rewrite.q_ru: Что ещё значит «babushka» в английском, кроме бабушки?
rewrite.q_en: Besides 'grandmother', what does 'babushka' mean in English?
rewrite.why_better: All options are now short granny-style objects of equal length, so nothing gives the answer away.

original.ru: Мы зовём знак @ «собакой». А как его называют итальянцы?
original.en: Russians call the @ sign 'the little dog'. What do Italians call it?
original.fact: The Dutch say 'monkey's tail', the Danes 'elephant's trunk', and Israelis 'strudel'.

verdict: Everyone knows the Russian 'sobaka', and the decoys are other countries' real names for @, which the fact then reveals. The snail shape gives an intuition path.

original.ru: Сколько букв в гавайском алфавите?
original.en: How many letters are in the Hawaiian alphabet?
original.fact: There are only eight consonants, counting the glottal stop, and every syllable ends in a vowel: aloha, Honolulu.

verdict: Players can reason from 'aloha' and 'Honolulu' that the alphabet is tiny; 13 is a surprising number, and the fair tolerance rewards that logic.

original.ru: В каком году реформа орфографии убрала из алфавита букву «ять»?
original.en: In what year did a spelling reform drop the old letter yat from Russian?
original.fact: Two more letters went with it, and the hard sign stopped being written at the end of words like 'khleb'.

verdict: Anyone who links the reform to the revolution gets it, and the ±25 tolerance makes it nearly free. Tightening the tolerance and naming all three letters makes it a real estimate.

rewrite.q_ru: В каком году из русского алфавита исчезли «ять», «і» и «фита»?
rewrite.q_en: In what year did yat, i and fita disappear from the Russian alphabet?
rewrite.why_better: A tight tolerance rewards players who place the reform right after the revolution instead of giving points for any 20th-century guess.

original.ru: Какое главное угощение Масленицы?
original.en: What is the signature food of Maslenitsa?
original.fact: 'Pancake as sun' was dreamed up by 19th-century scholars: blini were really an old food for honouring the dead.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition: everyone answers blini. The myth-busting fact (the 'pancake as sun' idea was invented by 19th-century scholars) is a real payoff and will start an argument.

original.ru: За чем бегут вниз по крутому холму на ежегодном празднике в английском Глостершире?
original.en: What do people chase down a steep hill at a yearly festival in Gloucestershire, England?
options: * За кругом сыра | A wheel of cheese
original.fact: The 3–4 kg cheese rolls so fast it is nearly uncatchable, so the prize goes to whoever reaches the bottom first.

verdict: Many have seen the viral cheese-rolling videos, the answer is funny, and the 'cheese is uncatchable' fact lands. Slightly long question but still readable.

original.ru: На каком индийском празднике все обсыпают друг друга цветным порошком?
original.en: At which Indian festival does everyone throw coloured powder at each other?
original.fact: Holi welcomes spring, and its coloured powder, gulal, was once made from flowers and herbs.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition: Holi's colour powder is widely known. Decoys are real festivals, but the fact (welcomes spring, powder from flowers) is flat.

original.ru: Какая страна каждый год дарит Лондону ёлку для Трафальгарской площади?
original.en: Which country gives London a Christmas tree for Trafalgar Square every year?
original.fact: Since 1947 it has been Oslo's thank-you to Britain for its help during the Second World War.

verdict: Plausible decoys (Canada, Finland, Germany) and a warm thank-you story from WWII as payoff. Solid medium question.

original.ru: Из чего вырезают фигуры на конкурсе 23 декабря в мексиканском городе Оахака?
original.en: What are figures carved from at the 23 December contest in Oaxaca, Mexico?
original.fact: The Night of the Radishes dates from 1897, and its radishes are grown huge and twisted on purpose.

verdict: Wonderful 'wait, seriously?' answer, but the correct option is twice as long and the only oddly specific one, and 'ice' or 'cheese' make little sense in Mexico. Balanced Mexican-plausible options keep the surprise without the telegraph.

rewrite.q_ru: Из чего вырезают фигуры на празднике 23 декабря в мексиканском городе Оахака?
rewrite.q_en: What are figures carved from at the 23 December festival in Oaxaca, Mexico?
rewrite.why_better: Short, equal options that all sound Mexican make players genuinely weigh sugar skulls and corn, so the radish reveal is a real surprise.

original.ru: Кто приносит подарки итальянским детям в ночь на 6 января?
original.en: Who brings Italian children presents on the night before 6 January?
options: * Добрая ведьма Бефана | Befana, a kind witch
original.fact: Befana flies on a broomstick, filling good children's stockings with sweets and bad ones' with coal.

verdict: Befana is a fun figure, but the Easter Bunny and Saint Valentine in January are throwaways and 'kind witch' description singles out the answer. Real Christmas gift-bringers as decoys make it a genuine choice.

rewrite.q_ru: Кто приносит подарки итальянским детям в ночь на 6 января?
rewrite.q_en: Who brings Italian children presents on the night before 6 January?
rewrite.why_better: Every option is a real holiday gift-bringer (the Three Kings even come on 6 January in Spain), so the broomstick witch is a surprise rather than the only sensible answer.

original.ru: В Альпах вместе со святым Николаем ходит рогатый демон и пугает непослушных детей. Кто это?
original.en: In the Alps, a horned demon follows St Nicholas to scare naughty children. Who is he?
original.fact: On the eve of 6 December, crowds dressed as shaggy Krampuses still parade through Austrian towns.

verdict: Krampus is known from films, and the long description plus non-Alpine decoys (Grinch, Koschei) make it easy elimination. A shorter question and a credible bogeyman decoy tighten it.

rewrite.q_ru: Кто ходит по Альпам вместе со святым Николаем и пугает непослушных детей?
rewrite.q_en: Who walks the Alps with St Nicholas, scaring naughty children?
rewrite.why_better: Shorter and readable at a glance, and the Babay decoy is a real child-scaring figure for Russian players.

original.ru: Кого, по легенде, отпугивают петардами и красным цветом на китайский Новый год?
original.en: In legend, who are firecrackers and red decorations at Chinese New Year meant to scare off?
original.fact: 'Nian' also means 'year' in Chinese, so 'guo nian', to celebrate the New Year, can be read as 'to get past Nian'.

verdict: Great pun payoff (Nian also means 'year'), but 'beast' is the only monster among mice, a rabbit and a bear, so the answer is telegraphed. Make every option a mythical creature.

rewrite.q_ru: Кого, по легенде, отпугивают петардами и красным цветом на китайский Новый год?
rewrite.q_en: In legend, who are firecrackers and red decorations at Chinese New Year meant to scare off?
rewrite.why_better: All four are scary creatures, so players must reason instead of picking the only monster, and the 'Nian = year' pun still lands.

original.ru: В каком году в шведском городе Евле впервые поставили гигантского соломенного козла?
original.en: In which year did the Swedish town of Gävle first build its giant straw Christmas goat?
original.fact: It was burnt down on its very first New Year's Eve, and arsonists have repeated the feat many times since.

verdict: The burning-goat story is hilarious, but the question hides it behind a founding year nobody can estimate. Putting the arson tradition into the question gives context and makes the date a curiosity.

rewrite.q_ru: В шведском Евле на Рождество ставят огромного соломенного козла, а его часто сжигают. С какого года?
rewrite.q_en: Every Christmas the Swedish town of Gävle builds a giant straw goat, and people keep burning it. Since what year?
rewrite.why_better: The arson tradition up front gets laughs before the answer, and the fact (burnt on its very first night) becomes the punchline.

original.ru: Сколько рождественских парней — троллей-проказников — навещают исландских детей перед Рождеством?
original.en: How many Yule Lads, prankster trolls, visit Icelandic children before Christmas?
original.fact: They come one per night, each with his own mischief: one licks spoons, one slams doors, one swipes sausages.

verdict: Delightful folklore with a funny fact, but the number is pure guesswork as asked. Mentioning that they come one per night gives a reasoning path (count the nights before Christmas).

rewrite.q_ru: Перед Рождеством к исландским детям приходят тролли-проказники, по одному за ночь. Сколько их?
rewrite.q_en: Before Christmas, prankster trolls visit Icelandic children, one per night. How many are there?
rewrite.why_better: 'One per night' lets players reason from the run-up to Christmas, and the spoon-licker and door-slammer fact remains the payoff.

original.ru: В честь кого назван бефстроганов?
original.en: Who is beef Stroganoff named after?
options: Глагола «строгать» | The verb strogat, to whittle
Деревни Строгино | The village of Strogino
Повара Жана Строгана | Chef Jean Strogan
original.fact: The first known recipe was printed by Elena Molokhovets in 1871; the Stroganovs were among Russia's richest families.

verdict: Familiar dish; the joke decoys (the verb strogat, Strogino, chef Jean Strogan) make the table smile, though most will guess the counts. Fact is fine.

original.ru: Какую еду нашли в гробницах фараонов — и она до сих пор съедобна?
original.en: Which food found in pharaohs' tombs is still edible today?
original.fact: Honey holds little water and is acidic, so microbes cannot survive in it, even for thousands of years.

verdict: Well-known 'eternal honey' fact, but satisfying to get right, with credible food decoys and a clear science payoff.

original.ru: Откуда у гамбургера такое название?
original.en: Where does the hamburger get its name?
options: От фамилии изобретателя | Its inventor's surname
От первой закусочной «Бургер» | A diner called Burger's
* От города Гамбурга | The city of Hamburg
original.fact: German immigrants brought the minced 'Hamburg steak' to America; there is no ham in a hamburger at all.

verdict: Familiar, with a fun 'ham' trap that the fact explicitly debunks. Most will reason their way to Hamburg.

original.ru: Почему в пасту, ставшую потом «Нутеллой», положили так много фундука?
original.en: Why did the spread that became Nutella get so much hazelnut?
options: * После войны не хватало какао | Cocoa was scarce after the war
Так требовал закон Италии | Italian law required it
Фундук продлевал срок годности | Hazelnut kept it fresh longer
Ради рекламного слогана | For an advertising slogan
original.fact: In 1946 Pietro Ferrero of Piedmont, hazelnut country, stretched scarce cocoa with nuts; the Nutella name came in 1964.

verdict: Everyone loves Nutella, and the post-war cocoa shortage is a surprising and satisfying reason. The 'advertising slogan' decoy is weaker but acceptable.

original.ru: Мороженое пломбир названо в честь…
original.en: Plombir ice cream is named after…
options: Кондитера Пломбье | A confectioner called Plombier
* Французского городка | A French spa town
original.fact: It is the spa town of Plombières-les-Bains; in Russia plombir means the richest ice cream, at least 12% milk fat.

verdict: Excellent: everyone eats plombir and the dental filling (plomba) trap is irresistible; a French spa town is a real surprise.

original.ru: Слово «пельмени» пришло из коми и удмуртского языков. Что оно значит?
original.en: The word pelmeni comes from the Komi and Udmurt languages. What does it mean?
original.fact: Pelmeni do look like little ears: Russians took both the dish and its name from the peoples of the Urals.

verdict: Familiar food, surprising origin, and once you hear 'bread ear' you look at a pelmen and agree. Decoys are credible.

original.ru: Где придумали «гавайскую» пиццу с ананасами?
original.en: Where was Hawaiian pizza with pineapple invented?
original.fact: In 1962 Greek-born Sam Panopoulos made it in Ontario and named it after the brand of canned pineapple.

verdict: Calibration anchor: everyone knows the pizza, the Hawaii trap is perfect, and the Canada reveal starts arguments.

original.ru: Кто открыл первый ресторан «Макдоналдс»?
original.en: Who opened the first McDonald's restaurant?
options: Клоун Рональд Макдональд | Ronald McDonald the clown
original.fact: Ray Kroc sold the brothers milkshake mixers, and in 1961 he bought the whole company from them.

verdict: Ray Kroc is a great trap (The Founder film), but Walt Disney and Ronald the clown are throwaways. Swapping them for another fast-food founder makes it a real two-way think.

rewrite.q_ru: Кто открыл первый ресторан «Макдоналдс»?
rewrite.q_en: Who opened the first McDonald's restaurant?
rewrite.why_better: Colonel Sanders replaces the clown, so two credible fast-food founders compete with the brothers and the Kroc trap still works.

original.ru: «Как управлять страной, где столько сортов сыра?» — жаловался де Голль. Сколько сортов он назвал?
original.en: 'How can you govern a country with so many kinds of cheese?' de Gaulle asked. How many did he name?
original.fact: The 1962 quip stuck, although France actually has far more cheeses than that.

verdict: Famous quote and a fun estimate, but the exact number in de Gaulle's line is reported differently across sources. The wide tolerance (±60) already absorbs the variants, so it plays fine once the figure is confirmed.
fact_check_note: The cheese count in de Gaulle's quote circulates as 246, 258 and 265 depending on the source; confirm which figure the cited source supports (tolerance 60 covers all three).
lead_check: Not web-checked: 246, 258 and 265 all circulate; the tolerance of 60 covers all three, so play is unaffected.

original.ru: В 2018 году учёные описали древнейший известный хлеб — обугленные крошки из Иордании. Сколько ему лет?
original.en: In 2018 scientists reported the oldest known bread, charred crumbs from Jordan. How old is it?
original.fact: Hunter-gatherers baked it from wild cereals, about 4,000 years before farming began.

verdict: Great fact (bread older than farming), but the Russian question is over 100 characters and mentions a 2018 report nobody needs. A shorter question keeps the estimate and the payoff.

rewrite.q_ru: Древнейшему найденному хлебу — обугленным крошкам из Иордании — сколько лет?
rewrite.q_en: The oldest bread ever found, charred crumbs from Jordan: how old is it?
rewrite.why_better: Shorter and easier to read on the TV, with the same surprising 'older than farming' reveal.

original.ru: Из чего делают традиционный квас?
original.en: What is traditional kvass made from?
original.fact: Stale rye bread or malt ferments with yeast into a drink so mild that Russians pour it into cold soup.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition for Russians; rice, milk and potatoes are throwaways and the okroshka fact is common knowledge. Acceptable only as a warm-up.

original.ru: Чем ароматизирован чай «Эрл Грей»?
original.en: What gives Earl Grey tea its flavour?
original.fact: Bergamot is a sour citrus whose peel oil flavours the tea, thought to be named after Earl Grey, British prime minister in the 1830s.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition: most tea drinkers know bergamot. The fact that bergamot is a sour citrus (many think it is a herb) is a small payoff.

original.ru: Что означает итальянское слово «латте»?
original.en: What does the Italian word 'latte' mean?
original.fact: Order just a 'latte' in Italy and you will likely get a glass of milk: the coffee drink is caffè latte.

verdict: Easy to guess, but the payoff (order a 'latte' in Italy and get a glass of milk) is a story people repeat.

original.ru: В каком кофе больше кофеина?
original.en: Which coffee has more caffeine?
options: Зависит только от обжарки | Only the roast decides
original.fact: Robusta beans hold about 2.7% caffeine, arabica about 1.5%: robusta is more bitter and goes into instant coffee.

verdict: A real kitchen debate (many believe arabica is 'stronger'), but the dry framing does not invite the argument. Framing it as a coffee dispute and using the popular dark-roast myth as a decoy makes it social.

rewrite.q_ru: Кофейный спор: в каких зёрнах больше кофеина?
rewrite.q_en: Coffee argument: which beans have more caffeine?
options: Поровну, разница во вкусе | Equal, only the taste differs
Больше в тёмной обжарке | Dark roast has more
rewrite.why_better: Calling it an argument invites the table to take sides, and the dark-roast myth is a believable trap.

original.ru: Откуда взялось слово «мокко»?
original.en: Where does the word 'mocha' come from?
options: От реки в Бразилии | A river in Brazil
От турецкого слова «пена» | The Turkish word for foam
* От порта в Йемене | A port in Yemen
От итальянского шоколатье | An Italian chocolatier
original.fact: For centuries the port of Mocha on the Red Sea was the world's main coffee market.

verdict: Pleasant etymology, but the 'Brazil river' and 'Italian chocolatier' decoys are easy to dismiss. An Ethiopian decoy (the home of coffee) makes the Yemeni port a real surprise.

rewrite.q_ru: Откуда взялось слово «мокко»?
rewrite.q_en: Where does the word 'mocha' come from?
options: * От порта в Йемене | A port in Yemen
От города в Эфиопии | A town in Ethiopia
От реки в Бразилии | A river in Brazil
От турецкого слова «пена» | The Turkish word for foam
rewrite.why_better: Ethiopia, the birthplace of coffee, is a strong trap next to Yemen, so coffee-lovers must actually think.

original.ru: Ради чего придумали растворимый кофе «Нескафе»?
original.en: What problem was Nescafé invented to solve?
options: * Пристроить излишки бразильского кофе | Brazil's unsold coffee surplus
Накормить лётчиков в полёте | Feeding pilots in flight
Кофе для альпинистов | Coffee for climbers
Нехватку чайников в Швейцарии | A kettle shortage in Switzerland
original.fact: After the 1929 crash prices collapsed and warehouses filled with Brazilian coffee, so a bank asked Nestlé for help.

verdict: Familiar brand with a surprising economic origin; the kettle-shortage decoy is a nice joke though the correct option is the longest.

original.ru: Монах Дом Периньон, «отец шампанского», на самом деле пытался…
original.en: Dom Pérignon, the 'father of champagne', actually tried to…
options: Делать вино из яблок | Make wine from apples
Подслащивать вино мёдом | Sweeten wine with honey
* Избавиться от пузырьков | Get rid of the bubbles
Сделать вино игристее | Make wine more sparkling
original.fact: Refermentation burst bottles in the cellars; the quote 'I am tasting the stars' first appeared in an 1800s advert.

verdict: Great reversal (the 'father of champagne' fought bubbles), though 'actually' hints that the answer is the opposite of expected. The 'tasting the stars' quote being an ad is a bonus payoff.

original.ru: Рубль нельзя было вывезти. Чем СССР в 1970-х платил за «Пепси»?
original.en: The rouble was useless abroad. How did the USSR pay for Pepsi in the 1970s?
original.fact: Under a 1972 deal PepsiCo got the rights to sell Stolichnaya vodka in the West, and Pepsi came to the USSR.

verdict: Strong: everyone knows Pepsi and Stolichnaya, all decoys are credible Soviet exports, and the barter story is a perfect Soviet-nostalgia reveal.

original.ru: В каком году монгольский хан прислал царю Михаилу Фёдоровичу в подарок четыре пуда чая?
original.en: In what year did a Mongol khan send Tsar Michael four poods (about 65 kg) of tea?
original.fact: The boyars found the drink odd at first; regular tea caravans from China began only after a 1679 treaty.

verdict: An exact year of a diplomatic gift that only history buffs can place; the reign of Michael Fyodorovich is the only anchor and few remember it. The 'boyars found it odd' fact is not enough.

original.ru: По мексиканскому списку цен 1545 года, сколько какао-бобов стоила хорошая индейка?
original.en: In a Mexican price list from 1545, how many cocoa beans did a good turkey hen cost?
original.fact: Cocoa beans were real money: a small rabbit cost 30 beans and a large tomato just one.

verdict: Lovely fact (cocoa beans as money), but there is no anchor to estimate a turkey's price. Giving the rabbit's price in the question turns it into a fun ratio guess.

rewrite.q_ru: В Мексике XVI века какао-бобы были деньгами: маленький кролик стоил 30 бобов. А хорошая индейка?
rewrite.q_en: In 16th-century Mexico cocoa beans were money: a small rabbit cost 30 beans. And a good turkey?
rewrite.why_better: The rabbit price gives an everyday anchor (a turkey is worth a few rabbits), so players estimate instead of guessing blindly.

original.ru: Почему в Америке кроссовки называют sneakers?
original.en: Why are sports shoes called sneakers in America?
options: * В них можно тихо подкрасться | You can sneak around in them
Их шили из змеиной кожи | They were made of snakeskin
По фамилии изобретателя | After the inventor's surname
В честь батончика Snickers | After the Snickers bar
original.fact: Rubber soles did not clack like leather ones, so you could creep up on anyone unheard.

verdict: Guessable from the English verb 'sneak', which rewards intuition; the Snickers decoy gets a smile. A pleasant easy question.

original.ru: Шпилька по-английски — stiletto. Что значит это слово по-итальянски?
original.en: A spike heel is called a stiletto. What does the Italian word mean?
original.fact: Such thin, high heels only became possible in the 1950s, when a steel rod was put inside them.

verdict: Deliberate easy question: Russian 'стилет' already means a dagger, so many will get it by sound. The steel-rod fact is a modest payoff.

original.ru: Чем в XVIII веке пудрили парики?
original.en: What was 18th century wig powder made of?
original.fact: In 1795 Britain taxed hair powder at a guinea a year, and powdered wigs soon went out of fashion.

verdict: Easy warm-up with a fun icing-sugar decoy; the 1795 powder tax that killed the fashion is the real payoff. Acceptable as an easy question.

original.ru: Почему французский король Людовик XIII в 1624 году начал носить парик?
original.en: Why did King Louis XIII of France start wearing a wig in 1624?
options: * Он рано облысел | He was going bald
Он был в трауре | He was in mourning
Чтобы казаться выше | To look taller
Чтобы греться на охоте | To keep warm when hunting
original.fact: Courtiers rushed to copy the king, and under his son Louis XIV a wig became a must for any gentleman.

verdict: Most will guess baldness and feel clever; the decoys (mourning, height, warmth) are believable for a king. The idea that a whole fashion began with a bald king is fun.

original.ru: Откуда англичане привезли слово и моду на пижамы?
original.en: Where did the British pick up the word and fashion for pyjamas?
original.fact: Pai jama means leg garment in Persian and Hindi: the British in colonial India took to these loose trousers.

verdict: Familiar garment, credible Asian decoys, and the 'leg garment' etymology is a satisfying reveal.

original.ru: Чья свадьба в 1840 году сделала модным белое свадебное платье?
original.en: Whose 1840 wedding made the white wedding dress fashionable?
original.fact: Before her, brides usually wore their best dress of any colour; white, too impractical to wear again, showed wealth.

verdict: Good subject, but the year 1840 eliminates Marie Antoinette, Josephine and Catherine, who were all dead by then. Dropping the year makes the decoys live.

rewrite.q_ru: Чья свадьба сделала модным белое свадебное платье?
rewrite.q_en: Whose wedding made the white wedding dress fashionable?
rewrite.why_better: Without the date, all four royal brides are credible, so players have to reason rather than check death dates.

original.ru: Какую причёску по закону носили мужчины в Китае при династии Цин?
original.en: What hairstyle did Chinese men have to wear by law under the Qing dynasty?
options: * Бритый лоб и длинная коса | Shaved forehead, long braid
Голову наголо | A fully shaved head
Длинные распущенные волосы | Long loose hair
original.fact: The Manchu rulers demanded it as a sign of loyalty; men cut their braids en masse only after the 1911 revolution.

verdict: Recognisable from films, but the correct option is the only detailed two-part answer and the reveal reads like a history lesson. Little surprise or group reaction.

original.ru: От названия какого народа произошло французское слово cravate — галстук?
original.en: The French word cravate, a necktie, comes from the name of which people?
original.fact: In the 17th century the French admired the neck scarves of Croatian mercenaries and started wearing them too.

verdict: Cravate sounds like 'Croat', so intuition is rewarded, and the mercenaries story is a nice payoff.

original.ru: В каком году Луи Виттон открыл в Париже своё дело?
original.en: In what year did Louis Vuitton open his business in Paris?
original.fact: He made travel trunks, and in 1858 gave them flat lids: the old rounded ones could not be stacked.

verdict: A brand's founding year is an exam fact nobody can estimate within ±15; the flat-lid trunk fact is mildly nice but cannot carry a bare date.

original.ru: Сколько лет кожаному башмаку, найденному в 2008 году в армянской пещере Арени-1?
original.en: How old is the leather shoe found in 2008 in Armenia's Areni-1 cave?
original.fact: It is the oldest known leather shoe: a size 37 moccasin stuffed with grass, lying there since about 3500 BC.

verdict: The oldest leather shoe (size 37, stuffed with grass) is a fun fact, but the cave name makes the question feel specialist. Asking about the world's oldest shoe directly keeps the estimate and drops the jargon.

rewrite.q_ru: Древнейшую кожаную туфлю в мире нашли в пещере в Армении. Сколько ей лет?
rewrite.q_en: The world's oldest leather shoe was found in a cave in Armenia. How old is it?
rewrite.why_better: 'World's oldest shoe' is instantly relatable, so players reason about prehistory instead of stumbling over a cave name.

original.ru: Что такое катамаран?
original.en: What is a catamaran?
options: * Судно с двумя корпусами | A boat with two hulls
Судно с двумя мачтами | A boat with two masts
Маленькая подводная лодка | A small submarine
Плот из бочек | A raft made of barrels
original.fact: The word comes from Tamil in southern India, where kattumaram means 'tied logs'.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition; 'barrel raft' is weak. The Tamil 'tied logs' etymology is a nice surprise payoff.

original.ru: Какого цвета «чёрный ящик» самолёта?
original.en: What colour is an aircraft's 'black box'?
original.fact: Flight recorders are painted bright orange with reflective strips so they can be found quickly in wreckage.

verdict: The 'black' option is a perfect intended trap and people love being told the black box is orange. Fact explains why.

original.ru: Какую советскую машину в народе прозвали «копейкой»?
original.en: Which Soviet car was nicknamed 'Kopeyka', the kopeck?
original.fact: The first Zhiguli was a reworked Italian Fiat 124, strengthened for Russian roads and frosts.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition with strong nostalgia for the older generation; all decoys are real Soviet cars. The Fiat 124 fact is fairly well known.

original.ru: Где стоял двигатель у «горбатого» «Запорожца» ЗАЗ-965?
original.en: Where was the engine of the 'humpbacked' Zaporozhets ZAZ-965?
options: Двигателя не было | It had no engine
original.fact: Its air-cooled engine sat at the back and the boot was under the bonnet, like the Italian Fiat 600 it resembled.

verdict: Nostalgic for the older players, but 'it had no engine' and 'under the seats' are throwaways, leaving front vs back. Credible engine positions make it a real question.

rewrite.q_ru: Где стоял двигатель у «горбатого» «Запорожца» ЗАЗ-965?
rewrite.q_en: Where was the engine of the 'humpbacked' Zaporozhets ZAZ-965?
options: Под полом салона | Under the cabin floor
Посередине, за сиденьями | In the middle, behind the seats
rewrite.why_better: All four positions exist on real cars, so younger players cannot eliminate jokes and the older ones get to show off.

original.ru: Какой конструктор построил в России самолёт «Илья Муромец», а в США — первые серийные вертолёты?
original.en: Who designed Russia's Ilya Muromets plane and later America's first mass-produced helicopters?
original.fact: The 1913 Ilya Muromets was one of the first passenger planes, with heating, electric lights and even a toilet.

verdict: Mil and Kamov are clever helicopter traps and the US link points to the emigrant Sikorsky; the plane-with-a-toilet fact is fun. The question is long; trimming it helps readability.

rewrite.q_ru: Кто построил «Илью Муромца», а потом в США — первые серийные вертолёты?
rewrite.q_en: Who built the Ilya Muromets plane and later America's first mass-produced helicopters?
rewrite.why_better: Shorter and readable in a few seconds, so more players engage with the 'emigrant designer' reasoning path.

original.ru: Что по британскому закону 1865 года должно было двигаться перед паровым автомобилем?
original.en: Under an 1865 British law, what had to go in front of a steam road vehicle?
options: * Человек с красным флагом | A man with a red flag
Всадник с горном | A rider with a horn
Собака с колокольчиком | A dog with a bell
Полицейский с барабаном | A policeman with a drum
original.fact: He walked 60 yards ahead to warn horse riders, and the limit was 4 mph, or 2 mph in towns.

verdict: Absurd-sounding but true; all decoys are equally silly, so it plays as a fun guessing game, and the 4 mph limit is a great payoff.

original.ru: Какая компания придумала трёхточечный ремень безопасности и отдала патент всем бесплатно?
original.en: Which carmaker invented the three-point seat belt and let everyone use the patent free?
original.fact: Engineer Nils Bohlin designed it in 1959, and Volvo let rivals use it free, so it became the standard worldwide.

verdict: Volvo's safety reputation gives a reasoning path, and giving the patent away for free is a satisfying story.

original.ru: Первый в мире светофор поставили в Лондоне в 1868 году. Чем он светил ночью?
original.en: The first traffic light went up in London in 1868. What lit it at night?
original.fact: Gas was its downfall: in 1869 a leak made a lamp explode, badly injuring the policeman who worked it.

verdict: Good reasoning path (1868 means no electric bulbs yet) and the exploding traffic light is a memorable payoff.

original.ru: Сколько колёс было у шасси самого тяжёлого самолёта в истории, Ан-225 «Мрия»?
original.en: How many wheels did the An-225 Mriya, the heaviest aircraft ever built, have?
original.fact: 32 wheels spread a take-off weight of up to 640 tonnes so it would not crush the runway.

verdict: Mriya is well known to this family, but the fact only restates why so many wheels. Putting the 640 tonnes in the question gives an estimation path.

rewrite.q_ru: Ан-225 «Мрия» весил на взлёте до 640 тонн. Сколько колёс держало его на земле?
rewrite.q_en: The An-225 Mriya weighed up to 640 tonnes at take-off. How many wheels held it up?
rewrite.why_better: The weight lets players estimate tonnes per wheel instead of guessing a bare count.

original.ru: Сколько тонн груза может поднять Ми-26, самый большой серийный вертолёт в мире?
original.en: How many tonnes can the Mi-26, the largest helicopter ever mass-produced, carry?
original.fact: Enough to carry another helicopter: in 2002 a Mi-26 lifted two US Chinooks off a mountain in Afghanistan.

verdict: A fair estimate with an everyday sense of scale, and the payoff (it airlifted American Chinooks) is a great story.

original.ru: Какое животное носит имя путешественника Пржевальского?
original.en: Which animal is named after the explorer Przhevalsky?
original.fact: It was last seen in the wild in 1969; in the 1990s zoo bred horses were returned to the steppes of Mongolia.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition for Russian players; the extinct-in-the-wild-and-returned story is a good payoff.

original.ru: Как прозвали медсестру Флоренс Найтингейл?
original.en: What was nurse Florence Nightingale's nickname?
options: * Леди с лампой | The Lady with the Lamp
Орлеанская дева | The Maid of Orleans
original.fact: A Times reporter wrote that at night, after the doctors had gone, she made her rounds alone with a lamp in hand.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition; the other nicknames belong to queens or Joan of Arc, so it is easy to eliminate. The night-rounds fact is gentle.

original.ru: Кто стал первыми пассажирами воздушного шара братьев Монгольфье в 1783 году?
original.en: Who were the first passengers of the Montgolfier brothers' balloon in 1783?
options: Король и королева | The king and queen
* Баран, утка и петух | A sheep, a duck and a rooster
Собака и кошка | A dog and a cat
original.fact: People feared height might harm living things; watched by the king and queen, the animals flew 3 km and landed safely.

verdict: Delightful answer that gets a laugh; the correct option is the only three-part one, but the reveal is worth it.

original.ru: Кого Никола Тесла под старость любил больше всего на свете?
original.en: Whom did Nikola Tesla love most in his old age?
original.fact: He said he loved her as a man loves a woman, and spent over $2,000 nursing her broken wing and leg.

verdict: Very surprising and funny, but 'white pigeon' is far longer than the one-word decoys. A one-word option fixes the telegraph cheaply.

rewrite.q_ru: Кого Никола Тесла под старость любил больше всего на свете?
rewrite.q_en: Whom did Nikola Tesla love most in his old age?
rewrite.why_better: Four single-word pets of equal length, so the pigeon is a pure surprise.

original.ru: Как Софья Ковалевская смогла уехать учиться за границу?
original.en: How did Sofia Kovalevskaya manage to go abroad to study?
options: Её отправила императрица | The Empress sent her
* Вступила в фиктивный брак | A sham marriage
Переоделась юношей | Disguised as a young man
Сбежала на корабле | Ran away on a ship
original.fact: Russian universities did not admit women, and a woman could travel abroad only with a father's or husband's leave.

verdict: Disguising as a young man is a great trap and the sham marriage is a surprising, story-like reveal.

original.ru: Где погиб капитан Джеймс Кук?
original.en: Where did Captain James Cook die?
original.fact: His crew were the first recorded Europeans to see Hawaii, in 1778, and a year later he died there in a clash on the shore.

verdict: Cook is famous, but the question misses the hook every Russian knows: Vysotsky's song about natives eating Cook. Quoting it makes the table laugh before they answer.

rewrite.q_ru: «Почему аборигены съели Кука?» — пел Высоцкий. А где капитан погиб на самом деле?
rewrite.q_en: 'Why did the natives eat Cook?' sang Vysotsky. Where did the captain really die?
rewrite.why_better: The Vysotsky line gives an instant laugh and a shared cultural hook for both generations.

original.ru: Какую должность предложили Эйнштейну в 1952 году (он отказался)?
original.en: What post was Einstein offered in 1952, and turned down?
original.fact: He replied that he lacked both the natural aptitude and the experience to deal properly with people.

verdict: Surprising and reasonable via Einstein being Jewish, but 'Head of NASA' is an anachronism (NASA dates from 1958), which sharp players notice. Swap it for a credible post.

rewrite.q_ru: Какую должность предложили Эйнштейну в 1952 году (он отказался)?
rewrite.q_en: What post was Einstein offered in 1952, and turned down?
rewrite.why_better: Removes the NASA anachronism so no decoy can be ruled out by dates.

original.ru: Почему на вечеринку Стивена Хокинга в 2009 году никто не пришёл?
original.en: Why did nobody come to Stephen Hawking's party in 2009?
options: Она была на Южном полюсе | It was at the South Pole
Приглашения были в формулах | The invitations were equations
Он забыл назвать дату | He forgot to give a date
* О ней объявили уже после | He announced it only afterwards
original.fact: It was a party for time travellers: only someone who learned of it in the future could have come.

verdict: Hawking's time-traveller party is a perfect 'wait, seriously?' with a logical path for those who think about time travel; big group reaction.

original.ru: До какого возраста дожила француженка Жанна Кальман, видевшая в детстве Ван Гога?
original.en: To what age did Jeanne Calment, who met Van Gogh as a girl, live?
original.fact: As a girl she met him in her uncle's shop: ugly, ungracious and very disagreeable. She lived 122 years and 164 days.

verdict: 'Oldest person ever' gives a good anchor near 120, the tolerance is fair, and Calment calling Van Gogh ugly and disagreeable is a great payoff.

original.ru: Сколько дней плот «Кон-Тики» Тура Хейердала плыл через Тихий океан?
original.en: How many days did Thor Heyerdahl's raft Kon-Tiki take to cross the Pacific?
original.fact: A raft of nine balsa logs with not a single nail drifted almost 7,000 km from Peru to Polynesia.

verdict: Kon-Tiki is familiar and the range is fair, but there is little to reason from. Putting the 7,000 km distance in the question gives a speed-based estimate.

rewrite.q_ru: Плот «Кон-Тики» прошёл почти 7000 км от Перу до Полинезии. Сколько дней длилось плавание?
rewrite.q_en: The Kon-Tiki raft drifted almost 7,000 km from Peru to Polynesia. How many days did it take?
rewrite.why_better: With the distance given, players can estimate a raft's daily drift, so the guess rewards reasoning.

original.ru: С каким счётом Германия разгромила Бразилию в полуфинале ЧМ-2014?
original.en: By what score did Germany crush Brazil in the 2014 World Cup semi-final?
original.fact: Germany were 5–0 up after 29 minutes, in Brazil, in front of Brazil's own fans.

verdict: Iconic score that even non-fans remember; the '5-0 after 29 minutes, at home' fact makes it sting again.

original.ru: Что сделал Зинедин Зидан в финале чемпионата мира 2006 года?
original.en: What did Zinedine Zidane do in the 2006 World Cup final?
options: Отказался выходить на поле | Refused to take the field
* Ударил соперника головой | Headbutted an opponent
Забил гол пяткой | Scored with his heel
Встал в ворота | Went in goal

rewrite.q_en: At Euro 2008 Russia knocked out the Netherlands, with a Dutch coach. Who?

rewrite.q_en: A 1958 record: how many goals did France's Just Fontaine score at a single World Cup?
