original.en: In which year is Umberto Eco's The Name of the Rose set?
original.fact: Eco, a scholar of the Middle Ages, said he began the novel because he "felt like poisoning a monk".

verdict: 'Middle Ages' gives an anchor, but the year itself is dull; the 'felt like poisoning a monk' line is the real gem. Framing the novel as a monastery murder mystery gives context and a tighter tolerance makes the estimate count.

rewrite.q_ru: «Имя розы» Эко — детектив в средневековом монастыре. В каком году идёт действие?
rewrite.q_en: Eco's The Name of the Rose is a murder mystery in a medieval abbey. In what year is it set?
rewrite.why_better: The murder-mystery framing gives context for everyone who has not read it, and the 'poison a monk' quote stays as the payoff.

original.ru: Сколько примерно книг написал или составил Айзек Азимов?
original.en: About how many books did Isaac Asimov write or edit?
original.fact: His books appear in nine of the ten main classes of the Dewey Decimal library system, from chemistry to Shakespeare.

verdict: Calibration anchor: a surprising number, but the name is only half familiar to young players and there is little to reason from. Naming his best-known book helps familiarity and 'incredibly prolific' gives a scale hint.

rewrite.q_ru: Фантаст Айзек Азимов («Я, робот») был невероятно плодовит. Сколько книг он написал или составил?
rewrite.q_en: Sci-fi writer Isaac Asimov (I, Robot) was incredibly prolific. About how many books did he write or edit?
rewrite.why_better: 'I, Robot' makes the name click for younger players, and 'incredibly prolific' pushes guesses into the hundreds.

original.ru: Как зовут мальчика, лучшего друга Винни-Пуха?
original.en: What is the name of Winnie the Pooh's best friend, the boy?
original.fact: He was A. A. Milne's real son, and Pooh was based on the boy's own teddy bear.

verdict: Deliberate easy recognition; the real son and teddy bear fact is fairly well known but pleasant.

original.ru: На чём Емеля приехал к царю «по щучьему веленью»?
original.en: What did Emelya ride to the tsar's palace, by the pike's command?
options: На ковре-самолёте | On a flying carpet
На сером волке | On a grey wolf
original.fact: In Afanasyev's version the tsar later seals Emelya and the princess in a barrel and throws it into the sea.

verdict: Easy recognition with fun fairy-tale decoys; the dark barrel-in-the-sea ending from Afanasyev surprises people who only know the cartoon.

original.ru: Из-за чего Иван-царевич потерял Царевну-лягушку?
original.en: Why did Ivan Tsarevich lose the Frog Princess?
options: * Сжёг её лягушачью кожу | He burned her frog skin
Выдал её тайну отцу | He told his father her secret
Не поцеловал её | He never kissed her
Посмеялся над ней | He laughed at her
original.fact: Her father had cursed her for three years; had Ivan waited a little longer, she would have been his forever.

verdict: Familiar tale with a good Western trap (the kiss), and 'had he waited a little longer' is a satisfying payoff.

original.ru: Добрались ли бременские музыканты до Бремена в сказке братьев Гримм?
original.en: In the Grimms' tale, did the Town Musicians of Bremen ever reach Bremen?
options: * Нет, остались в доме разбойников | No, they stayed in the robbers' house
Да, и стали городским оркестром | Yes, and became the town band
Да, но их прогнали | Yes, but they were chased out
Нет, вернулись к хозяевам | No, they went back to their owners
original.fact: Bremen loves them anyway: in 1953 it put up a statue of them by the town hall.

verdict: Genuine surprise: most assume they reach Bremen (or know only the Soviet cartoon), and the city loving them anyway is a sweet payoff.

original.ru: Как зовут итальянского «брата» Буратино?
original.en: Who is Buratino's Italian original?
original.fact: Alexei Tolstoy set out to translate Pinocchio but wrote his own tale; burattino is Italian for puppet.

verdict: Too easy as asked: Geppetto is Pinocchio's father and Karabas is Buratino's villain, so only Cipollino competes. All-Italian '-ino' style names make players think, and the burattino = puppet fact pays off.

rewrite.q_ru: Как зовут итальянского «брата» Буратино?
rewrite.q_en: Who is Buratino's Italian original?
rewrite.why_better: Four Italian puppet-or-tale names mean players must actually recall the original rather than eliminate side characters.

original.ru: Чем Коллоди закончил «Пиноккио», когда печатал его в журнале в 1881 году?
original.en: How did Collodi first end Pinocchio in the 1881 magazine serial?
options: * Его повесили на дубе | He was hanged from an oak
Он стал мальчиком | He became a real boy
Он сгорел в очаге | He burned in the fireplace
Его проглотила акула | A shark swallowed him
original.fact: Four months later readers and the editor got Collodi to carry on, and the Fairy saved Pinocchio.

verdict: Shocking reveal (the author hanged Pinocchio) that gets a strong reaction, plus readers rescuing him is a great story.

original.ru: У какого писателя Пушкин позаимствовал сюжет «Сказки о золотом петушке»?
original.en: Whose story did Pushkin borrow for The Tale of the Golden Cockerel?
options: Ганса Христиана Андерсена | Hans Christian Andersen
original.fact: Anna Akhmatova traced it to the American Irving's Legend of the Arabian Astrologer.

verdict: Very surprising source, but Andersen is an anachronism for 1834 and Irving is pure memorisation. A Walter Scott decoy (Pushkin's favourite) makes the British/European options more tempting.

rewrite.q_ru: У какого писателя Пушкин позаимствовал сюжет «Сказки о золотом петушке»?
rewrite.q_en: Whose story did Pushkin borrow for The Tale of the Golden Cockerel?
rewrite.why_better: Walter Scott, whom Pushkin admired, is a believable trap, so the American Irving lands as a bigger surprise.

original.ru: Английские шляпники XIX века и правда часто сходили с ума. Что их травило?
original.en: Hatters in Carroll's England really did go mad. What poisoned them?
original.fact: Mercury was used to turn fur into felt, and its fumes caused tremors and odd behaviour.

verdict: Satisfying 'mad as a hatter' explanation with a reasoning path (toxic chemicals), but 'Mercury' is much shorter than the decoys. 'Mercury fumes' balances the lengths.

rewrite.q_ru: Английские шляпники XIX века и правда часто сходили с ума. Что их травило?
rewrite.q_en: Hatters in Carroll's England really did go mad. What poisoned them?
rewrite.why_better: Equal-length two-word options so the short answer does not stand out.

original.ru: Сколько тюфяков положили поверх горошины в «Принцессе на горошине»?
original.en: In The Princess and the Pea, how many mattresses were piled on the pea?
original.fact: The pea went into the royal museum, 'where it may still be seen, if no one has stolen it'.

verdict: Everyone knows the tale but not the number, so the guesses vary widely and spark laughter; the pea in the museum 'if no one stole it' is a charming payoff.

original.ru: В каком году вышла первая книга Алана Милна о Винни-Пухе?
original.en: In which year did A. A. Milne's first Winnie-the-Pooh book come out?
original.fact: Christopher Robin's real toys, Pooh, Eeyore, Piglet, Kanga and Tigger, are kept at the New York Public Library.

verdict: Bare publication date; the toys-in-New-York fact is the real payoff. Linking the question to the real teddy bear gives a little warmth and context.

rewrite.q_ru: Плюшевый мишка Кристофера Робина стал Винни-Пухом. В каком году вышла первая книга о нём?
rewrite.q_en: Christopher Robin's teddy bear became Winnie-the-Pooh. In what year did the first book come out?
rewrite.why_better: The real-teddy framing makes the date feel connected to a story, setting up the real-toys-in-New-York fact.
